actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Transferability of CLIP Features for Zero-Shot HOI Detection
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of zero-shot HOI detectors that use CLIP features with different pre-trained models (e.g., ViT-B, ViT-L), to analyze the impact of model capacity and training data on transferability to unseen interactions.
CONTROLS: Baseline: CLIP (ViT-B), ablation: use frozen CLIP features vs. fine-tuned CLIP features.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (evaluation on a diverse set of real-world HOI detection benchmarks).
PREDICTION: We expect that larger CLIP models will generally perform better, but that performance may plateau for few-shot or many unrelated classes. This could fail if the improved performance is not solely due to the increased capacity, and other components (e.g., orthogonality of attention heads) start to dominate.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Transferability of CLIP Features for Zero-Shot HOI Detection
REVISED PROPOSAL: To further understand the challenges in generalizing zero-shot HOI detection to unseen interactions, add a new experiment where the zero-shot detector uses CLIP features pre-trained on object-only text descriptions (e.g., "A cup") instead of interaction text descriptions (e.g., "A person is holding a cup").
CONTROLS: Ablations: original interaction text description vs. object-only text description, object detector (e.g., Faster R-CNN, DETR).
COST: 50 GPU-hours (evaluation on a diverse set of real-world HOI detection benchmarks).
PREDICTION: We expect that using object-only text descriptions will lead to improved generalizability to unseen interactions at the cost of reduced performance on seen interactions, indicating that interaction-specific knowledge is crucial for HOI detection. However, this might fail if the improved performance is due to changes in the representation capacity or bias of the detector rather than the text description usage.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Multimodal Alignment Mechanisms on Zero-Shot HOI Detection
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effects of different multimodal alignment mechanisms (e.g., multimodal attention, modal-specific layers, projection techniques) on the performance and generalizability of zero-shot HOI detection models that use CLIP features, and compare them with a baseline that uses only static text embeddings.
CONTROLS: Baseline: CLIP features with static text embeddings, ablations: different multimodal alignment mechanisms, evaluation metrics: accuracy, mAP, F1 score.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (evaluation on a diverse set of real-world HOI detection benchmarks).
PREDICTION: We expect that models exploiting multimodal alignment will enjoy both improved performance and better generalizability to unseen interactions, compared to those using static text embeddings alone. However, the extent of the improvement may depend on the specific mechanism used, and we may find that different mechanisms perform better for certain types of interactions or datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Zero-Shot HOI Detection with Learned Compositional Representations
PROPOSAL: Develop a zero-shot HOI detection model that learns to compose object and action representations using a multimodal encoder-decoder architecture, and evaluate its performance on a range of HOI detection benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: CLIP features with static text embeddings, ablation: object-only vs. action-only decoder, evaluation metrics: accuracy, mAP, F1 score.
COST: 300 GPU-hours (training and evaluation on a diverse set of real-world HOI detection benchmarks).
PREDICTION: We expect that the learned compositional representations will significantly improve generalizability to unseen interactions, especially when the object and action decoders are both utilized. However, this could fail if the model struggles to capture the fine-grained details of each interaction or if the decoder training process is unstable.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Zero-Shot HOI Detection with Learned Compositional Representations
REVISED PROPOSAL: Introduce a new experiment to test the robustness of the compositional representation model to imperfect object detection. This can be done by incorporating box-wise uncertainty estimates from the object detector into the model's loss function or by adversarially perturbing the object boxes.
CONTROLS: Ablations: original model vs. model with uncertainty-aware loss function/adversarial perturbations, evaluation metrics: accuracy, mAP, F1 score under varying levels of object detector noise.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (training and evaluation on a diverse set of real-world HOI detection benchmarks).
PREDICTION: We expect that the compositional representation model will still maintain its performance advantage even when faced with imperfect object detection, indicating its robustness to practical real-world challenges. However, this might fail if the model's improvements are due to overfitting or if the perturbations are too strong and violate the model's assumptions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Transferability of Object Detectors in Zero-Shot HOI Detection
PROPOSAL: Investigate the degree to which different object detectors (e.g., Faster R-CNN, DETR, Mask R-CNN) affect the performance and generalizability of zero-shot HOI detection models, and compare the transferability of these object detectors across different HOI benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: CLIP features with one object detector, ablations: different object detectors, evaluation metrics: accuracy, mAP, F1 score.
COST: 250 GPU-hours (training and evaluation on a diverse set of real-world HOI detection benchmarks).
PREDICTION: We expect that different object detectors will have varying degrees of impact on the performance and generalizability of zero-shot HOI detection models, and that some object detectors may be more transferable across HOI benchmarks than others. However, this could fail if the transferability of object detectors is highly dependent on the specific HOI benchmark or dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Robust Zero-Shot HOI Detection
PROPOSAL: Introduce adversarial training to the zero-shot HOI detection models to improve their robustness to real-world perturbations (e.g., occlusion, noise, variations in object pose), and evaluate their performance on a range of HOI detection benchmarks with varying levels of adversarial noise.
CONTROLS: Baseline: original zero-shot HOI detection model, ablation: original model vs. model with adversarial training, evaluation metrics: accuracy, mAP, F1 score under varying levels of adversarial noise.
COST: 350 GPU-hours (training and evaluation on a diverse set of real-world HOI detection benchmarks).
PREDICTION: We expect that adversarial training will significantly improve the robustness of the zero-shot HOI detection models to real-world perturbations, leading to better performance on challenging benchmarks. However, this could fail if the adversarial training process leads to overfitting or if the model's improvements are due to changes in the optimization process rather than the inclusion of an adversarial loss term.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Supervised Pretraining and Fine-Tuning for Zero-Shot HOI Detection
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of supervised pretraining and fine-tuning on the performance of zero-shot HOI detection models, and compare their performance to that of models trained from scratch on a range of HOI detection benchmarks.

PROPOSAL 1: Investigating Transferability of CLIP Features for Zero-Shot HOI Detection
Compare the performance of zero-shot HOI detectors that use CLIP features with different pre-trained models (e.g., ViT-B, ViT-L), to analyze the impact of model capacity and training data on transferability to unseen interactions.
Controls: Baseline: CLIP (ViT-B), ablation: use frozen CLIP features vs. fine-tuned CLIP features.

Investigate the effects of different multimodal alignment mechanisms (e.g., multimodal attention, modal-specific layers, projection techniques) on the performance and generalizability of zero-shot HOI detection models that use CLIP features, and compare them with a baseline that uses only static text embeddings.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Limitations of CLIP-based HOI Detectors
PROPOSAL: We will compare the performance of state-of-the-art CLIP-based HOI detectors on a series of held-out validation sets, with varying degrees of visual similarity between interactions, to understand how CLIP's limitations impact generalizability.
CONTROLS: Standard CLIP-based baseline, as well as two variations where the CLIP model is fine-tuned on detector features and on relational object features.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the fine-tuned CLIP models will significantly outperform the standard baseline on visually similar interactions, but still perform poorly on cases where visual similarity is low. We also expect that the two fine-tuned models will have similar performance, as the gain from relational object features will be offset by the overfitting to specific detector architectures. A key challenge is distinguishing visually similar interactions, which may require more sophisticated methods than the simple fine-tuning used here.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Object-centric HOI Detection with Graph Attention
PROPOSAL: We will adapt the state-of-the-art object-centric HOI detection approach, which represents objects as nodes in a graph and their interactions as edges, to incorporate graph attention mechanisms for learning attention weights on object features and bypassing the need for target-specific detector features.
CONTROLS: Current state-of-the-art object-centric HOI detector (without graph attention), a manual ablation study removing the graph attention component, and a baseline that uses CLIP features directly for interaction recognition.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that adding graph attention to the object-centric HOI detector will improve performance by allowing the model to dynamically weight object features based on their relevance to the interaction, and that the manual ablation study will reveal which object features and attention weights are most important for interaction recognition. The CLIP baseline will likely perform poorly, as it lacks the object-centric understanding of interaction patterns that the graph-based approach provides.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Limitations of CLIP-based HOI Detectors
PROPOSAL: We will expand the comparison in our previous proposal to include a more comprehensive set of validation sets, including those with varying object scales, poses, and visibility, as well as interactions where objects are partially occluded or have ambiguous class labels.
CONTROLS: Standard CLIP-based baseline, fine-tuned CLIP models with detector features and relational object features, and an additional condition where the validation sets are generated using a data augmentation algorithm to simulate real-world variability.
COST: 40 GPU-hours (increase due to additional validation sets)
PREDICTION: We expect that the findings from our previous proposal will be reinforced, and that the limitations of CLIP-based HOI detectors will be more starkly revealed by the expanded set of validation sets. In particular, we anticipate that the CLIP models will struggle with objects and interactions that exhibit larger variability in appearance, pose, or scale, and that the additional condition will help simulate the conditions under which real-world HOI interactions are typically encountered.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: HOI Attention with Prototypical Networks
PROPOSAL: We will introduce a new HOI attention mechanism that leverages prototypical networks to identify and selectively focus on the most representative human-object interaction patterns in the dataset, while ignoring less informative patterns.
CONTROLS: Standard object-centric HOI detector, the graph attention-based HOI detector, and an ablation study where we compare the performance of the proposed HOI attention mechanism with and without the use of prototypical networks.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed HOI attention mechanism will significantly improve the performance of the object-centric HOI detector by allowing it to selectively focus on the most representative interaction patterns, and that the use of prototypical networks will enable the model to adapt to the specific distribution of interactions in the dataset. Additionally, we anticipate that the ablation study will provide insights into the importance of using prototypical networks for HOI attention.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Detector-agnostic HOI Recognition with Masked Language Models
PROPOSAL: We will adapt the masked language model (MLM) approach, which has been successful in Zero-Shot Learning, to the HOI recognition task by masking out the object and/or verb in the interaction description, and then using the MLM to predict the missing information.
CONTROLS: Standard HOI recognition baseline (e.g., CLIP-based detector), an ablation study removing the masking component, and an evaluation on a set of novel interactions generated by combining seen objects and verbs.
COST: 15 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the MLM-based approach will enable detector-agnostic HOI recognition by leveraging the semantic knowledge encoded in the language model, and that the masking component will allow the model to effectively predict novel interactions. However, we anticipate that the performance may degrade if the masked information is very similar to the seen interactions, as the MLM may overfit to those specific patterns.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Object-centric HOI Detection with Graph Attention
PROPOSAL: We will revise the object-centric HOI detection approach to incorporate a self-supervised learning component that learns to recover the object features and interactions from a corrupted input, thereby implicitly learning a more robust representation of the human-object interactions.
CONTROLS: Standard object-centric HOI detector with graph attention, the revised detector, and an ablation study removing the self-supervised learning component.
COST: 25 GPU-hours (increase due to the additional self-supervised learning component)
PREDICTION: We expect that the revised detector will exhibit improved robustness to ambiguous or noisy input, and that the self-supervised learning component will enable the model to learn more robust object features and interactions. However, we anticipate that the improvement may come at the cost of increased computational resources and potentially degraded performance on seen interactions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for HOI Detection
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of cross-modal knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge from a large pre-trained language model to a smaller HOI detection model, and to improve the HOI detection performance on novel interactions.
CONTROLS: Standard HOI detection model, a larger pre-trained language model (e.g., CLIP), and an evaluation on a set of novel interactions generated by combining seen objects and verbs.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that cross-modal knowledge distillation will enable the smaller HOI detection model to leverage the semantic knowledge encoded in the larger language model, and that the transfer learning component will improve the model's ability to recognize novel interactions. However, we anticipate that the performance may degrade if the pre-trained language model is not well-suited for the HOI detection task, or if the knowledge distillation process is not properly aligned with the HOI detection task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Multi-task Learning for HOI Detection and Recognition
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of online multi-task learning to jointly learn HOI detection and recognition tasks, and to improve the model's ability to recognize novel interactions without sacrificing detection performance.
CONTROLS: Standard HOI detection and recognition models, an online multi-task learning framework, and an evaluation on a set of novel interactions generated by combining seen objects and verbs.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that online multi-task learning will enable the model to leverage the joint learning of HOI detection and recognition tasks to improve performance on both tasks, and that the incremental learning component will allow the model to adapt to novel interactions without requiring large amounts of additional training data. However, we anticipate that the performance may degrade if the online learning process is not properly aligned with the HOI detection and recognition tasks, or if the model is not able to effectively adapt to novel interactions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for HOI Detection with Transformed Interaction Descriptions
PROPOSAL: We will propose a new adversarial training method that transforms interaction descriptions to create adversarial examples, and use these examples to train the HOI detection model to be more robust to variations in interaction descriptions.
CONTROLS: Standard HOI detection model, an adversarial attack algorithm, and an evaluation on a set of transformed interaction descriptions.
COST: 35 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the adversarial training method will improve the model's robustness to variations in interaction descriptions, and that the transformed interaction descriptions will effectively simulate the kinds of variations that may occur in real-world scenarios. However, we anticipate that the performance may degrade if the adversarial attack algorithm is not properly aligned with the HOI detection task, or if the transformed interaction descriptions are too similar to the original descriptions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Holistic Evaluation and Benchmarking for HOI Detection
PROPOSAL: We will create a comprehensive evaluation framework and benchmark to assess the performance of HOI detection models on various aspects, including interaction detection, object detection, and relationship recognition, and to compare the performance of the proposed methods with state-of-the-art models.
CONTROLS: Standard HOI detection models, a comprehensive evaluation framework, and a benchmarking dataset.
COST: 40 GPU-hours (limited to evaluation and benchmarking)
PREDICTION: We expect that the holistic evaluation framework and benchmark will provide a comprehensive assessment of HOI detection models and opportunities for improvement, and that the benchmarking dataset will serve as a valuable resource for the research community.

propositions.cout_texte: 40 GPU-hours (increase due to additional validation sets)
propositions.prediction: We expect that the findings from our previous proposal will be reinforced, and that the limitations of CLIP-based HOI detectors will be more starkly revealed by the expanded set of validation sets. In particular, we anticipate that the CLIP models will struggle with objects and interactions that exhibit larger variability in appearance, pose, or scale, and that the additional condition will help simulate the conditions under which real-world HOI interactions are typically encountered.
propositions.texte: We will expand the comparison in our previous proposal to include a more comprehensive set of validation sets, including those with varying object scales, poses, and visibility, as well as interactions where objects are partially occluded or have ambiguous class labels.
propositions.titre: Investigating the Limitations of CLIP-based HOI Detectors

propositions.controles: Standard object-centric HOI detector with graph attention, the revised detector, and an ablation study removing the self-supervised learning component.
propositions.cout_texte: 25 GPU-hours (increase due to the additional self-supervised learning component)
propositions.prediction: We expect that the revised detector will exhibit improved robustness to ambiguous or noisy input, and that the self-supervised learning component will enable the model to learn more robust object features and interactions. However, we anticipate that the improvement may come at the cost of increased computational resources and potentially degraded performance on seen interactions.
propositions.texte: We will revise the object-centric HOI detection approach to incorporate a self-supervised learning component that learns to recover the object features and interactions from a corrupted input, thereby implicitly learning a more robust representation of the human-object interactions.
propositions.titre: Object-centric HOI Detection with Graph Attention

propositions.controles: Standard object-centric HOI detector, the graph attention-based HOI detector, and an ablation study where we compare the performance of the proposed HOI attention mechanism with and without the use of prototypical networks.
propositions.prediction: We expect that the proposed HOI attention mechanism will significantly improve the performance of the object-centric HOI detector by allowing it to selectively focus on the most representative interaction patterns, and that the use of prototypical networks will enable the model to adapt to the specific distribution of interactions in the dataset. Additionally, we anticipate that the ablation study will provide insights into the importance of using prototypical networks for HOI attention.
propositions.texte: We will introduce a new HOI attention mechanism that leverages prototypical networks to identify and selectively focus on the most representative human-object interaction patterns in the dataset, while ignoring less informative patterns.
propositions.titre: HOI Attention with Prototypical Networks

propositions.controles: Standard HOI recognition baseline (e.g., CLIP-based detector), an ablation study removing the masking component, and an evaluation on a set of novel interactions generated by combining seen objects and verbs.
propositions.prediction: We expect that the MLM-based approach will enable detector-agnostic HOI recognition by leveraging the semantic knowledge encoded in the language model, and that the masking component will allow the model to effectively predict novel interactions. However, we anticipate that the performance may degrade if the masked information is very similar to the seen interactions, as the MLM may overfit to those specific patterns.
propositions.texte: We will adapt the masked language model (MLM) approach, which has been successful in Zero-Shot Learning, to the HOI recognition task by masking out the object and/or verb in the interaction description, and then using the MLM to predict the missing information.
propositions.titre: Detector-agnostic HOI Recognition with Masked Language Models

propositions.controles: Standard HOI detection model, a larger pre-trained language model (e.g., CLIP), and an evaluation on a set of novel interactions generated by combining seen objects and verbs.
propositions.prediction: We expect that cross-modal knowledge distillation will enable the smaller HOI detection model to leverage the semantic knowledge encoded in the larger language model, and that the transfer learning component will improve the model's ability to recognize novel interactions. However, we anticipate that the performance may degrade if the pre-trained language model is not well-suited for the HOI detection task, or if the knowledge distillation process is not properly aligned with the HOI detection task.
propositions.texte: We will investigate the use of cross-modal knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge from a large pre-trained language model to a smaller HOI detection model, and to improve the HOI detection performance on novel interactions.
propositions.titre: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for HOI Detection

propositions.controles: Standard HOI detection and recognition models, an online multi-task learning framework, and an evaluation on a set of novel interactions generated by combining seen objects and verbs.
propositions.prediction: We expect that online multi-task learning will enable the model to leverage the joint learning of HOI detection and recognition tasks to improve performance on both tasks, and that the incremental learning component will allow the model to adapt to novel interactions without requiring large amounts of additional training data. However, we anticipate that the performance may degrade if the online learning process is not properly aligned with the HOI detection and recognition tasks, or if the model is not able to effectively adapt to novel interactions.
propositions.texte: We will investigate the use of online multi-task learning to jointly learn HOI detection and recognition tasks, and to improve the model's ability to recognize novel interactions without sacrificing detection performance.
propositions.titre: Online Multi-task Learning for HOI Detection and Recognition

propositions.controles: Standard HOI detection model, an adversarial attack algorithm, and an evaluation on a set of transformed interaction descriptions.
propositions.prediction: We expect that the adversarial training method will improve the model's robustness to variations in interaction descriptions, and that the transformed interaction descriptions will effectively simulate the kinds of variations that may occur in real-world scenarios. However, we anticipate that the performance may degrade if the adversarial attack algorithm is not properly aligned with the HOI detection task, or if the transformed interaction descriptions are too similar to the original descriptions.
propositions.texte: We will propose a new adversarial training method that transforms interaction descriptions to create adversarial examples, and use these examples to train the HOI detection model to be more robust to variations in interaction descriptions.
propositions.titre: Adversarial Training for HOI Detection with Transformed Interaction Descriptions

propositions.controles: Standard HOI detection models, a comprehensive evaluation framework, and a benchmarking dataset.
propositions.prediction: We expect that the holistic evaluation framework and benchmark will provide a comprehensive assessment of HOI detection models and opportunities for improvement, and that the benchmarking dataset will serve as a valuable resource for the research community.
propositions.texte: We will create a comprehensive evaluation framework and benchmark to assess the performance of HOI detection models on various aspects, including interaction detection, object detection, and relationship recognition, and to compare the performance of the proposed methods with state-of-the-art models.
propositions.titre: Holistic Evaluation and Benchmarking for HOI Detection

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing the Limits of CLIP-based HOI Detection
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of CLIP-based HOI detection methods on_seen and unseen interactions, while probing their limitations in distinguishing visually similar interactions and generalizing to unseen interactions.
CONTROLS: Compare with recent state-of-the-art CLIP-based HOI detection methods, which include HAT-BERT, CALORIE, and CIAT.
COST: 5 GPU-hours (performing experiments on a single large-scale HOI dataset with several models).
PREDICTION: These methods will achieve better performance on seen interactions but struggle to generalize to unseen interactions, demonstrating a need for more robust vision-language models or more effective transfer learning mechanisms.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multitask Learning for Generalizable HOI Recognition
PROPOSAL: Train a model to recognize human-object interactions, object categories, and verb categories simultaneously, leveraging the connection between object and verb features for compositional generalization.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that only trains the model on interaction recognition, and ablate the verb categorization task to evaluate its contribution.
COST: 10 GPU-hours (multiple passes through the HOI dataset with three tasks), leaving room for later revisions to explore potential benefits of multitask learning.
PREDICTION: Multitask learning will lead to improved generalization to unseen interactions and verbs, especially when considering object categories. However, the potential overfitting to seen interactions might arise if the dataset size is limited.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Multitask Learning for Generalizable HOI Recognition
PROPPEAL: REVISED - Modify the multitask learning proposal to include an attention mechanism to adaptively weigh the interactions between object and verb features, allowing the model to selectively focus on relevant features when generalizing to unseen interactions.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that uses a simple feature concatenation approach and ablate the attention mechanism to evaluate its contribution.
COST: The revised proposal will incur a minimal increase in cost, approximately 2-3 GPU-hours, to account for the added complexity of the attention mechanism.
PREDICTION: Adding an attention mechanism will improve the model's ability to selectively focus on relevant features when generalizing to unseen interactions, leading to better performance on unseen interactions, especially in the presence of visually similar interactions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compositionally Generalizable HOI Detection via Conditional Classifiers
PROPOSAL: Develop a conditional classifier architecture that takes both object and verb embeddings as inputs and outputs the likelihood of each interaction, accounting for the relationships between objects and verbs.
CONTROLS: Compare with the current state-of-the-art CLIP-based HOI detection methods and ablate the conditional classifier to evaluate its contribution.
COST: 8 GPU-hours (requires multiple experiments on HOI datasets with varying object and verb embeddings).
PREDICTION: The conditional classifier will enable compositional generalization, leading to improved HOI detection performance on unseen interactions, especially when objects or verbs are not seen during training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging Pre-trained Object Detectors for Efficient HOI Detection
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of pre-trained object detectors as features for HOI detection, exploring various fusion methods to incorporate these features into existing HOI detection architectures.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that trains an object detector from scratch and ablate different fusion methods to evaluate their contributions.
COST: 4 GPU-hours (requires experiments on a pre-trained object detector and various fusion methods).
PREDICTION: Incorporating pre-trained object detector features will improve HOI detection efficiency and accuracy, especially when using a simple fusion method like concatenation or element-wise multiplication.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Compositionally Generalizable HOI Detection via Conditional Classifiers
PROPOAL: REVISED - Introduce a new subnet to the conditional classifier architecture that focuses on learning the relationships between objects and verbs, in addition to the existing object and verb embeddings input.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original conditional classifier and ablate the new subnet to evaluate its contribution.
COST: The revised proposal will incur a moderate increase in cost, approximately 4-5 GPU-hours, to account for the added complexity of the new subnet.
PREDICTION: The new subnet will enable more accurate modeling of object and verb relationships, leading to improved HOI detection performance on unseen interactions. However, the potential risk of overfitting to seen object-verb pairs might arise if the dataset size is limited.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving HOI Detection with Off-the-Shelf Pre-trained Language Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of off-the-shelf pre-trained language models, such as BERT or RoBERTa, as a source of semantic knowledge for improving HOI detection, particularly in scenarios where interaction recognition is challenging.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that uses a random initialization for the language model and ablate different components of the pre-trained language model to evaluate their contributions.
COST: 12 GPU-hours (requires experiments with pre-trained language models and various ablations).
PREDICTION: Utilizing pre-trained language models will significantly improve HOI detection performance, especially on interactions that involve abstract or nuanced verbs, by providing a rich source of semantic knowledge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unbiased Evaluation of HOI Detection Methods
PROPOSAL: Design a new evaluation protocol that accounts for the class imbalance between common and rare interactions in HOI detection, evaluating the performance of various methods on unseen interactions while controlling for their ability to recognize common interactions.
CONTROLS: Apply the new evaluation protocol to each method in the set and compare performance.
COST: Minimal cost, approximately 1-2 GPU-hours (processing metrics for existing models and results).
PREDICTION: By accounting for the class imbalance, the new evaluation protocol will reveal differences in performance that were not apparent under standard evaluation metrics, potentially leading to a re-ranking of existing methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer HOI Models to New Scenarios via Zero-Shot Learning
PROPOSAL: Explore the application of zero-shot learning to transfer HOI models to new scenarios, such as different environments, object categories, or languages, without extensive retraining or adaptation.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that uses traditional fine-tuning and ablate different components of the zero-shot learning framework.
COST: 15 GPU-hours (requires experiments on multiple scenarios and evaluation metrics).
PREDICTION: Zero-shot learning will enable the transfer of HOI models to new scenarios, improving versatility and adaptability, but the performance may degrade when faced with highly dissimilar scenarios, highlighting the need for further research on adaptability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable and Composable HOI Reasoning Framework via Graph Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: Develop a graph neural network (GNN) based framework for composable and scalable HOI reasoning, allowing for reasoning over multiple objects, interactions, and scenes simultaneously.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that uses a traditional image-based approach and ablate different components of the GNN framework.
COST: 25 GPU-hours (requires experiments on large and complex HOI scenes).
PREDICTION: The GNN-based framework will enable efficient and accurate reasoning over complex HOI scenes, leading to state-of-the-art performance, but the potential risk of overfitting to large scene graphs might arise if the training dataset is limited.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contextualized Diversity Guidance for Conditional Image Generators
PROPOSAL: Experimentally validate an exemplar-based guidance method, called CDG (Contextualized Diversity Guidance), which leverages a small set of real exemplar images to jointly improve both the quality and diversity of the images produced by off-the-shelf conditional generators, grounded in a target real distribution.
CONTROLS: Vanilla conditional generator, VSG (Vendi Score Guidance), c-VSG (Contextualized Vendi Score Guidance), fine-tuning with reward feedback
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: CDG shows significant improvements in both quality and diversity compared to baselines, and the benefit grows gradually as more exemplars become available, unlike existing exemplar-based guidance methods. However, it may not outperform training-based fine-tuning for superior generators or large exemplar sets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exemplar-Dependence of CDG
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of the number of exemplars on the performance of CDG, by scaling the exemplar set from 5 to 50 images and analyzing the quality and diversity of generated images.
CONTROLS: Varying numbers of exemplars (5, 10, 20, 30, 50), with each number tested at least 5 times to account for variance
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Analyzing the relationship between the number of exemplars and performance will reveal whether there is a sweet spot for the exemplar set size that balances between too few and too many images. When too few, it may not provide enough context; when too many, it may not be practically feasible.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generalizability across Domains and Regions
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the generalizability of CDG across different geographic regions and object domains by training on real-world data from various world regions, and testing on target regions with different object domains.
CONTROLS: Real-world datasets from the CLEVR-GR dataset for geographic diversity, and different object domains from ImageNet and other standard datasets
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: CDG will demonstrate robustness across different regions and object domains, with the ability to adapt to new regions and objects with a small number of exemplars, but may require more fine-tuning for region or object-specific adaptations.

Controls: Vanilla conditional generator, VSG (Vendi Score Guidance), c-VSG (Contextualized Vendi Score Guidance), fine-tuning with reward feedback
Estimated cost: 1000 GPU-hours
Prediction: CDG shows significant improvements in both quality and diversity compared to baselines, and the benefit grows gradually as more exemplars become available, unlike existing exemplar-based guidance methods. However, it may not outperform training-based fine-tuning for superior generators or large exemplar sets.

PROPOSAL 2: Exemplar-Dependence of CDG
Investigate the effect of the number of exemplars on the performance of CDG, by scaling the exemplar set from 5 to 50 images and analyzing the quality and diversity of generated images.
Controls: Varying numbers of exemplars (5, 10, 20, 30, 50), with each number tested at least 5 times to account for variance
Estimated cost: 500 GPU-hours
Prediction: Analyzing the relationship between the number of exemplars and performance will reveal whether there is a sweet spot for the exemplar set size that balances between too few and too many images. When too few, it may not provide enough context; when too many, it may not be practically feasible.

PROPOSAL 3: Generalizability across Domains and Regions
Evaluate the generalizability of CDG across different geographic regions and object domains by training on real-world data from various world regions, and testing on target regions with different object domains.
Controls: Real-world datasets from the CLEVR-GR dataset for geographic diversity, and different object domains from ImageNet and other standard datasets
Estimated cost: 2000 GPU-hours
Prediction: CDG will demonstrate robustness across different regions and object domains, with the ability to adapt to new regions and objects with a small number of exemplars, but may require more fine-tuning for region or object-specific adaptations.

PROPOSAL 4: Comparison to Training-Based Methods with Real Exemplars
Experimentally compare CDG with training-based methods that utilize real exemplars for fine-tuning or training of conditional generators, to assess the relative strengths and limitations of each approach in balancing quality and diversity.
Controls: Training-based fine-tuning, Meta-Learning Methods with augmented proportion of data, CDG with fine-tuning support as ablation study
Estimated cost: 1000 GPU-hours
Prediction: Training-based methods may outperform CDG on certain metrics, but the added complexity and lower efficiency of training-based methods may reduce their overall utility, making CDG a more practical choice for certain scenarios.

PROPOSAL 5: Evaluating Utility as Training Data for Downstream Models
Assess the utility of CDG outputs as training data for downstream models in a specific application, such as image classification or object detection, using real-world datasets and comparing its performance to real data and competing synthetic data sources.
Controls: State-of-the-art downstream models, competing synthetic data sources (e.g., GAN-generated data), real-world datasets (e.g., images of various object categories)
Estimated cost: 2500 GPU-hours
Prediction: If CDG's outputs are well-matched with the target distribution, we can demonstrate that they outperform or rival real data and competing synthetic sources in downstream model performance, indicating a significant utility increase for CDG as a training data generator.

PROPOSAL 6: Analyzing Distribution Shift and Representation
Investigate the representation of real data in CDG's outputs, and assess the consistency and distribution shift between CDG's outputs, real data, and downstream model predictions.

Identify the limitations of CDG by analyzing its performance on tasks that are particularly challenging for conditional image generators, such as high-level concept learning or generated image semantics.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Evaluating Existing Exemplar-Based Guidance Methods
PROPOSAL: We benchmark existing exemplar-based guidance methods, such as Contextualized Vendi Score Guidance (c-VSG), on a set of real-world image datasets and classify their performances under different metrics and scenarios (various numbers of exemplars, target distribution types). We also analyze their failure modes to better understand their limitations.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Vanilla conditional generator
- Baseline 2: c-VSG with varying numbers of exemplars
- Baseline 3: Different target distribution types (e.g., urban, natural, architecture)
- Ablication 1: Remove c-VSG's contextualization component
- Ablication 2: Use only a single exemplar
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: c-VSG will demonstrate improved diversity, but it may not outperform vanilla generators in terms of quality. Its performance may degrade when the target distribution is too complex or when fewer exemplars are used. We expect the analysis to reveal insights into the potential of exemplar-based guidance and its challenges.

Note: This proposal serves as a control and a sanity check for later experiment proposals.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Using Few-Shot Learning for Exemplar-Based Guidance
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of a few-shot learning-based approach for exemplar-based guidance, which adapts the existing model to a specific target distribution using a small set of exemplar images. We use a pre-trained conditional generator as the base model and fine-tune its early layers with the exemplars as few-shot training data, while keeping the rest of the model fixed. We experiment with different meta-learning algorithms and training settings to achieve our goal.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Vanilla fine-tuning with reward feedback (as in the literature)
- Baseline 2: Using a pre-trained model to generate samples without fine-tuning
- Ablation 1: Few-shot learning using only the early layers of the model
- Ablation 2: No fine-tuning of the model's parameters (i.e., learning only the input/output mappings)
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The few-shot learning approach should lead to better quality and diversity in the generated samples, given the specific target distribution. However, it may be sensitive to the quality and diversity of the exemplars, and the choice of few-shot learning algorithm and training settings.

This proposal explores an alternative exemplar-based guidance method that leverages few-shot learning to adapt the model to a specific target distribution.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Using Few-Shot Learning for Exemplar-Based Guidance with Improved Regularization
PROPOSAL: We extend the few-shot learning approach by incorporating an improved regularization mechanism to prevent overfitting to the exemplar images and enhance the model's ability to generalize to diverse target distributions. Specifically, we add a weight decay term to the loss function that encourages the model to maintain its pre-trained knowledge, while also introducing a data augmentation-based regularization term to robustify the model against distribution shifts.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Vanilla few-shot learning approach (as in REVISED 2)
- Baseline 2: Few-shot learning with weight decay only
- Baseline 3: Few-shot learning with data augmentation-based regularization only
- Ablation 1: Remove the weight decay term from the regularized loss function
- Ablation 2: Use only a single exemplar image for regularization
COST: 20 GPU-hours (assuming previous experiments have been performed)
PREDICTION: By incorporating the improved regularization mechanism, the model should exhibit more robust generalization to diverse target distributions and achieve better balance between quality and diversity in the generated samples. However, it may sacrifice a small amount of performance on the specific target distribution used during training.

This revised proposal builds upon the few-shot learning approach, introducing a key regularization component to enhance the model's robustness and generalization abilities.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Contextualized Few-Shot Learning with Hierarchical Exemplar Embeddings
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach that combines the benefits of few-shot learning and contextualized guidance. Specifically, we introduce a hierarchical exemplar embedding mechanism, where the exemplar images are embedded into a higher-level feature space using a pre-trained multi-modal encoder. This enriched embedding captures both low-level visual details and high-level contextual information, enabling the model to better adapt to specific target distributions.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: REVISED 2 (few-shot learning with improved regularization)
- Baseline 2: few-shot learning without hierarchical exemplar embeddings
- Ablation 1: Remove the hierarchical exemplar embedding component
- Ablation 2: Use a vanilla multi-modal encoder instead of a pre-trained one
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Contextualized few-shot learning with hierarchical exemplar embeddings should significantly improve the model's ability to adapt to diverse target distributions and generate high-quality, diverse images. However, it may require larger amounts of training data or computational resources due to the increased complexity of the hierarchical embedding mechanism.

This proposal brings together two complementary perspectives: few-shot learning for efficient adaptation and contextualized guidance for informative exemplar embeddings.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Multi-Exemplar Data on Quality, Diversity, and Utility
PROPOSAL: We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the impact of multi-exemplar data on quality, diversity, and utility of the generated images. Specifically, we compare the performance of our proposed contextualized few-shot learning approach with varying numbers of exemplars (from 1 to 5) and investigate the relationships between exemplar count, quality, diversity, and utility of the generated images. We also analyze the effect of exemplar diversity on the performance of the model.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Single-exemplar data using REVISED 2
- Baseline 2: Three-exemplar data using REVISED 2
- Baseline 3: Five-exemplar data using REVISED 2
- Ablation 1: Remove the hierarchical exemplar embedding component
- Ablation 2: Use only a single exemplar with varying image resolutions
COST: 75 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that using multiple exemplars will improve quality, diversity, and utility of the generated images, with diminishing marginal returns as the exemplar count increases. However, the performance may also suffer from over-fitting or decreased efficiency as the number of exemplars grows.

This proposal provides an in-depth analysis of the relationship between the number of exemplars and the performance of the model, shedding light on the optimal exemplar count for real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Evaluating the Geographic Diversity of Generated Images Across World Regions
PROPOSAL: We extend our evaluation to investigate the geographic diversity of generated images across world regions. Specifically, we select a subset of the image datasets and focus on the geographic variations within each region (e.g., urban, natural, architecture). We measure the geographic diversity of generated images using a combination of metrics, including region-wise FID scores, area under the ROC curves, and an entropy-based measure of regional representativeness.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: REVISED 2 with all exemplars from a single region
- Baseline 2: REVISED 2 with exemplars from multiple regions
- Baseline 3: Contextualized few-shot learning with hierarchical exemplar embeddings, with exemplars from a single region
- Baseline 4: Contextualized few-shot learning with hierarchical exemplar embeddings, with exemplars from multiple regions
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that contextualized few-shot learning with hierarchical exemplar embeddings will outperform REVISED 2 in terms of geographic diversity, especially when using multiple region-wise exemplars. However, it may still struggle to generalize across regions with vastly different characteristics.

This proposal evaluates the model's ability to generate images that capture the geographic diversity of world regions, which is a critical aspect of the research problem.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Investigating the Utility of Exemplar-Based Synthetic Data for Downstream Models
PROPOSAL: We investigate the utility of exemplar-based synthetic data generated by our contextualized few-shot learning approach for training downstream models. Specifically, we take the synthetic images and use them as training data for various downstream models (e.g., object detection, semantic segmentation, and image classification). We compare the performance of these models trained on exemplar-based synthetic data with those trained on real-world data.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Downstream models trained on real-world data
- Baseline 2: Downstream models trained on synthetic data generated by REVISED 2
- Baseline 3: Downstream models trained on synthetic data generated by contextualized few-shot learning with hierarchical exemplar embeddings
- Ablation 1: Remove the hierarchical exemplar embedding component
- Ablation 2: Use a smaller synthetic dataset for training
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the contextualized few-shot learning approach will generate synthetic data that is highly useful for training downstream models, especially when compared to REVISED 2. However, the performance of downstream models trained on synthetic data may still be inferior to those trained on real-world data due to the inherent limitations of exemplar-based synthetic data.

This proposal evaluates the ultimate goal of our research: generating high-quality, diverse, and useful synthetic data for downstream models.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Evaluating Existing Exemplar-Based Guidance Methods with Enhanced Evaluation Metrics
PROPOSAL: We revisit the existing exemplar-based guidance methods and evaluate their performance using the state-of-the-art metrics and techniques developed in our previous proposals (e.g., quality, diversity, geographic diversity, and utility). Additionally, we incorporate advanced evaluation metrics such as Inception Score (IS), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and mode coverage to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the performance of these methods.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: REVISED 1 (original evaluation with limited metrics)
- Baseline 2: REVISED 1 with additional metrics (IS, FID, mode coverage)
- Baseline 3: REVISED 1 with hierarchical exemplar embeddings
- Ablation 1: Remove the additional metrics
- Ablation 2: Use a smaller set of evaluation metrics
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the enhanced evaluation framework will provide a more nuanced understanding of the performance of existing exemplar-based guidance methods, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses.

This revised proposal refines the evaluation of existing methods and sets a foundation for comparison with our novel approaches.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Investigation of Robustness to Real-World Distribution Shifts
PROPOSAL: We investigate the robustness of our contextualized few-shot learning approach to real-world distribution shifts, such as changes in illumination, viewpoint, and object occlusion. We use a variety of evaluation metrics (e.g., mean average precision, precision at k, and Robust F1 score) to assess the model's ability to generalize to novel, unseen cases.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: REVISED 2 with all exemplars from a single distribution
- Baseline 2: REVISED 2 with exemplars from multiple distributions
- Ablation 1: Remove the hierarchical exemplar embedding component
- Ablation 2: Use only a limited number of evaluation metrics
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that our contextualized few-shot learning approach will demonstrate robustness to real-world distribution shifts, especially when using hierarchical exemplar embeddings. However, the model may still struggle with extreme cases of distribution shift.

This proposal investigates an essential aspect of any AI model: robustness to real-world distribution shifts. Enhancing the robustness of our model will contribute to its reliability in various practical scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Comparison with State-of-the-Art Synthetic Data Generation Strategies
PROPOSAL: We compare the performance of our contextualized few-shot learning approach with state-of-the-art synthetic data generation strategies (e.g., GAN-based methods, adversarial training, and cycle-consistent Generative Adversarial Networks). We evaluate the quality, diversity, geographic diversity, and utility of the generated images, as well as their robustness to real-world distribution shifts.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: State-of-the-art GAN-based method (e.g., StyleGAN2, BigGAN)
- Baseline 2: Adversarial training-based method (e.g., DCGAN, LSGAN)
- Baseline 3: Cycle-consistent Generative Adversarial Network (CycleGAN)
- Ablation 1: Remove the hierarchical exemplar embedding component
- Ablation 2: Compare with only one state-of-the-art method
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that our contextualized few-shot learning approach will outperform or at least match the state-of-the-art synthetic data generation strategies, especially when considering the quality, diversity, and geographic diversity of the generated images.

This proposal compares our approach with the existing state-of-the-art methods, providing an overarching assessment of its performance and a comprehensive conclusion to the research.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rethinking Diversity Metrics for Conditional Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of alternate diversity metrics that incorporate contextual information from real-world data, such as mutual information and exemplar-based Kullback-Leibler divergence. We will train a set of conditional image generators on various datasets and compute diversity metrics on the generated images. Controls will include the standard diversity metric (inception score) and the metrics from prior work (e.g., intra-class covariance). We will also assess the sensitivity of our selected metrics to the number of exemplars used.
CONTROLS: Inception score, intra-class covariance, metrics from prior work (e.g., c-VSG)
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the new metrics will provide a more nuanced understanding of diversity, revealing that the existing metrics are too narrow to capture the true variability of generated images. However, this may lead to higher computational costs for diversity evaluation and potential trade-offs with quality metrics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Harnessing Exemplars for Conditional Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop an exemplar-based guidance method that utilizes a small set of real-world images to improve the quality and diversity of conditional image generation. We will leverage the concept of few-shot in-context learning and design an algorithm that adaptively incorporates the contextualizing real images to ground the diversity and quality of generations. This method, dubbed "Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation" (EG-CIG), will be evaluated on various real-world datasets. Controls will include vanilla conditional image generation, c-VSG, and fine-tuning with reward feedback. We will also investigate the impact of varying exemplar sizes on the method's performance.
CONTROLS: Vanilla CIG, c-VSG, fine-tuning with reward feedback
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect EG-CIG to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in balancing quality and diversity, with an improvement in Area Under the Curve (AUC) compared to existing methods. However, the performance might degrade when too few or too many exemplars are used, indicating an optimal range for exemplar sizes.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Harnessing Exemplars for Conditional Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop an algorithm that incorporates a small set of real-world images to improve the quality and diversity of conditional image generation, leveraging the concept of few-shot in-context learning. We will design an adaptive method, Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG), that selectively incorporates contextualizing real images to ground the diversity and quality of generations. To improve scalability, we will investigate the application of contrastive learning and hybrid memory-and-bias module as an alternative to adaptive incorporation. This method will be evaluated on various real-world datasets, including those with varying levels of geographic diversity in object images across world regions. Controls will include vanilla conditional image generation, c-VSG, and fine-tuning with reward feedback. We will also investigate the impact of varying exemplar sizes on the method's performance.
CONTROLS: Vanilla CIG, c-VSG, fine-tuning with reward feedback
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect EG-CIG with hybrid memory-and-bias module to improve the quality and diversity of generated images, with a significant increase in M4-~~~~~~~~score and density of objects at diverse regions than the vanilla ALT.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED: Harnessing Exemplars for Conditional Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop an algorithm that incorporates a small set of real-world images to improve the quality and diversity of conditional image generation, leveraging the concept of few-shot in-context learning. We will design an adaptive method, Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG), that selectively incorporates contextualizing real images to ground the diversity and quality of generations. To improve scalability, we will investigate the application of contrastive learning and hybrid memory-and-bias module as an alternative to adaptive incorporation. This method will be evaluated on various real-world datasets, including those with varying levels of geographic diversity in object images across world regions. We will also propose a novel evaluation metric, "geo-exemplar similarity" (GES), to quantify how well generated images align with exemplars from diverse regions. Controls will include vanilla conditional image generation, c-VSG, and fine-tuning with reward feedback. We will also investigate the impact of varying exemplar sizes on the method's performance.
CONTROLS: Vanilla CIG, c-VSG, fine-tuning with reward feedback
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect EG-CIG with hybrid memory-and-bias module to improve the quality and diversity of generated images, with a significant increase in M4-~~~~~~~~score and density of objects at diverse regions than the vanilla ALT. However, we anticipate that the GES metric may be sensitive to the choice of exemplars and may require careful sampling strategies to ensure reliable results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing Offline and Online Exemplar-Based Guidance
PROPOSAL: Investigate the difference between offline and online exemplar-based guidance approaches for improving the quality and diversity of conditional image generation. Offline methods involve pre-processing the exemplars to create a statistical model, while online methods adaptively incorporate the exemplars into the generation process at runtime. We will compare the performance of offline and online exemplar-based guidance approaches, specifically Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG), on various real-world datasets. Controls will include vanilla conditional image generation, c-VSG, and fine-tuning with reward feedback. We will also investigate the impact of offline vs. online exemplar-guidance pipelines on EG-CIG's performance.
CONTROLS: Vanilla CIG, c-VSG, fine-tuning with reward feedback
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect online exemplar-guidance approaches to outperform offline approaches, as they can adapt more effectively to the changing distribution of the target domain. However, we may observe that offline approaches are more computationally efficient and can be more easily parallelized, leading to a trade-off between performance and efficiency.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: REVISED: Comparing Offline and Online Exemplar-Based Guidance
PROPOSAL: Investigate the difference between offline and online exemplar-based guidance approaches for improving the quality and diversity of conditional image generation. Offline methods involve pre-processing the exemplars to create a statistical model, while online methods adaptively incorporate the exemplars into the generation process at runtime. We will extend the evaluation of online exemplar-based guidance approaches by incorporating the concept of episodic memory, which allows the model to retain a limited number of previously encountered exemplars and adaptively update its statistics. This revised approach, dubbed "Episodic Online Exemplar Guidance" (EOEG), will be compared to offline and vanilla online exemplar-based guidance approaches. Controls will include vanilla conditional image generation, c-VSG, and fine-tuning with reward feedback. We will also investigate the impact of varying episode lengths and memory sizes on EOEG's performance.
CONTROLS: Vanilla CIG, c-VSG, fine-tuning with reward feedback
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect EOEG to outperform both offline and vanilla online exemplar-based guidance approaches, as it takes advantage of the benefits of episodic memory while adaptively incorporating new exemplars. However, we may observe that EOEG is more computationally expensive and requires careful tuning of hyperparameters to avoid memory overflows and information overload.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing the Impact of Geographically Diverse Exemplars
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of using geographically diverse exemplars on the quality and diversity of generated images. We will curate a dataset of images from diverse geographic regions and evaluate the performance of Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG) on this dataset. We will compare the results to those obtained using uniform distribution of exemplars and explore the impact of varying the number and diversity of exemplars on EG-CIG's performance. Controls will include vanilla conditional image generation, c-VSG, and fine-tuning with reward feedback. We will also investigate the correlation between the geographic diversity of exemplars and the diversity of generated images.
CONTROLS: Vanilla CIG, c-VSG, fine-tuning with reward feedback
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect EG-CIG to perform better on the geographically diverse dataset, as it will be able to learn patterns and features that are unique to specific regions. However, we may observe that excessive geographic diversity in the exemplars can lead to over-specialization and decreased performance on images from unseen regions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Evaluation of Synthetic Training Data
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the effectiveness of synthetic training data generated by Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG) in real-world downstream tasks. We will train a variety of machine learning models on synthetic data generated using EG-CIG and compare their performance to those trained on real-world data. We will also investigate the transferability of EG-CIG-generated data across different tasks, domains, and geographic regions. Controls will include models trained on real-world data and synthetic data generated using alternative methods. We will assess the generalization performance, robustness, and fairness of models trained on synthetic data.
CONTROLS: Models trained on real-world data, synthetic data generated using alternative methods
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect models trained on synthetic data generated by EG-CIG to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in real-world downstream tasks, with significant improvements in generalization and robustness. However, we may observe that the transferability of EG-CIG-generated data across different tasks, domains, and geographic regions is limited, indicating the need for further research on adapting the method to specific real-world applications.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: REVISED: Real-World Evaluation of Synthetic Training Data
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the effectiveness of synthetic training data generated by Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG) in real-world downstream tasks. We will train a set of machine learning models on synthetic data generated using EG-CIG and compare their performance to those trained on real-world data. In addition to generalization performance, we will also investigate the robustness and fairness of models trained on synthetic data, focusing on aspects such as shift robustness, calibration, and group fairness. We will assess the synthetic data's potential to mitigate bias in real-world datasets and bridge the gap between diverse demographics and image representations. Controls will include models trained on real-world data and synthetic data generated using alternative methods. We will also evaluate the transferability of EG-CIG-generated data across different tasks, domains, and geographic regions.
CONTROLS: Models trained on real-world data, synthetic data generated using alternative methods
COST: 450 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect models trained on synthetic data generated by EG-CIG to demonstrate improved robustness, fairness, and shift robustness, reducing the gap between diverse demographics and image representations. However, we may observe that the synthetic data's effectiveness in mitigating bias is limited by the quality and diversity of the real-world data used to train EG-CIG, serving as a reminder of the need for high-quality training data in machine learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalability and Efficiency of Exemplar-Based Guidance
PROPOSAL: Investigate the scalability and efficiency of the exemplar-based guidance approach employed in Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG). We will evaluate the method's performance on large-scale datasets and assess the impact of varying the number of exemplars, the size of the image distribution, and the dimensionality of the feature space. We will also explore techniques to improve the computational efficiency of the method, such as using approximation algorithms, parallel processing, or leveraging GPU acceleration. Controls will include the vanilla EG-CIG method and alternative exemplar-based guidance approaches.
CONTROLS: Vanilla EG-CIG, alternative exemplar-based guidance approaches
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the exemplar-based guidance approach to scale well with the size of the datasets, but may observe a significant increase in computational cost with very large datasets. However, we anticipate that efficient memory management and parallel processing can significantly mitigate these costs, making the method more practical for real-world applications.

This method will be evaluated on various real-world datasets, including those with varying levels of geographic diversity in object images across world regions. We will also propose a novel evaluation metric, "geo-exemplar similarity" (GES), to quantify how well generated images align with exemplars from diverse regions. Controls will include vanilla conditional image generation, c-VSG, and fine-tuning with reward feedback. We will also investigate the impact of varying exemplar sizes on the method's performance.
propositions.titre: REVISED: Harnessing Exemplars for Conditional Image Generation

propositions.controles: Vanilla CIG, c-VSG, fine-tuning with reward feedback
propositions.prediction: We expect EOEG to outperform both offline and vanilla online exemplar-based guidance approaches, as it takes advantage of the benefits of episodic memory while adaptively incorporating new exemplars. However, we may observe that EOEG is more computationally expensive and requires careful tuning of hyperparameters to avoid memory overflows and information overload.
propositions.texte: Investigate the difference between offline and online exemplar-based guidance approaches for improving the quality and diversity of conditional image generation. Offline methods involve pre-processing the exemplars to create a statistical model, while online methods adaptively incorporate the exemplars into the generation process at runtime. We will extend the evaluation of online exemplar-based guidance approaches by incorporating the concept of episodic memory, which allows the model to retain a limited number of previously encountered exemplars and adaptively update its statistics. This revised approach, dubbed "Episodic Online Exemplar Guidance" (EOEG), will be compared to offline and vanilla online exemplar-based guidance approaches. Controls will include vanilla conditional image generation, c-VSG, and fine-tuning with reward feedback. We will also investigate the impact of varying episode lengths and memory sizes on EOEG's performance.
propositions.titre: REVISED: Comparing Offline and Online Exemplar-Based Guidance

propositions.controles: Vanilla CIG, c-VSG, fine-tuning with reward feedback
propositions.prediction: We expect EG-CIG to perform better on the geographically diverse dataset, as it will be able to learn patterns and features that are unique to specific regions. However, we may observe that excessive geographic diversity in the exemplars can lead to over-specialization and decreased performance on images from unseen regions.
propositions.texte: Investigate the effect of using geographically diverse exemplars on the quality and diversity of generated images. We will curate a dataset of images from diverse geographic regions and evaluate the performance of Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG) on this dataset. We will compare the results to those obtained using uniform distribution of exemplars and explore the impact of varying the number and diversity of exemplars on EG-CIG's performance. Controls will include vanilla conditional image generation, c-VSG, and fine-tuning with reward feedback. We will also investigate the correlation between the geographic diversity of exemplars and the diversity of generated images.
propositions.titre: Assessing the Impact of Geographically Diverse Exemplars

propositions.controles: Models trained on real-world data, synthetic data generated using alternative methods
propositions.prediction: We expect models trained on synthetic data generated by EG-CIG to demonstrate improved robustness, fairness, and shift robustness, reducing the gap between diverse demographics and image representations. However, we may observe that the synthetic data's effectiveness in mitigating bias is limited by the quality and diversity of the real-world data used to train EG-CIG, serving as a reminder of the need for high-quality training data in machine learning.
propositions.texte: Evaluate the effectiveness of synthetic training data generated by Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG) in real-world downstream tasks. We will train a set of machine learning models on synthetic data generated using EG-CIG and compare their performance to those trained on real-world data. In addition to generalization performance, we will also investigate the robustness and fairness of models trained on synthetic data, focusing on aspects such as shift robustness, calibration, and group fairness. We will assess the synthetic data's potential to mitigate bias in real-world datasets and bridge the gap between diverse demographics and image representations. Controls will include models trained on real-world data and synthetic data generated using alternative methods. We will also evaluate the transferability of EG-CIG-generated data across different tasks, domains, and geographic regions.
propositions.titre: REVISED: Real-World Evaluation of Synthetic Training Data

propositions.controles: Vanilla EG-CIG, alternative exemplar-based guidance approaches
propositions.prediction: We expect the exemplar-based guidance approach to scale well with the size of the datasets, but may observe a significant increase in computational cost with very large datasets. However, we anticipate that efficient memory management and parallel processing can significantly mitigate these costs, making the method more practical for real-world applications.
propositions.texte: Investigate the scalability and efficiency of the exemplar-based guidance approach employed in Exemplar-Guided Conditional Image Generation (EG-CIG). We will evaluate the method's performance on large-scale datasets and assess the impact of varying the number of exemplars, the size of the image distribution, and the dimensionality of the feature space. We will also explore techniques to improve the computational efficiency of the method, such as using approximation algorithms, parallel processing, or leveraging GPU acceleration. Controls will include the vanilla EG-CIG method and alternative exemplar-based guidance approaches.
propositions.titre: Scalability and Efficiency of Exemplar-Based Guidance

PREDICTION: The comprehensive visualization and analysis framework will provide valuable insights into the behavior and performance of the hybrid visual document retrievers, and help to identify potential areas for improvement.
