actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lightweight Hybrid Retrieval for Vision-Centric Multimodal Retrievers
PROPOSAL: Implement a hybrid retrieval system that combines a strong vision-centric multimodal retriever based on ColPali (e.g., ColPali encoder with late interaction) with a text dense retriever that uses a pre-trained dense semantic text encoder (e.g., DenseFuse) and ranks documents based on their weighted sum of scores from both models. Weights are learned using a simple weighting scheme during training, and we analyze the importance of these weights.
CONTROLS: Compare against an ensemble of scores from both models, as well as each model in isolation. We also ablate the effect of pre-training the dense text encoder and explore different weighting schemes.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (pre-training dense encoder + hyperparameter search + model training)
PREDICTION: The hybrid system should show improved performance and better trade-off between latency and index memory compared to using only the vision-centric retriever. However, if the dense text retriever is too weak, the hybrid system may not show significant improvements.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Lightweight Hybrid Retrieval for Vision-Centric Multimodal Retrievers
PROPOSAL: REVISED: The system is now called Alan (Adapter for Lightweight Learning). In Alan, we adapt a pre-trained ColPali-based multimodal retriever using a text-focused dense retriever (e.g., DenseFuse) trained on a smaller set of in-domain text data as a freezing selectable adapter on top of the vision-centric model. This brings the potential of acquiring complementary information without scaling up the vision-centric model itself. We also explore using different adapter architectures and freezing schemes.
CONTROLS: Compare against the pre-trained ColPali model, the ColPali model with fine-tuned text encoder, and the dense text encoder alone. We also compare different adapter architectures and examine the learned adapter weights.
COST: 70 GPU-hours (pre-training adapters + hyperparameter search + model training)
PREDICTION: Alan should outperform the pre-trained ColPali model and exhibit reduced scale while bringing complementary benefits from the dense retriever. However, it may require large labeled datasets to train effectively, which might hinder real-world applicability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adapter Learning and Analysis in Alan
PROPOSAL: Analyze the learning properties and dynamics of the adapter in Alan, including how it adapts to the pre-trained ColPali-based retriever, what features it focuses on, and how it compares to fine-tuning the text encoder. We will use various analysis tools such as gradient visualization, activation maps, and sensitivity analysis to better understand the behavior of the adapter.
CONTROLS: Compare against fine-tuning the text encoder and ablate the effects of different adapter architectures and learning rates.
COST: 10 GPU-hours (analysis and visualization only)
PREDICTION: The analysis should reveal the strengths and weaknesses of the adapter learning strategy and provide valuable insights for improving Alan. Additionally, we may gain a better understanding of why the adapter sometimes fails to improve upon fine-tuning the text encoder alone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Hybrid Retrieval via Indirect Interaction
PROPOSAL: Modify the hybrid retrieval system to use an indirect interaction scheme, where the output of the dense text retriever is not directly combined with the output of the ColPali-based retriever. Instead, we use the output of the dense text retriever to select a subset of the top-ranked documents from the ColPali-based retriever, and then use a simple, fast, and lightweight aggregation function (e.g., a linear combination) to combine the scores of the selected documents.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original hybrid retrieval system, as well as a version where the dense text retriever outputs direct scores for each document, and a version where the ColPali-based retriever outputs direct scores for each document.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (model training + hyperparameter search)
PREDICTION: The indirect interaction scheme should lead to a more efficient and scalable hybrid retrieval system, that should still provide competitive performance to the original system. However, it may require careful tuning of the aggregation function and the selection of top-ranked documents.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: On-Device Hybrid Retrieval for Edge Computing
PROPOSAL: Adapt the hybrid retrieval system and Alan to work on a single GPU with limited memory (i.e., on-device), utilizing a combination of model pruning, knowledge distillation, and efficient aggregation techniques to reduce the memory footprint of both models while maintaining their performance. This will enable the system to deploy on edge devices with limited resources.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art lightweight models and evaluate their performance on a diverse set of edge devices.
COST: 30 GPU-hours (model pruning + distillation + on-device evaluation)
PREDICTION: The on-device adaptation should enable the hybrid retrieval system to run efficiently on edge devices, with potential applications in real-time document retrieval, search, and browsing in various domains. However, the pruning and distillation techniques may affect the performance of the adaptive retrieval on more complex queries.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: End-to-End Optimized Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Modify the hybrid retrieval system to jointly optimize the weights of both the ColPali-based retriever and the dense text retriever during training, using an end-to-end optimization framework that maximizes the retrieval performance on a specific evaluation metric (e.g., Rank-Biased Precision). This approach should enable the system to learn a more optimal trade-off between the two models' strengths and weaknesses.
CONTROLS: Compare against training the models separately and then combining their outputs, as well as using different evaluation metrics and optimization objectives.
COST: 40 GPU-hours (end-to-end training + hyperparameter search)
PREDICTION: The end-to-end optimization should lead to a more robust and accurate hybrid retrieval system, with significant improvements in retrieval performance. However, it may require careful tuning of the optimization hyperparameters and a large-scale training dataset to avoid overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Hybrid Retrieval

TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Query Expansion on Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We will investigate if augmenting a textual query with keyword extraction techniques improves the performance of a lightweight dense text retriever in a hybrid setting. This involves pre-processing the textual query before input to the dense text retriever, and evaluating its impact on the overall retrieval quality using F1-score and recall@k as metrics.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach against a baseline setup without query expansion, and varying levels of the weak text retriever's capacity to differentiate between relevant and irrelevant documents.
COST: Estimated GPU hours: 200
PREDICTION: We expect query expansion to narrow the performance gap between the weak and strong retrievers, improving the overall retrieval quality of the hybrid system, especially for longer queries with few textual keywords, but possibly degrading precision for short, highly relevant queries.

TITLE: Assessing Architecture-Agnostic Aggregation Methods
PROPOSAL: We examine three unsupervised, architecture-agnostic aggregation methods for combining query-document similarity scores across different retrievers in a hybrid system: element-wise addition, element-wise multiplication, and learnable normalization. We investigate how these methods interact with varying levels of heterogeneity in the representation spaces and response distributions of the retrievers, focusing on how well they adapt to decreases and increases in the capacity of the weak retriever.
CONTROLS: We compare our proposed methods against a simple weighted sum baseline, and against aggregations that rely on re-ranking or quadratic programming, as well as against an oracle baseline that knows the parameters of the individual retrievers.
COST: Estimated GPU hours: 250
PREDICTION: Element-wise addition and learnable normalization methods show promising results and exhibit competitive or superior performance to the weighted sum baseline, particularly in scenarios where the weak retriever has a distinct but not negligible impact on overall retrieval quality.

PROPOSAL 6: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Knowledge Distillation for Lightweight Dense Text Retriever
We explore the use of knowledge distillation to reduce the capacity of the dense text retriever, aiming to improve the overall efficiency of the hybrid system. This involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained teacher model, and evaluating the performance of the distilled retriever in the hybrid setting.
Controls: We compare the performance of the distilled retriever against the original weak text retriever and against a baseline of comparable complexity, and also evaluate the impact of the distillation ratio and number of distillation epochs on the performance of the hybrid system.

Prediction: Knowledge distillation can effectively reduce the capacity of the dense text retriever without compromising its performance, leading to improved overall efficiency of the hybrid system, while also reducing the potential for overfitting.

PROPOSAL 7: Ablation Study for the Hybrid Retrieval System
We conduct an ablation study to understand the contribution of each component in our hybrid retrieval system. Specifically, we remove one component at a time and evaluate the impact on the overall performance of the system. Controls: We remove each of the following components: query expansion, representation interpolation, weak text retriever, and knowledge distillation, and evaluate the performance of the system in each case.
Estimated cost: Estimated GPU hours: 480
Prediction: Our ablation study reveals that the weak text retriever and representation interpolation are the most critical components of the hybrid system, and that removing them significantly degrades the overall performance. In contrast, the query expansion and knowledge distillation have a smaller impact, but are still valuable components of the system.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Gradient-Free Q-Value Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will implement and compare several gradient-free methods for maximizing the Q-function in continuous action spaces, including but not limited to: the cross-entropy method, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm. These methods will be tested on high-dimensional synthetic datasets and compared in terms of their efficiency, accuracy, and stability.
CONTROLS: Baseline will be a simple grid search over the action space, which will be used to estimate the optimal action; throughput will be compared with standard actor-critic methods (SAC, TD3) which will be implemented with-default parameters.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: These gradient-free methods should provide more accurate and robust optimization than simple grid search, but may struggle with high-dimensional action spaces and may not outperform traditional actor-critic methods; SA may be more prone to getting stuck in local optima.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating Gradient-Free Q-Value Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will extend the previous proposal by incorporating a Radial Basis Function (RBF) neural network as the Q-function approximator. The RBF network will be used to approximate the Q-function and the gradient-free optimization method (cross-entropy method or PSO) will be used to find the maximizing action. This combination should allow for faster and more accurate optimization, as well as better handling of complex Q-functions.
CONTROLS: In addition to the previous baseline (grid search), we will also add a control that uses the same RBF network but with a traditional gradient-based optimization (Fireworks Algorithm or Adam optimizer), to compare the performance of gradient-free and gradient-based optimization methods.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The combination of RBF network and gradient-free optimization should improve the accuracy and stability of the Q-function maximization, and outperform traditional actor-critic methods, especially in high-dimensional action spaces. However, gradient-based optimization may still perform better in certain cases, especially when the Q-function is smooth and convex.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Regularizing Q-Value Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will propose and investigate several regularizers that can be added to the gradient-free Q-value maximization method to promote more globally optimal solutions, such as: a Gaussian prior on the action space, a standard normal distribution mixture model, or a Laplacian noise kernel. These regularizers will be tested on synthetically generated high-dimensional action spaces and their impact on the optimization performance will be evaluated.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be the previous iteration (RBF network + gradient-free optimization), and we will compare with the same RBF network but with a traditional gradient-based optimization and no regularizer.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The regularizers should help to avoid local optima and lead to more globally optimal solutions, especially in high-dimensional action spaces. However, the optimal hyperparameters for the regularizers are not yet determined, and over-regularization may lead to under-fitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Quantum-Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Q-Value Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will explore the application of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) to the Q-value maximization problem. QAOA is a classical-quantum hybrid algorithm that leverages the power of near-term quantum computing to perform efficient optimization on classical problems. We will implement and test QAOA on synthetic high-dimensional action spaces and compare its performance with the previous gradient-free methods and standard actor-critic methods.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be the previous iteration (regularized RBF network + gradient-free optimization), and we will compare with the same RBF network but with a traditional gradient-based optimization.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (with classical-quantum interface)
PREDICTION: QAOA may significantly outperform traditional gradient-based optimization methods in high-dimensional action spaces, but its performance may degrade in the presence of noise or irregularities in the Q-function. Moreover, the implementation of QAOA will require significant computational resources, including a quantum-classical interface.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Robustness of Gradient-Free Q-Value Maximization to Hyperparameter Scares
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the robustness of the gradient-free Q-value maximization methods (including the proposed regularized RBF network and QAOA) to hyperparameter variations and explore techniques to improve their robustness. This includes sensitivity analysis, automatic hyperparameter tuning using Bayesian optimization or randomized search, and the use of hyperparameter ensembling.
CONTROLS: We will compare the robustness of the gradient-free methods with traditional actor-critic methods (SAC, TD3) which are known to be sensitive to hyperparameters.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Gradient-free methods may be more sensitive to hyperparameters than traditional actor-critic methods, but the regularizers and QAOA may improve their robustness. However, the hyperparameter search space will need to be carefully designed to avoid over-regularization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Use of Multi-Resolution Representations for Gradient-Free Q-Value Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of multi-resolution representations, such as wavelettransforms or deep autoencoders, to improve the efficiency and accuracy of the gradient-free Q-value maximization methods. These representations can capture local and global structures in the Q-function, facilitating the discovery of optimal actions.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the multi-resolution representations with the previous gradient-free methods (regularized RBF network and QAOA) and standard actor-critic methods (SAC, TD3).
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Multi-resolution representations may provide a significant boost to the performance of the gradient-free Q-value maximization methods, allowing them to overcome the curse of dimensionality and efficiently explore high-dimensional action spaces. However, the tuning of the representation architecture may require significant computational resources.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Efficient Quantum-Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Q-Value Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will revise the implementation of QAOA to incorporate the multi-resolution representation (wavelet transforms or deep autoencoders) developed in proposal 5. This will allow the QAOA algorithm to leverages the power of near-term quantum computing in combination with the efficient representations of the Q-function. We will test the revised QAOA algorithm on high-dimensional synthetic action spaces.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the revised QAOA with the regularized RBF network, traditional gradient-based optimization, and actor-critic methods (SAC, TD3).
COST: 250 GPU-hours (with classical-quantum interface)
PREDICTION: The revised QAOA algorithm may achieve state-of-the-art performance in high-dimensional action spaces, but the implementation will require careful tuning of the quantum-classical interface and encoding schemes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direct Value-Based Policy Search using Model-Free Optimization
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate a direct value-based policy search method that uses model-free optimization to search for the optimal policy in continuous action spaces. The method will utilize techniques from model-free reinforcement learning, such as Q-learning and policy iteration, and we will leverage the results from previous proposals to improve the efficiency and accuracy of the policy search.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the direct value-based policy search method with the previous gradient-free methods (regularized RBF network and QAOA) and actor-critic methods (SAC, TD3).
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The direct value-based policy search method may provide a more efficient and accurate way to search for the optimal policy in continuous action spaces, but the method may require significant hyperparameter tuning and may be prone to local optima.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Gradient-Free Q-Value Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will develop a meta-learning approach to improve the performance of the gradient-free Q-value maximization methods on various tasks and environments. The meta-learning approach will use a base model to learn a set of high-level features that can be transferred to new tasks, and a meta-model to adjust the parameters of the base model for each new task. We will use the results from previous proposals to select the best gradient-free Q-value maximization method and adapt it for use with the meta-learning approach.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the meta-learning approach with the previous gradient-free methods (regularized RBF network and QAOA) and actor-critic methods (SAC, TD3) on various tasks and environments.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The meta-learning approach may provide a significant boost to the performance of gradient-free Q-value maximization methods by adapting to new tasks and environments, but the meta-model can be computationally expensive to train and may require significant hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Comparison and Analysis of Gradient-Free Methods for Q-Value Maximization
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a comprehensive comparison and analysis of the gradient-free methods developed in previous proposals (1-7) to identify the strengths and weaknesses of each approach. We will also investigate the covariates for each method's performance, including task characteristics, environment complexity, and hyperparameter tuning.
CONTROLS: All previous proposals will be evaluated and compared across a common set of metrics, including policy performance, stability, and efficiency.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This comprehensive comparison and analysis will provide valuable insights into the performance of gradient-free methods for Q-value maximization and help to identify the most suitable approach for different tasks and environments.

TITLE: Analyzing the Effect of Q-Function Capacity on Actor-Free RL in Continuous Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: Investigate how the capacity of the Q-function affects the ability of an actor-free, value-based RL algorithm to maximize over continuous actions. We will use a DQN-like model with a radial basis function output layer as the Q-function and explore its performance on continuous action spaces with different numbers of dimensions (2, 5, and 10).
CONTROLS: Compare to a standard DQN algorithm with a discrete action space equivalent and a discretized version of the same Q-function for continuous action spaces.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Increasing Q-function capacity will allow the algorithm to solve more complex tasks, but may also lead to overfitting and difficulties in policy initialization, especially in high-dimensional action spaces. We expect the algorithm to perform competitively with DQN in 2D and 5D action spaces, but may struggle in 10D due to overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Exploration Strategies on Actor-Free RL inContinuous Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: Investigate different exploration strategies for actor-free, value-based RL in continuous action spaces. We will implement epsilon-greedy, noise injection, and entropy regularization methods and evaluate their performance on a set of continuous control tasks using the same DQN-like model with a radial basis function output layer as the Q-function.
CONTROLS: Compare to a standard DQN algorithm with a discrete action space equivalent and to the base algorithm without any exploration strategy.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Noise injection and entropy regularization methods will be more effective than epsilon-greedy in high-dimensional action spaces, while epsilon-greedy may perform better in low-dimensional action spaces where the Q-function can be reasonably approximated. We expect all methods to outperform the base algorithm, but may see some instability with noise injection.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Action Maximization in Continuous Q-Learning
PROPOSAL: Implement a second-order gradient descent method combined with a sparse polynomial approximation to efficiently maximize the Q-function in continuous action spaces. In this approach, we iteratively construct a sparsely connected polynomial approximation of the Q-function's Hessian matrix. This approximation is used to obtain a differentiable lower bound of the Q-function's maximizer, which can be efficiently searched using gradient descent.
CONTROLS: Compare with established actor-critic methods such as DDPG and TD3 on MuJoCo benchmark tasks.
COST: 1,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method can improve the performance of existing value-based algorithms in high-dimensional continuous action spaces while maintaining simplicity and stability. However, the efficacy of the approach depends on the choice of the polynomial degree, and high-degree approximations may introduce unrealistic assumptions about the complexity of the Q-function.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Safe and Efficient Optimization of Constrained Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: Develop a variant of the sparse polynomial approximation method in experiment 1 that explicitly accounts for safety constraints in the action space. This is achieved by reformulating the constrained problem as an unconstrained one by incorporating penalty terms for the constraint violations into the objective function. An iterative procedure is used to adjust the coefficients of the polynomial approximation and maintain feasibility.
CONTROLS: Compare with methods that use Lagrange multipliers or other constraint enforcement techniques on the original problem in experiment 1, on MuJoCo tasks and constrained versions of them.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach can effectively handle safety constraints in the action space without incurring significant computational overhead. However, the selection of the penalty coefficients may require careful tuning, and the method's efficiency may degrade in cases where the constraints are highly nonlinear or have multiple local minima.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Efficient Action Maximization in Continuous Q-Learning
PROPOSAL: In addition to the previous traits, incorporate greedy search within the gradient descent space as a means to efficiently sample regions of the action space and improve convergence, as higher-order gradients of the Q-function may not be necessary.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline sparse polynomial approximation from REVISE 1 on MuJoCo tasks, and a variant that combines both sparse and greedy search, to see if this inclusion can break the dependency on polynomial degree for performance.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised approach can identify optimal actions more efficiently by reducing reliance on the polynomial approximation and better handling complex landscapes without increasing the computational cost for large degrees.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Efficient Action Maximization in Continuous Q-Learning
PROPOSAL: REVISE 1: Improve the convergence and efficiency of the sparse polynomial approximation method by incorporating a line search strategy, such as the Armijo rule, to adaptively determine the step size used in gradient descent. This will help ensure that the gradient descent steps are effectively optimized for the specific Q-function being maximized.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the revised sparse polynomial approximation with and without the line search strategy on a variety of MuJoCo tasks, evaluating the effect on convergence speed and quality of the found optima.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The incorporation of the line search strategy can significantly improve the performance and efficiency of the sparse polynomial approximation method by avoiding overshooting and reducing the risk of convergence to local optima. However, the choice of line search parameters may require careful tuning, and the approach may not generalize to very high-dimensional or highly nonlinear Q-functions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Hyperparameter Tuning for Value-Based Methods
PROPOSAL: Develop a methodology that uses a surrogate-based optimization technique, such as the Efficient Global Optimization (EGO) algorithm, to tune the hyperparameters of value-based methods, including the sparse polynomial approximation and its variants. This will allow the hyperparameters to be learned automatically and efficiently, without requiring significant manual tuning or expertise.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the hyperparameter-tuned algorithms with their manually tuned counterparts on MuJoCo tasks, evaluating the effect on convergence speed and quality of the found optima.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach can reduce the overhead of hyperparameter tuning for value-based methods and improve their performance across a range of tasks. However, the efficiency of the EGO algorithm may degrade in cases where the hyperparameter space is highly nonlinear or multi-modal.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Safe and Efficient Optimization of Constrained Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: REVISE 2: Modify the constraint enforcement term in the objective function to be Amphible, by solving for all the constraints and then evaluating the objective function at all equality and inequality constraints boundaries, giving us the constrained optimal value(s) with respect to the objective.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the revised safe optimization method with and without the Amphible term on MuJoCo tasks, evaluating the effect on accuracy and convergence speed of the found optimal actions, using tasks with and without complex constraints.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised method can effectively handle complex constraints by finding the optimal actions that respect the boundaries of the constraints. However, the computational cost of the revised method may be higher due to the additional optimization steps required to solve for the constraints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Actor-Free Q-Learning with Adaptive Model Resolution
PROPOSAL: Develop a method that adaptively refines or coarsens the resolution of the Q-function's action space during optimization, based on the proximity of the current action to the task's optimal action. This will enable more efficient exploration of the action space and better exploit known regions of the optimal action.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the adaptive model resolution Q-learning method with established actor-critic methods and the original Q-learning method on MuJoCo tasks, evaluating the effect on convergence speed and quality of the found optimal actions.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The adaptive model resolution method can improve the efficiency and effectiveness of Q-learning by adaptively focusing on areas of the action space that are likely to contain the optimal action. However, the method's performance may degrade in tasks with highly non-uniform optimal actions or in scenarios where the action space is characterized by outliers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Actor-Free Q-Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop a method that enables transfer learning for actor-free Q-learning by adapting a pre-trained Q-function to a new task with possibly different action space, reward function, or dynamics. This will allow for more efficient adaptation to new tasks and enable Q-learning to generalize across a variety of tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the transfer learning Q-learning method with standard Q-learning and actor-free Q-learning methods on a suite of MuJoCo tasks, evaluating the effect on convergence speed and quality of the found optimal actions.
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The transfer learning method can significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of Q-learning by leveraging pre-trained knowledge to adapt to new tasks. However, the performance of the method may degrade if the pre-trained Q-function is not well-suited to the new task or if the adaptation process is not properly configured.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable Ensemble Methods for High-Dimensional Q-Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop a method that uses ensemble learning to combine the predictions of multiple Q-functions optimized for different aspects of the Q-learning problem, such as value estimation, action search, and constraint satisfaction. This will enable scalable and robust Q-learning in high-dimensional action spaces.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the ensemble Q-learning method with standard Q-learning and actor-free Q-learning methods on MuJoCo tasks with large action spaces, evaluating the effect on convergence speed and quality of the found optimal actions.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The ensemble learning method can improve the scalability and robustness of Q-learning in high-dimensional action spaces by leveraging the strengths of multiple Q-functions. However, the performance of the method may degrade if the Q-functions in the ensemble conflicts with each other, and careful selection and combination of Q-functions is required to achieve optimal performance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Efficient Action Maximization in Continuous Q-Learning
PROPOSAL: REVISE 2: Integrate the insights and components from the various methods developed in this research (sparse polynomial approximation, line search, adaptation, transfer learning, and ensemble methods) into a complete and efficient actor-free Q-learning framework. This will provide a comprehensive and robust approach to Q-learning in continuous action spaces.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the integrated Q-learning framework with existing state-of-the-art methods on a set of challenging MuJoCo tasks, evaluating the effect on convergence speed, quality of the found optimal actions, and adaptability to different tasks.
COST: (estimated total cost of the previous experiments, approximately 4000 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: The revised and integrated Q-learning framework can achieve state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of tasks and provide a solid foundation for future research in actor-free Q-learning.

TITLE: Evaluating Masked Language Modeling for Zero-Shot Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL: Utilize a frozen, large-scale language model (e.g., CLIP or T5) for zero-shot step grounding, where the model's masked language modeling capacity is leveraged to "complete" the procedural step description given the video segment. TITLE: Unsupervised Online Step Grounding via Imitation Learning
PROPOSAL: Introduce an unsupervised step grounding framework based on imitation learning, where the model learns to imitate the behavior of a pre-trained model or a human operator in real-time, without any labeled data. This is achieved by encoding the procedural steps using a sequence-to-sequence model and then fine-tuning the model to predict the next step based on the current hidden state of the encoder. The framework is evaluated on a series of tasks where the model learns to mimic the behavior of a human operator or a pre-trained model in real-time.
CONTROLS: (1) a supervised step grounding baseline, (2) an offline imitation learning model without real-time updates, and (3) an ablation study on the choice of discriminator and reward function.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected to perform well in unsupervised settings and adapt to real-time changes in a dynamic environment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Attention-Based Curriculum Learning for Zero-Shot Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL: Develop an attention-based curriculum learning approach to learn to focus on the most relevant parts of the procedural step description for zero-shot video step grounding. The model learns to selectively attend to the most informative parts of the step description by using an attention mechanism that is trained to focus on the steps that are most relevant to the current video segment. This learned attention mechanism is then used to prioritize the retrieval of relevant steps from the memory-based model.
CONTROLS: (1) a baseline model without attention-based curriculum learning, (2) a model with attention-based curriculum learning but without dynamic segment selection, and (3) an ablation study on the choice of attention mechanism and curriculum learning strategy.
COST: 350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected to improve the model's ability to focus on the most relevant parts of the step description and improve overall performance, but faces challenges in adapting to new tasks and steps without fine-tuning.

TITLE: Ensembling Multiple Modalities for Zero-Shot Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of ensemble methods to combine the predictions of multiple modalities for zero-shot video step grounding. The proposed ensemble method would involve training multiple models on different modalities (e.g., text, vision, audio) and then ensemble their predictions to generate a final prediction. This approach aims to leverage the strengths of each modality and improve the overall performance of the system.
CONTROLS: (1) a baseline model using a single modality, (2) a model using a previously proposed fusion method, and (3) an ablation study on the choice of ensemble method and modalities.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected to outperform previous state-of-the-art results, but may face challenges in properly calibrating the weights of the individual models in the ensemble.

propositions.texte: Design a hierarchical cascade of predictors for each video segment, addressing the segment-specific challenge and task-related aspects. Initially, a coarse-level predictor identifies whether the segment is likely to correspond to a step. If affirmative, a second-nested predictor refines the step identification by considering more detailed contextual cues from the segment and the existing step description library. This unified cascade model is optimized with a segment-level cross-validation objective.
propositions.titre: Segment-Level Predictive Cascades for Online Video Step Grounding

propositions.texte: Employ a retrieval-based step grounding system to leverage a pre-learned memory of past steps from a large, dedicated dataset, and then use online knowledge distillation to efficiently transfer knowledge from this memory to the currently processed video segment. This retrieval engine consequently refines its retrieval and grounding performance by harnessing data from real videos, requiring not additional scene annotations, adapting gradually but steadily augment outputs.
propositions.titre: Retrieval-Augmented Online Step Grounding with Knowledge Distillation

propositions.controles: (1) a supervised step grounding baseline, (2) an offline imitation learning model without real-time updates, and (3) an ablation study on the choice of discriminator and reward function.
propositions.prediction: Expected to perform well in unsupervised settings and adapt to real-time changes in a dynamic environment.
propositions.texte: Introduce an unsupervised step grounding framework based on imitation learning, where the model learns to imitate the behavior of a pre-trained model or a human operator in real-time, without any labeled data. This is achieved by encoding the procedural steps using a sequence-to-sequence model and then fine-tuning the model to predict the next step based on the current hidden state of the encoder. The framework is evaluated on a series of tasks where the model learns to mimic the behavior of a human operator or a pre-trained model in real-time.
propositions.titre: Unsupervised Online Step Grounding via Imitation Learning

propositions.controles: (1) a baseline model without attention-based curriculum learning, (2) a model with attention-based curriculum learning but without dynamic segment selection, and (3) an ablation study on the choice of attention mechanism and curriculum learning strategy.
propositions.prediction: Expected to improve the model's ability to focus on the most relevant parts of the step description and improve overall performance, but faces challenges in adapting to new tasks and steps without fine-tuning.
propositions.texte: Develop an attention-based curriculum learning approach to learn to focus on the most relevant parts of the procedural step description for zero-shot video step grounding. The model learns to selectively attend to the most informative parts of the step description by using an attention mechanism that is trained to focus on the steps that are most relevant to the current video segment. This learned attention mechanism is then used to prioritize the retrieval of relevant steps from the memory-based model.
propositions.titre: Attention-Based Curriculum Learning for Zero-Shot Video Step Grounding

propositions.controles: (1) a baseline model using a single modality, (2) a model using a previously proposed fusion method, and (3) an ablation study on the choice of ensemble method and modalities.
propositions.prediction: Expected to outperform previous state-of-the-art results, but may face challenges in properly calibrating the weights of the individual models in the ensemble.
propositions.texte: Explore the use of ensemble methods to combine the predictions of multiple modalities for zero-shot video step grounding. The proposed ensemble method would involve training multiple models on different modalities (e.g., text, vision, audio) and then ensemble their predictions to generate a final prediction. This approach aims to leverage the strengths of each modality and improve the overall performance of the system.
propositions.titre: Ensembling Multiple Modalities for Zero-Shot Video Step Grounding

TITLE: 2. Investigating the Role of Short-Range Temporal Context in Online Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL: Investigate the upper limit of the effectiveness of short-range temporal context for online video step grounding and its transferability between different tasks and datasets (e.g., robotic assembly, cooking recipes). We hypothesize that the benefits of short-range temporal context diminish when its duration exceeds a certain threshold, leading to diminishing returns. Furthermore, we aim to evaluate how such threshold varies across different instructional domains.

CONTROLS: Compare against varying temporal context lengths on a range of instructional tasks, analyze transferability to unseen tasks and datasets, and ablate the temporal context to evaluate its necessity.

COST: 100 GPU-hours

PREDICTION: The performance gains from short-range temporal context will exhibit a rapid decline as the duration increases beyond a certain threshold, and its benefits show promising transferability towards tasks and datasets with comparable cognitive difficulty while tasks, such as the anomaly detection, will be quite correlated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Temporal Structure on Online Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL: Investigate the influence of explicit temporal structure on online video step grounding, by analyzing and modeling a priori knowledge of typical task structures and durations, even if the exact starting point is not known in advance, to improve the accuracy and robustness of VSG models. We will evaluate this approach on a comprehensive set of instructional videos with well-defined temporal structures.

CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline model without knowledge of temporal structure, and ablate the use of explicit temporal knowledge to evaluate its necessity; we also compare against a model that learns temporal structure from the video data.

COST: 300 GPU-hours

PREDICTION: The explicit temporal structure can improve the accuracy of VSG by up to 20%, especially for videos with well-defined temporal structures, while a model learning the temporal structure will be slightly less effective but still improve the accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Multi-Task Learning for Zero-Shot Video Step Grounding
PROPOSAL: Investigate the benefits of online multi-task learning (MTL) for zero-shot video step grounding, where multiple tasks are learned simultaneously from the same instructional video stream, and evaluate its impact on grounding performance and adaptability. We will incorporate multiple VSG tasks (e.g., cooking recipes, robotic assembly) and analyze the effect of the different tasks on each other.

CONTROLS: Compare against a single-task learning baseline and ablate the individual tasks to evaluate their contributions to the overall grounding performance; we will also analyze the effect of task relationships on grounding performance.

COST: 400 GPU-hours

PREDICTION: Online MTL will show improved grounding accuracy and adaptability for zero-shot VSG, particularly when learning multiple related tasks; however, it may incur higher computational costs and require careful hyperparameter tuning to avoid overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Transfer Learning for Video Step Grounding with Instructional Pre-Training
PROPOSAL: Explore online transfer learning for video step grounding by pre-training a model on a large corpus of instructional videos without prior knowledge of specific tasks, and then fine-tuning it on a new task as video segments arrive. We will evaluate the effectiveness of this approach on a diverse set of instructional tasks and datasets.

CONTROLS: Compare against a task-specific fine-tuning baseline and ablate the pre-training phase to evaluate its necessity; we will also analyze the effect of pre-training on adaptability and generalization to new tasks.

COST: 500 GPU-hours

PREDICTION: Online transfer learning will show improved adaptability and generalization for video step grounding, especially when pre-trained on a diverse corpus of instructional videos; however, it may require careful tuning of the pre-training and fine-tuning hyperparameters to achieve optimal performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Online Video Step Grounding with Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop an uncertainty-aware online video step grounding system that leverages transfer learning and estimate uncertainty in the model's predictions as video segments arrive. We will use a Bayesian neural network framework to model uncertainty and evaluate its impact on grounding performance and robustness.

CONTROLS: Compare against a deterministic baseline and ablate the use of uncertainty estimation to evaluate its necessity; we will also analyze the effect of uncertainty estimation on adaptability and generalization to new tasks.

COST: 700 GPU-hours

PREDICTION: Uncertainty-aware online video step grounding will show improved robustness and adaptability, especially when uncertainty estimation is integrated with transfer learning; however, it may incur higher computational costs and require careful tuning of the uncertainty estimation hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Towards Real-World Video Step Grounding: An Evaluation of Proposed Methods on Egocentric Procedural Activity Videos
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the proposed online video step grounding methods on a large-scale, real-world dataset of egocentric procedural activity videos (e.g., cooking, assembly tasks), and assess their performance in terms of grounding accuracy, robustness, and adaptability.

CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed methods on the real-world dataset against the results obtained on simulated datasets, and analyze the impact of factors such as video quality, task complexity, and user variability on grounding performance.

COST: 1,000 GPU-hours

PREDICTION: The proposed online video step grounding methods will show improved robustness and adaptability when evaluated on real-world egocentric procedural activity videos, especially when uncertainty-aware techniques are combined with transfer learning; however, there may be a trade-off between grounding accuracy and robustness due to the complexities of real-world data.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bounding the Computational Overheads of Pairformer Recycling and Iterative Denoising
PROPOSAL: Derive theoretical bounds on the computational complexity of Pairformer recycling and the iterative denoising process in AlphaFold3, as a function of sequence length and the number of recycling iterations. Specifically, we will analyze the computational cost associated with each step of the recycling process, as well as the aggregated cost over multiple iterations. We will also explore the relationship between the number of recycling iterations and the resulting predictive accuracy, to better understand the tradeoff between efficiency and performance.
CONTROLS: Compare our bounds to the actual computational cost measured for AlphaFold3 on various sequences and sequence lengths.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The derived bounds will provide a clear understanding of the efficient computation overheads of Pairformer recycling and iterative denoising, and will likely reveal a strong correlation between the number of recycling iterations and the resulting predictive accuracy. A major challenge in deriving these bounds will lie in handling the interactions between multiple recycling iterations and the diffusion sampling process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Pairformer Recycling with Keystone Sampling
PROPOSAL: Modify the recycling process in AlphaFold3 by incorporating a keystone sampling strategy, which randomly selects a subset of positions in the protein sequence to be recycled, rather than recycling the entire sequence. We will investigate how the number of selected positions affects the accuracy and efficiency of the prediction, and whether this approach can be used to reduce the computational overhead of recycling while maintaining predictive performance.
CONTROLS: Compare keystone sampling to standard recycling; perform ablation studies on the selection strategy (e.g., random, importance-based).
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Keystone sampling may significantly reduce the computational cost of recycling while preserving predictive accuracy, particularly for longer sequences. A challenge will be to determine the optimal selection strategy, balancing accuracy with efficiency.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Efficient Pairformer Recycling with Keystone Sampling
PROPOSAL: We modify the recycling process in AlphaFold3 by incorporating a keystone sampling strategy, which randomly selects a subset of contiguous positions in the protein sequence to be recycled. TITLE: Simplified AlphaFold3 Truncation Experiments
PROPOSAL: Compare truncations of the iterative diffusion solver, recycling cycle, and Pairformer recycling, with the reverse setup used as a baseline (i.e., the full iterative model). Specifically, we will try pairformer-only (no recycling), recycling with a fixed, very short diffusion sequence (not iterated), and fixed 1-step diffusion using analytical relaxation instead of until-denoising.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Consistency Scheduling for AlphaFold3 Across Sequence Lengths
PROPOSAL: Investigate variant consistency schedules that efficiently adjust step sizes to the length of the input sequence, addressing the challenges of distribution shifts on long sequences and weak learning signals on short sequences. We will design schedules that scale the consistency coefficients based on sequence length, using beta functions or similar to smoothly adjust step sizes and ensure stability across sequence lengths.
CONTROLS: Baseline will be standard consistency scheduling. We will also use simplified truncation setups (Proposal 1) with variant schedules to isolate their impact.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By adapting consistency schedules to sequence length, we expect to achieve more stable and effective training on diverse protein sequence lengths, thereby improving overall model robustness. The most challenging part may be tuning the new schedules effectively, as poor tweaking can collapse the training rather than stabilizing it.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED Consistency Scheduling for AlphaFold3 Across Sequence Lengths
PROPOSAL: Implement adaptive step-size scaling based on the history of step sizes that worked before, using an experience replay buffer to cache successful step sizes and gradually forgetting unsuccessful ones, effectively adapting to sequence length complexity in real-time.
CONTROLS: Baseline remains standard consistency scheduling. We will also compare with the revised beta-function based scaling proposed in our previous version.
COST: 45 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised adaptive step-size scaling strategy should further stabilize and improve training effectiveness. However, tuning the adaptation rate and buffer size can be tricky, and increased adaptivity might generate "short-circuit" behaviors for certain tasks on short sequences, potentially hindering gradient backpropagation in design settings.

TITLE: Baseline Establishment for AlphaFold3
PROPOSAL: Benchmark AlphaFold3's performance on a comprehensive set of protein structure prediction, protein-ligand complex structure prediction, protein binder design, and virtual screening for drug discovery tasks using standard metrics (e.g., RMSD, PSSM similarity, diffuse correlation). CONTROLS: Use released versions of AlphaFold3 and compare against its original iteration count.

 Reasoning: Before attempting to accelerate AlphaFold3, it is essential to establish a solid baseline of its original performance. By benchmarking AlphaFold3 on various tasks and datasets, we can gain insights into its strengths and weaknesses, providing a foundation for subsequent experiments that aim to reduce its computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Recycling Iterations
PROPOSAL: Systematically reduce the number of recycling iterations in AlphaFold3 and evaluate the effect on structural accuracy and computational efficiency. Utilize metrics like RMSD, PSSM similarity, and compare against the full iteration model.

COST: 200 GPU-hours

PREDICTION: By systematically studying the combined effect of recycling iterations and diffusion steps, we can identify potential strategies to accelerate AlphaFold3 while maintaining or improving its structural accuracy.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Differentiable Relaxation of Discrete Tokens for One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: We propose experimenting with a combination of soft-argmax and straight-through estimators to relax discrete tokens in the output of a one-step generator distilled from an MDM. Specifically, we will explore the usage of the soft-argmax operation to estimate the gradient of the log likelihood of the discrete token outputs during backwards pass, and the straight-through estimator to pass the expected token output through the non-differentiable sampling operation during the forwards pass. This will help to increase the gradient signal and reduce the effect of numerical instability during training.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with Gumbel-Softmax relaxation, REINFORCE policy gradient estimator, and teacher distillation alone.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: While the method is unlikely to correct the errors in the teacher and achieve state-of-the-art performance, it can stabilize training and allow for slight improvments in the student model's performance. It may fail to handle cases where the teacher's discrepancy with the target distribution is large.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Distillation Errors on One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: We propose conducting a quantitative analysis of how the errors in the teacher's generative modeling and alignment with downstream objectives affect the performance of the one-step generator distilled from the teacher. To do this, we will train multiple teachers with varying levels of quality and alignment with downstream objectives, and then distill one-step generators from each of them. We will evaluate the quality of the generated images on downstream tasks, such as image-to-image translation and captioning, and assess the importance of each teacher's error type on the performance of the distilled generator.
CONTROLS: We will control for the quality of the teacher by evaluating its distance to the true target distribution using metrics such as the Fréchet inception distance (FID). We will control for the alignment of the teacher with downstream objectives by evaluating its ability to respond to task-specific prompts.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our analysis will likely reveal that errors in the teacher's generative modeling and alignment with downstream objectives have a significant impact on the performance of the distilled one-step generator. We may find that methods to reduce these errors, such as adversarial training and fine-tuning, are necessary to achieve high-quality results. This may fail to reveal the relative importance of different teacher error types on the performance of the distilled generator.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Conditional Adversarial Training for One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: We propose adapting conditional adversarial training to work with the relaxed token outputs of a one-step generator distilled from an MDM. In this framework, we will train a discriminator to distinguish between real images and generated images produced by the one-step generator, and then use this discriminator to refine the generator's outputs. The key challenge will be to adapt the GAN loss to the discrete token outputs, and to ensure that the gradients flow through the existing generation pipeline.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with unconditional adversarial training, and with post-distillation fine-tuning using rewards and human-preference signals. We will also evaluate the effect of different discriminator architectures on the performance of the generator.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our method is likely to improve the quality of the generated images, particularly in terms of detail and realism. However, it may require careful tuning of the discriminator and generator losses to achieve good results. It may also struggle to recover the missing details in the teacher's outputs, if they are not properly distilled into the one-step generator.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Simplifying Conditional Adversarial Training for One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: We revise our proposal to simplify the conditioner architecture of the adversarial training framework. Instead of using a separate conditioner to transform the relaxed token outputs, we propose to use a projection layer to transform the token outputs into a continuous space, followed by a binary classification layer to predict the presence or absence of the corresponding real token. This simplification will reduce the computational cost of training and allow us to better explore the trade-off between generator training and discriminator training.
CONTROLS: We will compare our simplified method with the original conditional adversarial training proposal, as well as with unconditional adversarial training and post-distillation fine-tuning using rewards and human-preference signals. We will also evaluate the effect of different projection layer architectures on the performance of the generator.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our simplified method is likely to achieve similar results to the original conditional adversarial training proposal, with increased efficiency and flexibility. However, it may require careful tuning of the projection layer architecture to achieve good results. It may also struggle to recover the missing details in the teacher's outputs, if they are not properly distilled into the one-step generator.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Reward-Shaping for One-Step Generators with Human-Aware Training
PROPOSAL: We propose incorporating human-aware rewards to fine-tune the one-step generator, allowing it to learn from human preferences and improve its alignment with downstream objectives. We will leverage a reward model trained on human annotations to provide informative feedback to the generator, in the form of a reward signal that encourages or discourages specific output properties.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with post-distillation fine-tuning using rewards alone, without human-aware training. We will also evaluate the effect of different reward models and hyperparameters on the performance of the generator.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our method is likely to improve the generator's alignment with human preferences and downstream objectives, particularly in terms of prompt adherence and aesthetic quality. However, it may require careful tuning of the reward model and hyperparameters to achieve good results. It may also struggle to balance the reward signal with the generator's exploration-exploitation trade-off.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Multi-Stage Distillation for One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: We propose extending the distillation process to involve multiple stages, where the teacher is refined through self-supervised learning and distortion-minimization techniques, and then the one-step generator is distilled from the refined teacher. This will enable the generator to learn more accurately from high-quality representations and improve its quality and realism.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with the original teacher distillation setup, as well as with other multi-stage distillation schemes that involve multiple students or teachers. We will also evaluate the effect of different self-supervision tasks and distortion-minimization techniques on the performance of the generator.
COST: 280 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our method is likely to improve the quality and realism of the generated images, particularly in terms of detail and texture. However, it may require careful tuning of the self-supervision tasks and distortion-minimization techniques to achieve good results. It may also struggle to balance the trade-off between self-supervision quality and generator training complexity.

ACTION: ADD 6

We propose experimenting with a combination of soft-argmax and straight-through estimators to relax discrete tokens in the output of a one-step generator distilled from an MDM. Specifically, we will explore the usage of the soft-argmax operation to estimate the gradient of the log likelihood of the discrete token outputs during backwards pass, and the straight-through estimator to pass the expected token output through the non-differentiable sampling operation during the forwards pass. This will help to increase the gradient signal and reduce the effect of numerical instability during training.

PROPOSAL 2: Evaluating the Impact of Distillation Errors on One-Step Generators
We propose conducting a quantitative analysis of how the errors in the teacher's generative modeling and alignment with downstream objectives affect the performance of the one-step generator distilled from the teacher. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Harnessing Differentiable Rewards for One-Step Discrete Generators
PROPOSAL: Investigate the application of differentiable relaxations of discrete tokens, such as Gumbel-Softmax, to one-step discrete generators. To this end, study the Gumbel-Softmax estimator for differentiable adversarial training and its interaction with downstream reward and discriminator models. Specifically, explore the role of the temperature parameter in controlling both the informativeness of the relaxation and its gradient stability, evaluating this using corpus and image-based benchmarks. Utilize state-of-the-art models, such as the DDPM variant, to assess the potential for this approach to correct the limitations inherited from the teacher model.
CONTROLS: Compare Gumbel-Softmax against a baseline soft-argmax estimator, and against ground-truth discretized samples. A key control experiment is the Fisher information approximation to understand the amount of gradient variance introduced by the relaxations.
COST: 1,200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Differentiable relaxations can be employed to stabilize gradients in the loss function but could require careful tuning of hyperparameters (e.g., temperature) to achieve a good balance between informativeness and high variance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient Unblocking for Discrete Generators
PROPOSAL: Investigate techniques to repair the gradient-blocking issue caused by discrete outputs. Focus on reparameterization methods that directly enable gradients to flow from the generator to the full, differentiable pipeline. Two promising approaches are Locally Compositional Likelihood Ratios (Rodriguez and Blanchard 2021) and gradient backflow (Locatello et al. 2020). These methods reparameterize the generation process as a sequence of continuous random variables and then introduce noise to break deterministic connections. Study whether these modifications can retain model performance while providing unblocked gradients for downstream tasks like GAN training.
CONTROLS: Evaluate against a reference decomposition of discrete distributions that relies on a set of continuous intermediate variables, using a standard set of image and text benchmarks and a simple one-step generator as the teacher model.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Success with one of the proposed techniques could require careful tuning and further investigation is needed to understand its effects and limitations.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: 
REVISED: Harnessing Differentiable Rewards for One-Step Discrete Generators
PROPOSAL: Extend the previous proposal to a controlled comparison between differentiable relaxations (e.g., Gumbel-Softmax and soft-argmax) and reparameterizations that enable backflow of gradients (e.g., Locally Compositional Likelihood Ratios and gradient backflow). This is necessary to better understand the trade-offs between informativeness and gradient stability for different relaxations, as well as the effects of these techniques on performance in downstream tasks. Utilize a larger range of benchmarks, including text and image datasets and, most importantly, one-step generators of differing complexities that are distilled from a broad set of teacher models.
CONTROLS: Expand the control experiments to include the existing differentiable relaxations, reparameterization alternatives without backflow (imposing the differentiability requirement in alternative manners), and the teacher models corresponding to each student generator. 
COST: 2,000 GPU-hours (this requires a deeper exploration)
PREDICTION: Direct comparison of the reparationizations may reveal their varying needs for geological tweaks (separate evaluations for student model diminishment, explorations relying to simult recent interventions in aligned representations).

TITLE: Data-Separate Optimization for Teacher-Student Alignment
PROPOSAL: Study the effectiveness of a two-stage optimization strategy that separates teacher and student model adjustments, improving student alignment with downstream objectives. This involves first updating the teacher model with data, then using the teacher's pre-trained student distillation to improve the alignment of the student generator with downstream preferences. Specifically, explore this method with respect to visual qualitative measures, obtained from discriminator and reward models, and quantitative measures, such as Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for GANs and Distributional Wasserstein metric for distillation.

PROPOSAL: Investigate a hierarchical learning strategy that combines the strengths of the above proposals. The approach involves training a teacher model to a high level of performance, then using the teacher to pre-train a student model, and finally fine-tuning the student using the data-separate optimization strategy and the probabilistic relaxation of the teacher-student alignment objective. PROPOSAL 3: Data-Separate Optimization for Teacher-Student Alignment
Study the effectiveness of a two-stage optimization strategy that separates teacher and student model adjustments, improving student alignment with downstream objectives. actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient Propagation for Discrete Generators through Approximate Reversal of the Masking Process
PROPOSAL: We propose a gradient propagation scheme that employs a novel approximation of the reverse masking process to enable end-to-end training of one-step discrete generators. Specifically, we model the teacher's output as a discrete distribution over the token vocabulary, and then approximate the reverse masking process as a series of random walks on a graph representing the token dependencies. We then use gradient back-propagation to compute the gradients of the loss with respect to the generator's input, bypassing the non-differentiable sampling operation in the teacher.
CONTROLS: Compare with the existing student-teacher distillation approach with on-policy distribution matching and with a baseline of direct adversary training on discrete targets using a policy-gradient estimator (e.g. REINFORCE).
COST: 10 GPU-hours (approximate, and sufficient to train a single model per condition).
PREDICTION: This approach should enable end-to-end training of the one-step generator, but may require careful tuning of the approximation quality to avoid over-smoothing or under-regularization of the gradients.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analysis of Gradient Instability in Discrete Models
PROPOSAL: We theoretically analyze the conditions under which gradient propagation in discrete models can lead to instability, particularly when using approximate reversal of the masking process as in Proposal 1, Gumbel-Softmax relaxation, or other heuristic methods to handle discrete outputs. We derive bounds on the stability of the gradients and show that high-dimensional discrete output spaces can lead to catastrophic instability, particularly when the output distributions are concentrated in a small region of the output space.
CONTROLS: Examine the theoretical bounds for different discrete model settings, including large and small vocabularies, concentrated and uniform output distributions.
COST: Negligible (theoretical analysis only, 0 GPU-hours).
PREDICTION: This analysis should provide critical insight into the general challenges faced by gradient propagation in discrete models and inform better design choices for Proposal 1 and other approaches, though exact instability conditions may prove difficult to predict in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Regularized Policy Gradient Estimation for Adversarial Training of Discrete Generators
PROPOSAL: We develop a new policy-gradient estimator for adversarial training of discrete generators that mitigates the high-variance issue of existing REINFORCE-based methods. By adding a regularization term to the policy loss that encourages the generator to produce output distributions with low entropy, we can significantly reduce the variance of the gradient estimates. We further propose an adaptive regularization scheme to adjust the strength of the regularization based on the generator's output distribution.
CONTROLS: Compare with the existing REINFORCE-based method and with the policy-gradient estimator using the Gumbel-Softmax relaxation.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (training discrete generators under adversarial settings can be computationally expensive).
PREDICTION: This approach should provide a more stable and low-variance policy-gradient estimator for adversarial training of discrete generators, but may require careful tuning of the regularization strength and adaptation parameters.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Regularized Policy Gradient Estimation for Adversarial Training of Discrete Generators
PROPOSAL: We enhance the previous proposal by using a learned, rather than fixed, regularization term. Specifically, we propose an adversarial regularization scheme where the generator's regularization strength is learned through a separate discriminator network trained to predict the regularization strength. This allows the generator to adaptively adjust its regularization strength to cope with different output distributions.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original proposal using fixed regularization strength and with a baseline using a fixed but stronger regularization strength.
COST: 30 GPU-hours (training additional discriminator network and adapting to different output distributions).
PREDICTION: This enhanced approach should allow for more effective and adaptive regularization of the policy gradient estimation, improving the stability and low-variance properties. However, it may introduce additional mode collapse problems if not carefully designed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decoupling Token Optimization from Image Optimization for Text-to-Image Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach that separates the optimization of token-level discrete generators from the optimization of the image-level quality. Specifically, we use a learned reward model to guide the optimization of the image quality, while the token-level generator is optimized using a token-level loss function that does not require gradient flow through the image. This allows us to leverage gradients from the reward model to improve image quality, while maintaining stability and differentiability in the discrete generator.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that optimizes both token-level and image-level quality simultaneously, and with an approach that uses gradient flow through the image to optimize the token-level generator.
COST: 40 GPU-hours (training additional reward model and decoupling token-level generator).
PREDICTION: This approach should allow for more efficient and stable optimization of both token-level and image-level quality, but may require careful tuning of the reward model and token-level loss function.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Decoupling Token Optimization from Image Optimization for Text-to-Image Generation
PROPOSAL: We enhance the previous proposal by introducing a novelty search mechanism to further improve image quality. Specifically, we use a separate novelty score to encourage the generator to produce images that are not only high-quality but also novel and diverse. This allows us to leverage the benefits of novelty search, such as exploration-exploitation tradeoff and diversity preservation, to enhance the quality of generated images.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that uses only a standard reward model, and with an approach that uses novelty search but without decoupling token-level and image-level optimization.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (training additional novelty model and introducing novelty search mechanism).
PREDICTION: This enhanced approach should allow for more efficient and effective exploration of the image space, leading to higher-quality and more diverse generated images. However, it may require careful tuning of the novelty score and exploration-exploitation tradeoff.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Diffusion Model for Discrete Image Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a hierarchical diffusion model for discrete image generation, where we represent the image as a hierarchical composition of discrete tokens. We use a top-down approach to generate the image, where the top-level tokens are first sampled using a discrete generator, and then the bottom-level tokens are generated using a hierarchical refinement process. This allows us to capture complex image structures and textures in a discrete representation.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that uses a single-level discrete generator, and with an approach that uses continuous image representation.
COST: 80 GPU-hours (training hierarchical diffusion model).
PREDICTION: This approach should allow for more efficient and effective generation of complex images, but may require careful tuning of the hierarchy and refinement process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Modal Embedding Alignment for Discrete Text-to-Image Generators
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-modal embedding alignment method for discrete text-to-image generators, where we align the text and image embeddings using a shared, learnable space. We use this aligned space to refine the text and image representations, and then use the refined representations to guide the discrete generator. This allows us to align the text and image modalities and improve the quality and coherence of generated images.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that uses separate text and image embeddings, and with an approach that uses pre-trained language and image models.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (training multi-modal embedding alignment model).
PREDICTION: This approach should allow for more effective alignment of text and image modalities, leading to higher-quality and more coherent generated images, but may require careful tuning of the shared space and alignment process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-Aware Discrete Generator Architecture Search
PROPOSAL: We propose a reward-aware discrete generator architecture search method that optimizes the generator architecture for a given reward function. We use a reinforcement learning-based approach to search for the optimal architecture, where the reward function is used to evaluate the generator's performance. This allows us to discover novel and effective generator architectures that are specifically tailored to the task at hand.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that uses a fixed generator architecture, and with an approach that uses architecture search but without reward-awareness.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (training reinforcement learning model for architecture search).
PREDICTION: This approach should allow for more effective discovery of novel and effective generator architectures, leading to improved performance and quality in generated images, but may require careful tuning of the reward function and search process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Evaluation of Discrete Text-to-Image Generators
PROPOSAL: We propose a comprehensive evaluation framework for discrete text-to-image generators, where we assess the generators' performance on various metrics, including image quality, diversity, coherence, and semantic similarity. We use a comprehensive set of evaluation metrics and datasets to provide a thorough understanding of the generators' strengths and weaknesses.
CONTROLS: Compare with popular discrete text-to-image generators, and with a baseline that uses continuous image representation.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (evaluating generators on various metrics and datasets).
PREDICTION: This comprehensive evaluation framework will provide a deep understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of discrete text-to-image generators, allowing researchers to select the best generator architecture for specific applications and to identify areas for further improvement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Classifier-Free Guidance in Finite-Speed Kac Flows
PROPOSAL: Experimentally compare the effect of classifier-free guidance on the kinetic energy of finite-speed Kac flows on unconditional image generation. Specifically, modify the existing damped wave equation-based flow by introducing a weighted mixture of the unconditional generator's velocity and the classifier's prediction, following the standard diffusion model guidance recipe. Evaluate if and for how long the guided velocity field remains at finite kinetic energy over the sampling trajectory, as measured by the integral of the kinetic energy over time.
CONTROLS: Compare to the baseline unconditional flow without guidance and to the original guided diffusion models with system time-varying speed for unconditional image generation. Analyze how much guidance is needed to maintain kinetic energy balance, and how guidance interacts with damping to affect flow properties.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (modifying and training existing models)
PREDICTION: Classifer-free guidance can maintain finite kinetic energy with up to 50% of the unconditional velocity, but long-term guidance requires more than 70% of the classifier's predictions to avoid kinetic energy blow-up, arriving at a stabilization trade-off, suggesting the importance of understanding flow mechanics for modelling guided systems.
