ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Necessity of Strict Equivariance in Metanetworks
PROPOSAL: Derive a mathematical framework to analyze the relationship between weight-level equivariance and functional equivalence in metanetworks. Specifically, we will prove that strict equivariance is not a necessary condition for metanetworks to preserve functional identity, by showing that a weaker requirement, namely "equivariance within functional equivalence classes," is sufficient.
CONTROLS: Compare our theoretical results to existing relaxations of equivariance in deep learning, such as relaxed convolution weights and soft constraints.
COST: 10 GPU-hours (theoretical work)
PREDICTION: We expect to show that strict equivariance is not necessary for metanetworks to preserve functional identity, but identifying a practical realization of this weaker requirement may require additional work.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Weakening Strict Equivariance for Metanetworks with Multihead Attention
PROPOSAL: Investigate the feasibility of relaxing strict equivariance in metanetworks that process multihead attention architectures. We will design a metanetwork layer that satisfies a weakened equivariance requirement, specifically "equivariance up to reordering of attention heads." This layer will use a permutation-equivariant neural network to aggregate the attention weights, and evaluate its performance on implicit neural representation classification tasks.
CONTROLS: Implement a baseline metanetwork layer with strict equivariance, and compare its performance to our relaxed equivariance implementation. Evaluate the robustness of our layer to variations in the attention head permutation.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (including training and evaluation)
PREDICTION: We expect to show that our layer is effective in preserving functional equivalence, but may be more susceptible to overfitting or require additional regularization compared to its strictly equivariant counterpart.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: A Comparison of Strict and Weakened Equivariance in Metanetworks for Implicit Neural Representation Classification
REVISED PROPOSAL: Refine the existing proposal for investigating the feasibility of relaxing strict equivariance in metanetworks that process multihead attention architectures. In addition to designing a metanetwork layer that satisfies a weakened equivariance requirement, specifically "equivariance up to reordering of attention heads," we will also experiment with existing permutation-equivariant neural networks as a baseline to compare the performance of our proposed approach. Furthermore, we will investigate how our weakened equivariance requirement affects the implicit neural representation classification tasks both in a classification metric and an edit metric. 
CONTROLS: Evaluate performance on the SINTEL dataset for implicit neural representation classification, and compare the classification and edit metrics between our proposed metanetwork layer and its strictly equivariant counterpart. Assess the robustness of our layer to variations in the attention head permutation and compare it with the baseline model.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (including training and evaluation)
PREDICTION: We expect to show that our layer can achieve competitive or better performance in both classification and edit metrics compared to the strictly equivariant layer, while providing a more flexible and expressive representation of neural network functionality.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: A Comparison of Strict and Weakened Equivariance in Metanetworks for Implicit Neural Representation Classification
REVISED PROPOSAL: Refine the existing proposal for investigating the feasibility of relaxing strict equivariance in metanetworks that process multihead attention architectures. In addition to designing a metanetwork layer that satisfies a weakened equivariance requirement, specifically "equivariance up to reordering of attention heads," we will also experiment with existing permutation-equivariant neural networks as a baseline to compare the performance of our proposed approach. Furthermore, we will investigate how our weakened equivariance requirement affects the implicit neural representation classification tasks both in a classification metric and an edit metric. 
CONTROLS: Evaluate performance on the SINTEL dataset for implicit neural representation classification, and compare the classification and edit metrics between our proposed metanetwork layer and its strictly equivariant counterpart. Assess the robustness of our layer to variations in the attention head permutation and compare it with the baseline model using a fixed number of edits (e.g. 5) to evaluate edit distance while reducing attempted edits of low confidence.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (including training and evaluation)
PREDICTION: We expect to show that our layer can achieve competitive or better performance in both classification and edit metrics compared to the strictly equivariant layer, while providing a more flexible and expressive representation of neural network functionality with constrained edit distance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Exploration of Approximate Equivariance for Metanetworks Processing Feedforward Networks
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a metanetwork layer that processes the weights of feedforward networks, satisfying a relaxed equivariance requirement, specifically "equivariance up to scaling and permutation." We will investigate how this layer performs on tasks such as neural network generalization prediction from weights and implicit neural representation editing.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of our approximately equivariant metanetwork layer to both a strictly equivariant layer and a randomly initialized metanetwork layer.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (including training and evaluation)
PREDICTION: We expect to show that our approximately equivariant metanetwork layer can provide a good balance between representational expressivity and symmetry preservation for feedforward networks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Equivariance Properties in Convolutional Networks
PROPOSAL: Study the symmetries present in the weights of convolutional networks and develop a theoretical understanding of how they impact the behavior of metanetworks processing these networks. Specifically, we will investigate the connection between convolutional neural network symmetry groups and the achievable equivariance properties of metanetworks, to identify cases where weak equivariance provides a suitable trade-off between representational capacity and symmetry preservation.
CONTROLS: Compare our theoretical findings to experimental results from metanetworks processing convolutional neural networks.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (theoretical work)
PREDICTION: We expect to show that convolutional networks exhibit distinct symmetry patterns, which can be leveraged to develop metanetwork architectures with optimal trade-offs between equivariance and expressivity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Designing a Pruning-Weight Optimizer for Metanetworks
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new algorithmic component to address the efficiency of pretrained metanetworks on various tasks. Specifically, we propose a pruning-weight optimizer that works in conjunction with the existing metanetwork framework and focuses on reducing the effective size of the network while preserving the learned equivalence classes, by leveraging information obtained from existing  pruning methods alongside a small additional training data set.
CONTROLS: Compare the pruning-weight optimizer's effectiveness to established pruning methods and the state-of-the-art pruning methods in terms of FLOPS reduction and performance maintenance on image grid edit tasks and a few CIFAR and ImageNet tasks with given edits to validate the model's robustness to pruning - edit loss within a specified bound.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (training, pruning, and validation)
PREDICTION: We expect to show that our pruning-weight optimizer can achieve a better trade-off between model size and accuracy compared to existing pruning methods, yielding a more efficient and scalable metanetwork architecture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Policy Learning using Equivalent Neural Network Policies
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of metanetworks to learn policies for decision-making tasks by treating equivalent neural network policies as different manifestations of the same policy. We will evaluate the impact of metanetworks on policy learning by modeling tasks such as Atari games or other reinforcement learning benchmarks, enabling researchers to equip AI systems with flexible, adaptation-friendly representations.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of our metanetwork-based policy learning to standard approaches to policy learning and ablate the importance of both the extent of functional equivalence enforced by the metanetwork and the optimization strategy employed.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (including model learning and control strategy)
PREDICTION: We expect that metanetworks can outperform or at least match the performance of existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of policy learning from fewer policy behaviors without the need for adding a frequency penalty or edit numerical loss.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bayesian Metanetworks for Uncertainty Estimation and Exploration-Exploitation Trade-offs
PROPOSAL: Develop a Bayesian approach to metanetworks that incorporates uncertainty estimation and exploration-exploitation trade-offs. We will introduce a probabilistic framework for metanetworks, which learns a distribution over the parameters of the network, allowing for uncertainty quantification and exploration-exploitation decision-making.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of our Bayesian metanetworks to standard metanetworks and other uncertainty estimation methods in tasks such as implicit neural representation prediction and edit predictions within specified distance tolerance on challenging problems from real-world benchmarks (e.g., Omniglot).
COST: 300 GPU-hours (including uncertainty estimation and decision-making)
PREDICTION: We expect that Bayesian metanetworks can provide accurate uncertainty estimates and exploratory policies, while offering a flexible framework for incorporating prior knowledge and eliminating dependence on specific weights when computationally feasible.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Necessity of Strict Equivariance in Metanetworks
REVISED PROPOSAL: Refine the existing theoretical framework for analyzing the relationship between weight-level equivariance and functional equivalence in metanetworks. Specifically, we will strengthen the proof that strict equivariance is not a necessary condition for metanetworks to preserve functional identity, and explore the implications of this result for meta-learning architectures.
CONTROLS: Compare the refined theoretical framework to existing metanetwork architectures, and evaluate the impact of our revised understanding of equivariance on tasks such as implicit neural representation classification and editing.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (theoretical work)
PREDICTION: We expect that our revised theoretical framework will provide a deeper understanding of the role of equivariance in metanetworks, and enable the development of more effective metanetwork architectures that balance representational capacity and symmetry preservation.

TITLE: Region Proposal by Uncertainty Sampling for Visual Question Answering
PROPOSAL: We'll train an MLLM to predict a heatmap of uncertainty scores for per-pixel relevance to a question, and iteratively refine its own regions of interest by selecting the pixels with the highest uncertainty scores. We adapt this uncertainty sampling approach from active learning research for standard computer vision tasks, so we'll apply the visual hardening and multiple negative sampling optimizations commonly used in that domain. ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Region Proposal by Uncertainty Sampling for Visual Question Answering
PROPOSAL: We investigate training a pretrained MLLM on an auxiliary objective that encourages uncertainty in relevance scores over varying image resolutions. Specifically, we modify the MLM loss to also predict a relevance map for each image pixel, sampled at a lower resolution than the original image. This setup encourages the model to reason about which visual details are relevant to the question, even when the image resolution is reduced. We apply the same setup to standard visual cropping baselines, to compare their robustness to reduced resolution to that of our uncertainty sampling approach.
CONTROLS: We compare this new auxiliary objective to the original version, and also vary the control resolution at which relevance maps are sampled. We also consider the performance of our approach when using interpolated relevance maps, as opposed to directly sampled ones.
COST: 150 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect a performance boost from our new auxiliary loss, as well as improved robustness to reduced resolution compared to standard visual cropping. However, our approach might suffer from overfitting, if the model relies too heavily on the auxiliary loss when the resolution is reduced.

TITLE: Analysis and Improvement of Local Explanability for Visual Question Answering 
PROPOSAL: We conduct a comprehensive analysis of the local explanations generated by our visual cropping methods (including the ones in set 1, 2, and 3), to identify what aspects of the output are most relevant to the question and what constitutes the "visual context" that contributes to the final answer. Our focus is specifically on explaining the relevance of small visual details, and making sure our methods pick up on these subtle contextual cues. We use saliency maps, feature importance scores, and other local interpretability techniques to break down the importance of each image region. 
Based on our analysis, we identify a set of critical improvements to local explainability and propose a novel "Region-Specific Feature Attention" (RSFA) mechanism to refine the visual context of small details by re-weighting the importance of each feature according to the relevance and coherence of their input regions.

TITLE: Adversarial Training for Robust Visual Cropping on Noisy and Partially Obscured Images
PROPOSAL: We propose an adversarial training framework to enhance the robustness of our visual cropping methods against various types of image noise and partial occlusions. Our method trains a generator to introduce image noise and occlusions, and a discriminator to distinguish between the original and noisy/occluded images. We extend this basic setup by adding a cropping module that can handle the noisy/occluded images and a discriminator that evaluates the correctness of the cropped regions. This adversarial training framework will enable our visual cropping methods to become more robust to real-world image imperfections. TITLE: Region-Specific Attention Augmentation for Fine-Grained Visual Question Answering
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel attention mechanism, Region-Specific Attention Augmentation (RSA), that selectively amplifies the importance of regions relevant to the question while suppressing irrelevant regions. RSA is designed to work in conjunction with our existing visual cropping methods. It leverages the localized attention capabilities of the masked vision transformers to provide an attention map that focuses on the most informative regions. By augmenting our baseline visual cropping methods with RSA, we expect to see significant improvements in fine-grained visual question answering tasks. We extend this setup by combining RSA with each of our other methods, to confirm that this extra layer of spatial contextualization can improve their performance.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the impact of RSA on our existing visual cropping methods, and analyze its performance against state-of-the-art models for fine-grained visual question answering.
COST: 180 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: RSA is likely to improve our methods' performance on fine-grained visual question answering tasks, but may also introduce some challenges related to interpreting the results, due to the increased complexity of the attention maps.

PROPOSAL: We modify the adversarial training approach from our previous proposal to focus specifically on adapting the MLLM to the local features extracted from relevant regions of the image. Our goal is to improve the robustness of our visual cropping methods to variations in the size and position of the target object within the image. We achieve this by using a spatial transformers-based approach to align the local features extracted from the image with the corresponding context in the text. TITLE: Evaluation and Comparison of Visual Question Answering Systems for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
PROPOSAL: We perform a comprehensive evaluation and comparison of the visual question answering systems developed throughout this research project. We assess their performance on a range of fine-grained visual understanding tasks, including object recognition, scene understanding, and visual reasoning. We also compare the performance of our systems to existing state-of-the-art models, including those that use global and local attention mechanisms. Our analysis will provide insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each system, as well as the challenges and limitations of fine-grained visual understanding tasks. We also provide recommendations for future research directions in this area.
CONTROLS: We compare our systems to existing state-of-the-art models, and also evaluate the performance of our systems on a range of tasks, including object recognition, scene understanding, and visual reasoning.

PROPOSAL 6: Region-Specific Attention Augmentation for Fine-Grained Visual Question Answering
We propose a novel attention mechanism, Region-Specific Attention Augmentation (RSA), that selectively amplifies the importance of regions relevant to the question while suppressing irrelevant regions. RSA is designed to work in conjunction with our existing visual cropping methods. It leverages the localized attention capabilities of the masked vision transformers to provide an attention map that focuses on the most informative regions. By augmenting our baseline visual cropping methods with RSA, we expect to see significant improvements in fine-grained visual question answering tasks. We extend this setup by combining RSA with each of our other methods, to confirm that this extra layer of spatial contextualization can improve their performance.
Controls: We evaluate the impact of RSA on our existing visual cropping methods, and analyze its performance against state-of-the-art models for fine-grained visual question answering.
Estimated cost: 180 GPU-hours.
Prediction: RSA is likely to improve our methods' performance on fine-grained visual question answering tasks, but may also introduce some challenges related to interpreting the results, due to the increased complexity of the attention maps.

PROPOSAL 7: Interactive Visual Question Answering with Reduced-Resolution Guidance
We design an interactive visual question answering system where the model first produces a reduced-resolution version of the image, and then iteratively refines its predictions based on user feedback. Our approach leverages a novel combination of our existing visual cropping methods and user guidance to focus on the most relevant regions of the image and improve the accuracy of the final answer. We test this system on a variety of user-interaction protocols, including both active and passive feedback, to evaluate its performance and limitations. PROPOSAL:  Revising the previous proposal to improve its scalability and inference speed, propose a lightweight region-guided cross-modal attention mechanism that leverages a hierarchical feature pyramid to filter out irrelevant image regions based on their semantic relevance to the question, and focus the MLLM's attention on the most relevant regions. TITLE: Active Visual Search via Contextual Few-Shot Learning
PROPOSAL:  Introduce an active visual search framework that integrates contextual few-shot learning to selectively search for relevant image regions that are likely to contain the answer to the question. Train a few-shot learner to adapt to new question-context pairs by learning to recognize the relevant visual features and objects, and use this knowledge to guide the visual search process. Evaluate its performance on fine-grained VQA benchmarks and compare to existing visual search methods.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Dynamic Contextual Few-Shot Learning for Active Visual Search
PROPOSAL:  Revising the previous proposal to improve its adaptability and robustness, introduce a dynamic contextual few-shot learning framework that dynamically selects the most relevant contextual information and image regions to adapt the few-shot learner to the current question-context pair. This is achieved by integrating a hierarchy of dynamic attention mechanisms that dynamically weigh the importance of different contextual features and image regions. Evaluate its performance on fine-grained VQA benchmarks and compare to existing visual search methods.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Efficient Visual Search for Fine-Grained VQA with Dynamic Region Partitioning
PROPOSAL: Implement a dynamic region partitioning strategy in mixture of experts architecture for MLLMs, where the partitioning is learned jointly with the MLLM's parameter update. This approach will divide the input image into a set of meaningful regions, each processed separately by an expert model, reducing the dimensionality of the visual tokens that the MLLM sees. 
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art visual cropping methods like SEAL, DC², and ViCrop, as well as a naive ablation with equal-sized grid partitioning.
COST: 100 GPU-hours ( prototype model + hyperparameter tuning)
PREDICTION: The dynamic partitioning approach will achieve state-of-the-art performance among visual cropping methods on fine-grained VQA benchmarks like VQA-2.0 and COCO-QA, while significantly reducing the computational overhead of exhaustive search methods. However, it might face challenges in handling images with high variability in object size and distributions, leading to suboptimal partitioning.

The following two experiments will use real-world images but then become cheaper simulated data only for efficiency.

1 - We will need just one of the next experiments (2 and 3) but won't choose which one until after they're designed.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Unreal World: Exploring Efficient Simulation-based Image Synthesis for Fine-Grained VQAs
PROPOSAL: Develop a physics-based simulator for generating high-resolution, realistic images with diverse fine-grained visual details from various object classes. This simulator will allow for rapid creation of large-scale datasets that mimic real-world scenarios, enabling efficient exploration of visual search strategies and quantitative analysis of their performance on fine-grained VQAs. The simulated data will be designed to match the distribution of real-world data in terms of object size, orientation, and context. 
CONTROLS: Evaluate the simulator-generated data using a currently available MLLM architecture, and compare its performance on fine-grained VQA benchmarks against the performance achieved by the same MLLM on real-world data.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (simulator development and initial dataset generation)
PREDICTION: The simulator-generated data will exhibit strong correlation with real-world datasets, enabling efficient exploration of visual search strategies and allowing researchers to develop robust fine-grained VQA models before fine-tuning on expensive real-world data. The simulator will also facilitate the testing of domain adaptation methods.

The following three experiments will use all MLLMs. 

2 - There are four experiments planned used on car-class data; like the Explore Similarity-Driven Model Optimization Method utilizing images built by the simulator.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Car-eer Advancement: Multi-Car Viewpoint Invariant Fine-Grained VQA
PROPOSAL: Utilize the simulator-generated data to train and evaluate MLLMs on fine-grained VQA tasks specific to the car class, focusing on multi-car viewpoints. This experiment will include the development of a new dataset consisting of diverse images showcasing different cars from varying viewpoints, and will be designed to test the MLLMs' ability to generalize across viewpoints. For control purposes, a baseline model will be fine-tuned on existing viewpoint-biased vehicle datasets, such as PRow (eg 100 images of different car frontal views). 
CONTROLS: Investigate the effect of viewpoint-invariant representation learning on the performance of popular MLLMs like Modern Local Encoder (MLE), Local-Global-Vision Transformer (LGVT), and reference the works of Ma et al.
COST: 300 GPU-hours (dataset generation & model training on MLE model, experimental sampling). 
PREDICTION: The viewpoint-invariant representations will show significant improvement for MLLMs' generalizability on real-world images of diverse viewpoints regarding fine-grained VQA problems related to automotive. The presented measures of viewpoint sensitivity of pre-trained MLLMs and newly proposed Q-tasks could possibly reach objectives to distil for more methodical performance revisions/trade-offs in the prerequisites localizer-partner co-working benchmarks research attempted i.e. reductions rational acquaintance rating flow performance.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Enhancing Flash Attention for Fine-Grained VQAs
PROPOSAL: Investigate and extend the FlashAttention framework to support hierarchical processing of visual tokens, allowing it to handle the increased sequence length resulting from processing local crops from high-resolution images. The goal is to enable efficient MLLMs to effectively leverage fine-grained visual details from local regions, while retaining the benefits of FlashAttention's efficient attention mechanism. 
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed FlashAttention extension with the standard FlashAttention implementation on fine-grained VQA benchmarks, as well as a baseline that uses a standard transformer decoder.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (model implementation & hyperparameter tuning)
PREDICTION: The extended FlashAttention will demonstrate improved performance on fine-grained VQA tasks, particularly on those requiring high-resolution visual features. Its compatibility with existing visual cropping strategies will also enable efficient visual search methods to further benefit from hierarchical attention processing.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: LEAF: Local Expert Attention Fusion for MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Develop a Local Expert Attention Fusion (LEAF) mechanism, which selectively utilizes expert models' outputs to mask and recalibrate the attention weights of a standard transformer decoder in a multi-task learning setup. LEAF will adapt to the spatial and contextual dependencies of visual features from local crops, allowing the MLLM to selectively attend to the most relevant regions for fine-grained VQA tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of LEAF with the naivest models, and other state-of-the-art embeddings-based tech. incorporating higher att-risk aggregation.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (model implementation & hyperparameter tuning)
PREDICTION: LEAF will exhibit significant improvements in accuracy for fine-grained VQA tasks, particularly when combined with efficient visual search methods or FlashAttention. By leveraging local expert knowledge, LEAF will effectively address the issue of redundant or irrelevant visual features that plague current MLLMs.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Car-eer Advancement: Multi-Scene Contextual Fine-Grained VQA
REVISED PROPOSAL: Utilize the simulator-generated data to train and evaluate MLLMs on fine-grained VQA tasks specific to the Autonomous Driving (AD) domain, focusing on detecting and describing roadway signs, lane markings, and road surface conditions. This experiment will include the development of a new dataset consisting of diverse images showcasing AD-specific scenes, and will be designed to test the MLLMs' ability to generalize across different scene contexts. For control purposes, a baseline model will be fine-tuned on existing viewpoint-biased AD datasets, and a scene-description model will be trained on the CLEVR-ADM dataset.
CONTROLS: Investigate the effect of multi-scene contextual representation learning on the performance of popular MLLMs like Modern Local Encoder (MLE), Local-Global-Vision Transformer (LGVT), and the proposed scene-description model.
COST: 300 GPU-hours (dataset generation & model training on MLE model, experimental sampling).
PREDICTION: The multi-scene contextual representations will show significant improvement for MLLMs' generalizability on real-world images of diverse scenes regarding fine-grained VQA problems related to autonomous driving, by judging both their described scene and accuracy capabilities regarding describable locations and objects, requiring both resolution and accuracy.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Efficient Visual Search for Fine-Grained VQA with Dynamic Region Partitioning
REVISED PROPOSAL: Implement a dynamic region partitioning strategy in a mixture of experts architecture for MLLMs, where the partitioning is learned jointly with the MLLM's parameter update and incorporates information from the image's semantic segmentation mask. This approach will divide the input image into a set of meaningful regions, each processed separately by an expert model, reducing the dimensionality of the visual tokens that the MLLM sees and improving recall and precision.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art visual cropping methods like SEAL, DC², and ViCrop, as well as a naive ablation with equal-sized grid partitioning, and a baseline model that uses a standard transformer decoder.
COST: 120 GPU-hours (prototype model + hyperparameter tuning)
PREDICTION: The revised dynamic partitioning approach will achieve state-of-the-art performance among visual cropping methods on fine-grained VQA benchmarks like VQA-2.0 and COCO-QA, while significantly reducing the computational overhead of exhaustive search methods.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Unreal World: Exploring Efficient Simulation-based Image Synthesis for Fine-Grained VQAs
REVISED PROPOSAL: Develop a physics-based simulator for generating high-resolution, realistic images with diverse fine-grained visual details from various object classes, specifically focusing on the Remote Sensing Imagery (RSI) domain. The simulator will be designed to mimic the high-level features and textures commonly found in RSI images, such as satellite or aerial images. This revised simulator will generate a data set that is highly relevant to the task of fine-grained VQA in the RSI domain and will help speed up the development of VQA models for this domain.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the revised simulator-generated data using a currently available MLLM architecture, and compare its performance on fine-grained VQA benchmarks against the performance achieved by the same MLLM on real-world RSI data.
COST: 220 GPU-hours (simulator development and initial dataset generation)
PREDICTION: The revised simulator-generated data will exhibit strong correlation with real-world RSI images, enabling efficient exploration of visual search strategies and allowing researchers to develop robust fine-grained VQA models for the RSI domain.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: LEAF: Local Expert Attention Fusion for MLLMs
REVISED PROPOSAL: Revise the LEAF mechanism to incorporate feedback from the MLLM's output and adjust the attention weights in a manner that balances the contributions of the expert models and the transformer decoder. This revised version of LEAF will be designed to adaptively weigh the importance of different visual features and attention weights, allowing the MLLM to learn more effective representations for fine-grained VQAs.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the revised LEAF with the original version, as well as a baseline model that uses a standard transformer decoder, on fine-grained VQA benchmarks.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (model implementation & hyperparameter tuning)
PREDICTION: The revised LEAF mechanism will demonstrate improved performance on fine-grained VQA tasks, particularly in scenarios where the MLLM needs to weigh the importance of different visual features and attention weights.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Environment-Specific Model Pretraining for Millimeter-Wave Radar Imagery
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a convolutional neural network (CNN) on a dataset of calibrated millimeter-wave radar imagery specifically designed to optimize performance on near-range objects with varied occlusion, texture, and geometry.
CONTROLS: Experiments will compare the pretraining strategy to standard image classification pretraining (e.g., ImageNet), and ablate the importance of specific dataset characteristics (e.g., varying occlusion levels, diverse textures).
COST: Estimated 10,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Environment-specific pretraining significantly outperforms standard pretraining on near-range, occluded objects, but may not transfer well to far-range scenarios or objects with drastically different appearance; performance could fail to generalize to novel environments or object classes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RF-Octree: An Adaptive Hierarchical Representation for Millimeter-Wave Radar Point Clouds
PROPOSAL: Design a hierarchical point cloud representation (RF-Octree) that recursively subdivides space into octrees, focusing on areas with the highest density of points; this representation will adapt to the spatial complexity of near-range objects and facilitate more efficient CNN processing.
CONTROLS: Experiments will compare the RF-Octree representation to other state-of-the-art point cloud representations (e.g., Ball Tree, k-d Tree) and evaluate its impact on downstream object reconstruction tasks.
COST: Estimated 3,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The RF-Octree representation leads to improved performance on millimeter-wave radar point clouds, particularly for objects with complex geometry, but may not be as effective for far-range or simple objects; potential failure to generalize to novel point cloud topologies or extremely large datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Specular Reflection Modeling and Inpainting for Enhanced Millimeter-Wave Radar Images
PROPOSAL: Develop a GAN-based approach that models and inpaints specular reflections in millimeter-wave radar images, allowing for better representation of object surfaces and improved reconstruction accuracy.
CONTROLS: Experiments will compare the specular reflection modeling approach to state-of-the-art inpainting methods (e.g., DeepFillv2) and evaluate its impact on downstream object reconstruction tasks; ablation studies will investigate the importance of different components within the GAN model (e.g., generator, discriminator).
COST: Estimated 5,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed approach significantly enhances millimeter-wave radar image quality and leads to improved reconstruction accuracy, particularly for objects with large specular reflections; however, potential issues may arise from mode collapse or instability in the GAN training process, particularly on complex or noisy data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Channel Fusion For Accurate Millimeter-Wave Radar Object Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of multi-channel fusion techniques (e.g., late fusion, early fusion) for combining information from multiple millimeter-wave radar frequency channels, with the goal of improving object reconstruction accuracy and robustness to occlusions and noise.
CONTROLS: Experiments will compare the multi-channel fusion approach to single-channel fusion and evaluate its impact on downstream object reconstruction tasks; ablation studies will investigate the importance of different fusion methods and parameters (e.g., channel selection, weights).
COST: Estimated 4,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Multi-channel fusion leads to improved object reconstruction accuracy and robustness, particularly on challenging data with heavy occlusions or noise; potential issues may arise from synchronization and phase alignment of multiple frequency channels, particularly in real-world scenarios with varying transmission conditions.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Through-Occlusion Imaging Framework with Residual Learning and Domain Knowledge
PROPOSAL: Revise the framework from proposing a feature extraction approach with domain knowledge and combine with modern deep residual learning techniques; this framework will recover the 3D geometry of occluded objects by exploiting millimeter-wave radar reflectivity patterns and learned features from a deep neural network.
CONTROLS: Experiments will compare the performance of the proposed framework with existing methods on through-occlusion imaging tasks and evaluate its robustness to varying occlusion levels, object complexity, and radar signal noise.
COST: Estimated 6,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The through-occlusion imaging framework with residual learning and domain knowledge significantly improves the recovery of 3D geometry of occluded objects and demonstrates robustness to challenging data conditions; however, potential issues may arise from over-reliance on domain knowledge, which might not generalize well to novel environments or objects with drastically different appearance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Radar and Vision Fusion for 3D Object Reconstruction from Millimeter-Wave and RGB Data
PROPOSAL: Develop a deep learning framework that jointly fuses millimeter-wave radar and RGB images to reconstruct 3D object geometry, leveraging the strengths of both sensing modalities to improve accuracy and robustness.
CONTROLS: Experiments will compare the performance of the joint radar and vision fusion approach to single-modality reconstruction and evaluate its impact on downstream tasks (e.g., object classification, segmentation).
COST: Estimated 8,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Joint radar and vision fusion leads to significantly improved 3D object reconstruction accuracy and robustness, particularly for complex or occluded objects; however, potential issues may arise from synchronization and alignment of radar and RGB data, which might be challenging in real-world scenarios with varying transmission conditions or object motion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learnable Radar Reflectivity Models with Graph Convolutional Networks
PROPOSAL: Develop a graph convolutional network (GCN)-based framework to learn radar reflectivity models from millimeter-wave radar data, enabling the discovery of complex reflectivity patterns and their embeddings in the 3D geometry of objects.
CONTROLS: Experiments will compare the learnable radar reflectivity models with traditional reflectivity models (e.g., dipole-based models) and evaluate their impact on downstream tasks (e.g., object classification, segmentation).
COST: Estimated 7,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The learnable radar reflectivity models demonstrate superior performance on complex object classification and segmentation tasks, particularly on data with varying reflectivity patterns; however, potential issues may arise from the requirement for large-scale training data and careful design of the GCN architecture, which might be challenging to optimize.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Dataset for Millimeter-Wave Radar-Based 3D Object Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Collect, label, and publicly release a large real-world dataset of millimeter-wave radar scans for 3D object reconstruction, including a diverse set of objects with varying geometry, texture, and occlusions.
CONTROLS: The dataset will be evaluated on its quality, diversity, and usefulness for training and benchmarking 3D object reconstruction models; ablation studies will investigate the impact of dataset size, diversity, and quality on model performance.
COST: Estimated 20,000 GPU-hours (for dataset creation) + 2,000 GPU-hours (for evaluation and ablation)
PREDICTION: The released dataset will become a de facto standard for millimeter-wave radar-based 3D object reconstruction research, leading to improved model performance and a wider range of applications; however, potential issues may arise from data annotation inaccuracies, dataset imbalance, or data distribution shifts that could affect model generalization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Millimeter-Wave Radar-Based 3D Object Reconstruction System for In-Transit Inspection
PROPOSAL: Develop a complete millimeter-wave radar-based 3D object reconstruction system for in-transit inspection, integrating and evaluating the proposed models from previous experiments to achieve high-performance reconstruction of objects inside containers or boxes during transportation.
CONTROLS: The system will be evaluated on its overall performance, robustness, and usability for real-world in-transit inspection scenarios; ablation studies will investigate the impact of individual models and their combinations on the system's performance.
COST: Estimated 10,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed system demonstrates superior performance on in-transit inspection scenarios, enabling accurate 3D object reconstruction and facilitating efficient and safe cargo inspection; however, potential issues may arise from real-world sensor noise, occlusions, or varying transmission conditions that could affect system robustness and reliability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Millimeter-Wave Radar Accuracy Limits in 3D Object Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical analysis of the fundamental limits of millimeter-wave radar accuracy in 3D object reconstruction, modeling the relationship between radar frequency, resolution, and accuracy, and providing insights into the optimal design of millimeter-wave radar systems for 3D object reconstruction.
CONTROLS: The analysis will provide a baseline understanding of the theoretical limits of millimeter-wave radar accuracy, and experiments will evaluate the agreement between theoretical predictions and empirical results from experiments (e.g., the impact of radar frequency and resolution on reconstruction accuracy).
COST: Estimated 1,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis reveals fundamental limits on millimeter-wave radar accuracy, providing a deeper understanding of the underlying physics and informing the design of future radar systems for 3D object reconstruction; however, potential issues may arise from oversimplifications or inaccuracies in the theoretical model, which could affect the reliability of the analysis.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Feedforward Neural Networks for RF-based 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate a feedforward neural network (FNN) for RF-based 3D object shape reconstruction from noisy real-world millimeter-wave measurements. The network will use a separate path for learning the noise distribution, which will be subtracted from the input in each noisy step of the Neural Network. Compare the results with a baseline FNN approach that ignores noise.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous RF reconstruction models with best known baseline, previously reported results with larger antennas in larger scenes
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This model can achieve state-of-the-art results in terms of reconstruction accuracy on real-world benchmarks for certain objects but will fail for more complex scenes with multiple occlusions due to its feedforward nature.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE:  Investigating Feedforward Neural Networks with Sparse Attention and Separate Noise Learning for RF-based 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Revise the feedforward neural network proposal from turn 1 to include sparse attention mechanisms in the network, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant features in the RF measurements. Additionally, introduce a separate path for learning the noise distribution, which will be subtracted from the input in each step of the network. Compare the performance with the baseline FNN approach and previous RF reconstruction models with best known baselines.
CONTROLS: Ablate the contributions of sparse attention and separate noise learning paths, compare with FNN approach
COST: 150 GPU-hours (increase due to added complexity and ablation study)
PREDICTION: This revised model is expected to outperform the original FNN in reconstruction accuracy, especially in scenes with complex occlusions, and achieve state-of-the-art results on real-world benchmarks due to the addition of sparse attention and separate noise learning. However, it may still struggle with very high-noise datasets due to its reliance on explicit noise modeling.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Investigating Graph Neural Networks for RF-based 3D Reconstruction with Topology Learning
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for RF-based 3D object shape reconstruction. In this approach, we will represent the RF measurements as a graph, where nodes correspond to individual RF measurement cells and edges capture spatial relationships between them. A GNN will then learn to predict the 3D geometry based on the graph representation. Additionally, design a topology learning module that infers the optimal graph structure from the RF measurements. Evaluate the performance of this GNN-based approach on real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous RF reconstruction models, original FNN with sparse attention and separate noise learning paths
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This GNN-based approach is expected to outperform the revised FNN in scenes with complex topological structures (e.g., objects with many holes or cavities), but may struggle with high-noise datasets due to the difficulty of learning graph structures from noisy data.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Utilizing Synthetic Data for Training and Calibration of RF Reconstruction Models
PROPOSAL: Create a synthetic dataset of RF measurements for near-range objects with varying shapes, materials, and occlusions. Train and calibrate RF reconstruction models (including both the revised FNN and the GNN) on this synthetic data, and evaluate their performance on real-world datasets. Investigate the benefits of pre-training on synthetic data and fine-tuning on real-world data. Analyze the transferability of models trained on synthetic data to real-world scenarios.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of models pre-trained on synthetic data fine-tuned on real-world data compared to those trained directly on real-world data
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Pre-training on synthetic data is expected to improve model performance on real-world datasets by providing a strong initialization and reducing the risk of overfitting. However, the effectiveness of this approach may depend on the quality and diversity of the synthetic data.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Investigating Collaborative RGB-RF Sensing for Enhanced 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Explore the fusion of RGB and RF sensing for enhanced 3D reconstruction. Propose a framework that leverages the strengths of both modalities, combining the depth information from RF measurements with the texture and color information from RGB images. Investigate various fusion techniques, such as patch-based fusion, feature-based fusion, and attention-based fusion. Evaluate the performance of this collaborative sensing approach on real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare with single-modal RF reconstruction (GNN, revised FNN) and additional multimodal models (RGB+RF)
COST: 350 GPU-hours (including additional GPU-hours for real-world RGB-RF datasets)
PREDICTION: Collaborative RGB-RF sensing is expected to provide state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction results, especially in scenes with high-texture and high-detail objects. However, it may require additional computational resources and data collection/processing steps, and may not generalize well to scenes with scars or damaged surfaces due to insuficient compatibilization of RGB and RF within same scene.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE:  Utilizing Synthetic Data with Physics-Based Simulators for Training and Calibration of RF Reconstruction Models
PROPOSAL: Update the synthetic data generation approach from turn 3 by incorporating physics-based simulators to accurately model the complex behavior of RF signals in various scenes, including occlusions and near-range objects. Train and calibrate RF reconstruction models (including both the revised FNN and the GNN) on this physics-based synthetic data, and evaluate their performance on real-world datasets. Investigate the benefits of using physically accurate simulations in model training and performance.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous synthetic data generation approaches (Turn 3), specific models' variants trained with/without physics-based simulator
COST: 420 GPU-hours (including additional GPU-hours for physics-based simulator computations)
PREDICTION: This updated approach is expected to provide more accurate and robust RF reconstruction results, especially in scenes with complex occlusions and near-range objects. However, the increased computational cost of physics-based simulators may incur a trade-off in training time and model flexibility, necessitating careful optimization and design decisions.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Investigating Efficient RF Reconstruction via Decomposition and Factorization
PROPOSAL: Explore decomposition and factorization techniques to efficiently reconstruct 3D geometry from RF measurements. Consider approximate methods such as sparse signal decomposition, matrix factorization, and others to reduce the computational complexity while maintaining acceptable accuracy. Evaluate the performance of this efficient approach on real-world datasets and compare it with the previous models.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous models (GNN, revised FNN, Collaborative RGB-RF), optimize under specific memory and speed constraints
COST: 200 GPU-hours (depending on specific decomposition and factorization techniques)
PREDICTION: Efficient RF reconstruction via decomposition and factorization is expected to provide faster and more memory-efficient solutions, especially when computational resources are limited. However, the accuracy of the results may suffer compared to more complex models, requiring careful optimization and trade-off between model complexity and computational resources.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating Hierarchical Feedforward Neural Networks with Sparse Attention and Separate Noise Learning for RF-based 3D Reconstruction

Explore the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for RF-based 3D object shape reconstruction. However, the increased computational cost of physics-based simulators may incur a trade-off in training time and model flexibility, necessitating careful optimization and design decisions.

PROPOSAL 4: Investigating Collaborative RGB-RF Sensing for Enhanced 3D Reconstruction
Explore the fusion of RGB and RF sensing for enhanced 3D reconstruction. Propose a framework that leverages the strengths of both modalities, combining the depth information from RF measurements with the texture and color information from RGB images. Investigate various fusion techniques, such as patch-based fusion, feature-based fusion, and attention-based fusion. Evaluate the performance of this collaborative sensing approach on real-world datasets.

Explore decomposition and factorization techniques to efficiently reconstruct 3D geometry from RF measurements. Evaluate the performance of this efficient approach on real-world datasets and compare it with the previous models.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Batch Normalization and Dropout for RF Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a hyperparameter search on the existing neural RF reconstruction model using radar data from the Part-A11 dataset and the 4DCT radar dataset in a controlled lab setting, applying various combinations of batch normalization and dropout rates.
CONTROLS: We will compare performance of the existing neural RF reconstruction model with different batch normalization schemes (batch norm, instance norm, layer norm) and dropout rates (0%, 20%, 40%, 60%), as well as a baseline without batch normalization or dropout.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see improvements in model stability and accuracy with the optimal choice of batch norm and dropout rates, but may see some performance degradation due to the increased regularization.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Comparing Frequency and Spatial Domain Processing for RF Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will implement various frequency domain and spatial domain processing techniques, such as windowed Fourier transform, short-time Fourier transform, and wavelet denoising, to see if they can improve signal-to-noise ratio and facilitate millimeter-level 3D RF reconstruction using the existing neural RF reconstruction model and radar data from the Part-A11 dataset and the 4DCT radar dataset in a controlled lab setting.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our implemented frequency and spatial domain processing techniques to a baseline without these techniques, and to existing neural RF reconstruction model using only spatial domain processing.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement in signal-to-noise ratio and millimeter-level 3D RF reconstruction accuracy with the best combination of frequency and spatial domain processing techniques, especially for through-occlusion imaging.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Multi-Sensor Fusion for Enhanced RF Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will collect and preprocess data from multiple mmWave radar sensors positioned around a stationary object, and then train a neural network to fuse the sensor views and improve the accuracy of millimeter-level 3D RF reconstruction using a dataset simulated with the physics engine of a 3D printer. This approach will combine the collective sensing modalities provided by the spatially diverse sensors to capture more comprehensive scene characteristics.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our multi-sensor fusion approach with that of using a single sensor, and evaluate the robustness of the multi-sensor approach to sensor failures or occlusions.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement in millimeter-level 3D RF reconstruction accuracy with the multi-sensor fusion approach, especially for through-occlusion imaging, but may encounter difficulties in calibrating and preprocessing the data, and in interpreting the spatial alignments of the sensors.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Physics-Guided Neural Network Modeling for RF Reflection Simulations
PROPOSAL: We will design and train a physics-guided neural network to model the reflection responses of surfaces under mmWave radar illumination, and integrate it into a scene reconstruction framework. We will validate this approach using simulations with ground truth and real-world mmWave radar data from the 4DCT radar dataset.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our physics-guided neural network model with that of a traditional deep learning model for RF reflection simulations, and evaluate the robustness of the physics-guided model to noise and occlusions.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement in accuracy of RF reflection simulations with our physics-guided neural network model, especially for complex scenes, but may encounter difficulties in selecting appropriate input parameters and validating the model with real-world data.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Physics-Guided Neural Network Modeling for RF Reflection Simulations (Revised)
PROPOSAL: We will design and train a physics-guided neural network to model the reflection responses of surfaces under mmWave radar illumination, accounting for the effects of surface roughness and gpointer layers, and integrate it into a scene reconstruction framework. We will validate this approach using simulations with ground truth and real-world mmWave radar data from the 4DCT radar dataset, aiming to reduce the hardness of the challenging through-occlusion imaging scenarios.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our revised physics-guided neural network model with that of a traditional deep learning model for RF reflection simulations, and evaluate the robustness of the physics-guided model to noise, occlusions and its angle-variance sensitivity.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (increased due to the additional complexities)
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement in accuracy and robustness of our revised physics-guided neural network model, especially for through-occlusion imaging scenarios, but may encounter difficulties in accurately characterizing the physical effects of surface roughness and gpointer layers.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: RF-ReID: A Novel Framework for RF-Based Object Identification and Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will develop a novel RF-based object identification and reconstruction framework (RF-ReID), which leverages the fingerprints of the RF signals to identify and reconstruct the 3D geometry of objects in a real-world scenario. RF-ReID will involve an encoder-decoder architecture that combines a modified version of the existing neural RF reconstruction model with a lightweight, convolutional neural network (CNN) that learns to identify the RF signatures of specific objects.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of RF-ReID with state-of-the-art object identification and reconstruction methods in the field of computer vision and RF sensing, and evaluate the robustness of RF-ReID under different types of occlusions and environments.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement in object identification and reconstruction accuracy with RF-ReID, especially for objects hidden behind occlusions, but may encounter difficulties in collecting and annotating large-scale RF datasets.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Learning to Remove Self-Interference in RF Signals for Improved Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will propose and train a neural network to remove self-interference in RF signals, which can lead to significant improvements in accuracy and robustness of RF reconstruction methods. The neural network will learn to identify and eliminate self-interference patterns in the RF signals by analyzing the correlation between temporally adjacent measurements.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our proposed approach with existing methods for self-interference removal and evaluate its impact on the performance of the existing neural RF reconstruction model and RF-ReID framework.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement in accuracy and robustness of RF reconstruction methods with our proposed approach, especially for objects hidden behind occlusions, but may encounter difficulties in collecting and annotating large-scale RF datasets.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Transfer Learning for RF Sensor Systems: Leveraging Outdoor Environments for Enhanced Performance in Indoor Scenarios
PROPOSAL: We will explore the use of transfer learning to leverage the performance of RF sensor systems in outdoor environments for improved performance in indoor scenarios. We will train and fine-tune a pre-trained neural RF reconstruction model on a large-scale outdoor dataset, and then apply it to indoor scenarios to evaluate its performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the pre-trained model with a model trained from scratch on an indoor dataset, and evaluate the effectiveness of transfer learning in adapting to indoor environments.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement in performance of RF sensor systems in indoor scenarios with our proposed approach, especially for RF-ReID and RF reconstruction, but may encounter difficulties in selecting the most suitable pre-trained model and fine-tuning schedule.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating Batch Normalization and Dropout for RF Reconstruction (Revised)
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a hyperparameter search on the existing neural RF reconstruction model using radar data from the Part-A11 dataset and the 4DCT radar dataset in a controlled lab setting, applying various combinations of batch normalization schemes, dropout rates, and depth-wise separable convolution techniques to improve the model's robustness and accuracy in handling noisy RF data.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our revised neural RF reconstruction model with the state-of-the-art methods in the field of RF sensing, and evaluate the robustness of our model under different types of occlusions and environments.
COST: 130 GPU-hours (increased due to the additional complexities)
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement in accuracy and robustness of our revised neural RF reconstruction model, especially for objects hidden behind occlusions, but may encounter difficulties in interpreting the results of the depth-wise separable convolution technique.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Experimental Evaluation and Benchmarking of RF Reconstruction Methods on Real-World Datasets
PROPOSAL: We will collect and preprocess real-world mmWave radar datasets from various sources, including the 4DCT radar dataset, the Part-A11 dataset, and custom datasets collected using dedicated hardware. We will then evaluate and benchmark the performance of the existing neural RF reconstruction model, RF-ReID, and other state-of-the-art methods using these real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the different methods under various conditions, such as different types of occlusions, clutter, and environments, and evaluate the robustness and accuracy of each method.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (estimated due to the large-scale experiment)
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement in performance and robustness of the RF reconstruction methods with our proposed experimental evaluation and benchmarking, and may identify potential areas for further improvement.

propositions.prediction: We expect to see significant improvement in accuracy and robustness of our revised physics-guided neural network model, especially for through-occlusion imaging scenarios, but may encounter difficulties in accurately characterizing the physical effects of surface roughness and gpointer layers.
propositions.texte: We will design and train a physics-guided neural network to model the reflection responses of surfaces under mmWave radar illumination, accounting for the effects of surface roughness and gpointer layers, and integrate it into a scene reconstruction framework. We will validate this approach using simulations with ground truth and real-world mmWave radar data from the 4DCT radar dataset, aiming to reduce the hardness of the challenging through-occlusion imaging scenarios.
propositions.titre: Physics-Guided Neural Network Modeling for RF Reflection Simulations (Revised)

propositions.controles: We will compare the performance of RF-ReID with state-of-the-art object identification and reconstruction methods in the field of computer vision and RF sensing, and evaluate the robustness of RF-ReID under different types of occlusions and environments.
propositions.prediction: We expect to see significant improvement in object identification and reconstruction accuracy with RF-ReID, especially for objects hidden behind occlusions, but may encounter difficulties in collecting and annotating large-scale RF datasets.
propositions.texte: We will develop a novel RF-based object identification and reconstruction framework (RF-ReID), which leverages the fingerprints of the RF signals to identify and reconstruct the 3D geometry of objects in a real-world scenario. RF-ReID will involve an encoder-decoder architecture that combines a modified version of the existing neural RF reconstruction model with a lightweight, convolutional neural network (CNN) that learns to identify the RF signatures of specific objects.
propositions.titre: RF-ReID: A Novel Framework for RF-Based Object Identification and Reconstruction

propositions.controles: We will compare the performance of our proposed approach with existing methods for self-interference removal and evaluate its impact on the performance of the existing neural RF reconstruction model and RF-ReID framework.
propositions.prediction: We expect to see significant improvement in accuracy and robustness of RF reconstruction methods with our proposed approach, especially for objects hidden behind occlusions, but may encounter difficulties in collecting and annotating large-scale RF datasets.
propositions.texte: We will propose and train a neural network to remove self-interference in RF signals, which can lead to significant improvements in accuracy and robustness of RF reconstruction methods. The neural network will learn to identify and eliminate self-interference patterns in the RF signals by analyzing the correlation between temporally adjacent measurements.
propositions.titre: Learning to Remove Self-Interference in RF Signals for Improved Reconstruction

propositions.controles: We will compare the performance of the pre-trained model with a model trained from scratch on an indoor dataset, and evaluate the effectiveness of transfer learning in adapting to indoor environments.
propositions.prediction: We expect to see significant improvement in performance of RF sensor systems in indoor scenarios with our proposed approach, especially for RF-ReID and RF reconstruction, but may encounter difficulties in selecting the most suitable pre-trained model and fine-tuning schedule.
propositions.texte: We will explore the use of transfer learning to leverage the performance of RF sensor systems in outdoor environments for improved performance in indoor scenarios. We will train and fine-tune a pre-trained neural RF reconstruction model on a large-scale outdoor dataset, and then apply it to indoor scenarios to evaluate its performance.
propositions.titre: Transfer Learning for RF Sensor Systems: Leveraging Outdoor Environments for Enhanced Performance in Indoor Scenarios

propositions.controles: We will compare the performance of the different methods under various conditions, such as different types of occlusions, clutter, and environments, and evaluate the robustness and accuracy of each method.
propositions.cout_texte: 200 GPU-hours (estimated due to the large-scale experiment)
propositions.prediction: We expect to see significant improvement in performance and robustness of the RF reconstruction methods with our proposed experimental evaluation and benchmarking, and may identify potential areas for further improvement.
propositions.texte: We will collect and preprocess real-world mmWave radar datasets from various sources, including the 4DCT radar dataset, the Part-A11 dataset, and custom datasets collected using dedicated hardware. We will then evaluate and benchmark the performance of the existing neural RF reconstruction model, RF-ReID, and other state-of-the-art methods using these real-world datasets.
propositions.titre: Experimental Evaluation and Benchmarking of RF Reconstruction Methods on Real-World Datasets

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Zero- Variance Prompts for Policy Optimization
PROPOSAL: Experimentally compare the reasoning performance and stability of a policy trained on real-world data using a standard Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) approach that filters out zero-variance prompts vs. an alternative approach that extracts feedback from these prompts by leveraging a knowledge-rich auxiliary model (e.g., a pre-trained robust language model) to generate contrastive responses to the noisier rollouts, thereby creating a balanced and informative set of advantages.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard GRPO with filtered zero-variance prompts, Ablation: Remove the auxiliary model and rely solely on the original rollouts.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (main experiments) + 10 GPU-hours (auxiliary model training and validation)
PREDICTION: Expected result: The proposed approach will significantly improve the reasoning performance and stability compared to the baseline, mainly because the generated contrastive responses will provide valuable information for the policy optimization process. Potential failure: Over-reliance on the auxiliary model might lead to biased or inaccurate feedback, causing unstable training or poor generalization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring Zero-Variance Prompt Frequency and Comparison Domains
PROPOSAL: Collect a large dataset of real-world prompts used in the GRPO process and categorize them based on whether they contain zero-variance or non-zero-variance prompts for each of the five competition-level mathematical problem solving, code generation, graduate-level science question answering, multi-subject knowledge question answering, and logical deduction and formal fallacy detection domains.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 50 GPU-hours (data collection and labeling)
PREDICTION: Expected result: The zero-variance prompt frequency will vary significantly across domains and will be higher in domains like code generation and lower in domains like logical deduction. This analysis will help identify which domains can benefit the most from the proposed approach in Investigating Zero-Variance Prompts for Policy Optimization.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Enhanced Zero-Variance Prompt Feedback Formulation
PROPOSAL: Revision of Investigating Zero- Variance Prompts for Policy Optimization: Use the insights from Measuring Zero-Variance Prompt Frequency and Comparison Domains to formulate a more tailored feedback approach for zero-variance prompts. Specifically, introduce a domain-agnostic and prompt-specific auxiliary model that adjusts the contrastive response generation method to produce more informative advantages. This approach will leverage domain-aware embeddings and zero-shot transfer learning to adapt to the diverse characteristics of different zero-variance prompts.
CONTROLS: Previous controls remain applicable, with the additional requirement to vary the domain-aware embeddings' incorporation.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (main experiments and auxiliary model retraining)
PREDICTION: Expected result: The revised feedback formulation will demonstrate improved reasoning performance and stability compared to the original Investigating Zero- Variance Prompts for Policy Optimization, particularly in domains where zero-variance prompts are more prevalent.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating Zero- Variance Prompts for Policy Optimization
PROPOSAL: Use a combination of techniques to extract informative feedback from zero-variance prompts, including contrastive response generation with a knowledge-rich auxiliary model (e.g., a pre-trained robust language model) and domain-aware embeddings. To further enhance the feedback signal, leverage knowledge distillation to transfer the knowledge from the auxiliary model to the policy model itself, allowing it to generate better responses even when provided with noisier rollouts.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard GRPO with filtered zero-variance prompts, Ablation: Remove the knowledge distillation step, Baseline with enhanced auxiliary model training: Standard GRPO with the same auxiliary model used for response generation.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (main experiments, auxiliary model training, and knowledge distillation)
PREDICTION: Expected result: The enhanced policy will demonstrate improved reasoning performance and stability compared to the baseline, while the ablated version will confirm the importance of knowledge distillation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Over-Smoothing Countermeasures for Zero-Variance Prompts
PROPOSAL: Investigate potential countermeasures to mitigate the effects of over-smoothing that can occur when relying solely on informative feedback from zero-variance prompts. This can be achieved by integrating a regularization term into the policy loss function that encourages the policy to generate diverse responses even when presented with a completely accurate or completely incorrect group of rollouts. Additionally, explore techniques that artificially introduce limited noise to the rollouts to create heterogeneity within the group and encourage more robust learning.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard GRPO with filtered zero-variance prompts, Negative control: Removing the regularization term or constant noise introduction.
COST: 120 GPU-hours (main experiments and hyperparameter tuning)
PREDICTION: Expected result: The countermeasures will help mitigate over-smoothing effects and contribute to more stable and robust policy learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Zero-Variance Prompt Invariant Regularization
PROPOSAL: Introduce a regularization term that penalizes the policy for making predictions that rely heavily on the specific characteristics of zero-variance prompts. This can be achieved by minimizing the mutual information between the policy's predictions and the properties of the zero-variance prompts. By doing so, the policy will learn to generate answers that are robust to the distribution of zero-variance prompts and less prone to over-smoothing.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard GRPO with filtered zero-variance prompts, Ablation: Removing the regularizer that targets zero-variance prompts, Comparison to existing stabilization techniques.
COST: 180 GPU-hours (main experiments and regularization term tuning)
PREDICTION: Expected result: The proposed regularization will improve policy robustness and reduce over-smoothing effects caused by zero-variance prompts, potentially leading to better performance on a variety of reasoning tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Prompt Filtering with Variance-Based Thresholding
PROPOSAL: Develop a dynamic filtering approach that selects zero-variance prompts based on their variance within a group, focusing on the most informative ones that are closest to the edge between completely accurate and completely incorrect responses. This can be achieved by introducing a variance-based threshold and adaptively adjusting it during training to maximize the policy's learning signal while minimizing noise. Comparative experiments will be conducted against a non-adaptive approach that relies on a static threshold.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard GRPO with filtered zero-variance prompts, Ablation: Using a non-adaptive and fixed variance threshold.
COST: 160 GPU-hours (main experiments and threshold tuning)
PREDICTION: Expected result: The proposed adaptive filtering will better balance informativeness and noise reduction, contributing to improved policy generalization and efficiency in leveraging zero-variance prompts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Zero-Variance Prompt Datasets for Dataset-Augmented Training
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of using zero-variance prompts as an additional training dataset for the policy model. This will involve creating a new dataset consisting only of zero-variance prompts and their associated rewards, augmenting the existing pool of training data by conditioning the policy on this separate dataset and evaluating its impact on performance.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard GRPO with filtered zero-variance prompts, Comparison to using mini-batches with zero-variance prompts as the only labeled examples, Evaluation on downstream tasks (e.g., multi-subject knowledge question answering, logical deduction).
COST: 220 GPU-hours (creating and training the augmented dataset, policy updates)
PREDICTION: Expected result: The augmented dataset will enable the policy model to learn more effectively from zero-variance prompts, which can then aid in solving more challenging and diverse tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Knowledge Distillation for Zero-Variance Prompt Ensembles
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of knowledge distillation to combine the strengths of multiple models trained on different subsets of zero-variance prompts, with the goal of creating ensembles that can generalize better to a wider range of tasks and conditions. This approach will involve selecting a set of zero-variance prompts, training separate models on each subset, and then distilling knowledge from the individual models into a single ensemble model.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard GRPO with filtered zero-variance prompts, Comparison to using multiple models with different parameterizations and training objectives.
COST: 280 GPU-hours (training separate models and knowledge distillation)
PREDICTION: Expected result: The ensemble model will demonstrate improved generalization and robustness by capturing a broader range of relationships and patterns within zero-variance prompts, making it a promising approach for tackling a variety of challenging tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Synthesizing Key Findings and Future Directions for Improving Zero-Variance Prompt Analysis
PROPOSAL: Integrate and synthesize the insights from the previous experiments, highlighting key lessons learned, best practices, and open challenges related to effectively leveraging zero-variance prompts for policy optimization and reasoning tasks. The report will also outline a set of future research directions aimed at further improving understanding and utility of zero-variance prompts, including investigation of new distillation methods, judicious use of auxiliary models and control variates, and exploration of reduced computational alternatives for modeling training- and inference-time zero-variance prompt indicators.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 0 GPU-hours (this proposal is a qualitative synthesis)
PREDICTION: This report will serve as a comprehensive guide for researchers and practitioners looking to tackle challenging reasoning tasks by more effectively harnessing the valuable information contained within zero-variance prompts.
