ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Unsupervised Learning for Denoising and Normalizing the FACS Parameter Space
PROPOSAL: Introduce an unsupervised learning stage to our rigging pipeline, where we use autoencoders to denoise and normalize the FACS parameter space. Specifically, train a conditional VaDE ( Conditional Variational Autoencoder with Disentangled Embeddings) model on our dataset of FACS parameterizations, and then use the learned embedding space to denoise and normalize the parameters. This step should help to reduce the redundancy in the FACS parameter space and improve the robustness of our rigging model.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained without the unsupervised learning stage.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours (~2 weeks on a single NVIDIA V100)
PREDICTION: Our unsupervised learning stage should improve the robustness of our rigging model, especially for difficult cases where the input FACS parameterization has high noise or outliers.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Transfer Learning for FACS-Based Facial Rigging Across Different Face Variations
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of transfer learning to adapt our FACS-based facial rigging model to different face variations, such as age groups, gender, or ethnicities. Specifically, train a backbone model on a large dataset of FACS parameterizations from a specific face variation, and then fine-tune it on a smaller dataset from another face variation. We will also explore using a multi-task learning approach to learn both the rigging task and the facial variation classification task simultaneously.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained from scratch on each face variation individually.
COST: 4000 GPU-hours (~4 weeks on a single NVIDIA V100)
PREDICTION: Our transfer learning approach should improve the robustness of our model across different face variations, especially when the variation is only slight. However, we may face challenges when adapting to face variations with large differences in morphology or expression.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Real-World Evaluation of FACS-Based Facial Rigging in 3D Avatars and Characters
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of our FACS-based facial rigging model on a real-world dataset of 3D avatars and characters, with a focus on its ability to produce realistic and expressive facial animations. We will collect a dataset of 3D avatars and characters with high-quality FACS parameterizations, and then compare the performance of our model against state-of-the-art methods in the field.
CONTROLS: Compare against the industry-standard FACS-based facial rigging software, FaceFX.
COST: 6000 GPU-hours (~6 weeks on a single NVIDIA V100)
PREDICTION: Our model should show strong performance in producing realistic and expressive facial animations, especially in comparison to the industry-standard software. However, we may face challenges in accurately capturing the nuances of human facial expressions, particularly in subtle or complex animations.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Enhancing FACS-Based Facial Rigging with Physiological Constraints and Real-World Feedback
PROPOSAL: Integrate physiological constraints, such as muscle anatomy and physiology, into our FACS-based facial rigging model to improve its accuracy and realism. We will also incorporate real-world feedback from users, such as human evaluators or commercial software, to fine-tune our model and ensure it meets the needs of real-world applications.
CONTROLS: Compare against a version of our model without physiological constraints and real-world feedback.
COST: 8000 GPU-hours (~8 weeks on a single NVIDIA V100)
PREDICTION: Our enhanced model should significantly improve the accuracy and realism of FACS-based facial rigging, and also improve its adaptability to real-world applications and user needs.

Investigate the use of transfer learning to adapt our FACS-based facial rigging model to different face variations, such as age groups, gender, or ethnicities. Specifically, train a backbone model on a large dataset of FACS parameterizations from a specific face variation, and then fine-tune it on a smaller dataset from another face variation. We will also explore using a multi-task learning approach to learn both the rigging task and the facial variation classification task simultaneously.

PROPOSAL 7: Real-World Evaluation of FACS-Based Facial Rigging in 3D Avatars and Characters
Evaluate the performance of our FACS-based facial rigging model on a real-world dataset of 3D avatars and characters, with a focus on its ability to produce realistic and expressive facial animations. Integrate physiological constraints, such as muscle anatomy and physiology, into our FACS-based facial rigging model to improve its accuracy and realism. actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direct FACS-based Facial Rigging using Conditional Normalizing Flows
PROPOSAL: Train a conditional normalizing flow (CNF) model to generate FACS blendshape weights for a given facial expression, utilizing a pre-trained 3D face geometry estimation model as the base feature extractor. The CNF will learn a probabilistic mapping from the input image to the latent blendshape parameters, allowing to generate a variety of facial expressions on a target neutral mesh. For datasets, use the recently collected Blender-FACS benchmark for rigging, alongside the notable 3DMM-FACS dataset. Evaluate performance using metrics such as mean squared error and expression quality scores.
CONTROLS: Train the model using a simplified FACS blendshape rig (e.g., only 8 action units) for initial ablation study and compare results against a strong baseline, e.g., NFR.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The CNF model should be capable of generating realistic and diversified facial expressions on a target mesh, but may struggle with certain challenging cases like mouths and eyes, which often require detailed manual corrections in,’

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Component Fusion Network for Joint Facial Animation
PROPOSAL: Design a multi-component fusion network (MCFN) that integrates feature maps from multiple light-weight neural networks, each specializing in learning the animation patterns for a specific facial component (e.g., eyes, eyebrows, nose, lips, etc.). The MCFN will utilize the attention mechanism to adaptively weight the learned features from each component network based on the input expression. Implement this using a capsule network architecture to learn the semantic representation of facial components. For training, leverage the detailed mesh annotation data available in numerous real-world facial expression capture datasets such as "BJUT 3D-FE" and evaluate using standard metrics like facial expression recognition accuracy.
CONTROLS: As a baseline comparison, utilize a standard but simplified 3D-representation-based- network, such as,  Baseline1 – Volume Registration with auc, or Baseline2 - Condition Non Volume Displacement and ms-ssim and a-hop statistics to test to its performance variability. 

COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The MCFN should be able to animate multiple facial components in a coordinated and realistic manner, with better performance particularly in animating facial areas such as eyes and lips where a lot of detailed manual corrections occur in many 3D facial animation systems

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Direct FACS-based Facial Rigging using Conditional Normalizing Flows
PROPOSAL: REVISED: Update the CNF model's input feature extractor to include a new module that estimates the wires of the neutral mesh, followed by a mesh transformer to align the target mesh features with the template mesh features used in NFR.  Expand the NFR architecture by adding self-attention to facilitate adaptive information exchange and aggregation of the generated 3D mesh features, allowing it to learn a more transferable latent space that abstracts the shape and appearance characteristics common across different facial shapes, thus enhancing its ability to generalize across in-the-wild facial shapes. Finally, re-implement and fine-tune NFR to be trained on and fit the templates and Sample Baidu, to attain performance gains against existing results
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the revised CNF model against its original architecture, and study the effect of different training strategies, data augmentation methods, and hyperparameter tuning in achieving the desired generalization across different facial shapes.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The updated CNF model will significantly improve its rigging quality and robustness, as it effectively leverages both the NFR template and the CNF probabilistic mapping capabilities to achieve high-quality output, however, additional methods may still be necessary for fine-tuning animations of challenging subjects such as  minor hands or mouths and angry (or old) faces, which require movement of detailed facial parts’ extreme skin distension and exhaustive updates

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mesh-to-Mesh Neural Rendering for Direct FACS-based Facial Rigging
PROPOSAL: Train a mesh-to-mesh neural rendering (MMNR) model that directly maps a given facial expression image to a rigged facial mesh, leveraging a neural rendering framework that can efficiently handle the geometry and appearance of a 3D facial mesh. The MMNR model will be trained on a diverse set of facial expression images and their corresponding rigged meshes, allowing it to learn a direct mapping between the input image and the FACS blendshape weights. Use this model as a post-processing step to refine the output of the CNF model, enhancing its rigging quality and realism.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the MMNR model's performance on a variety of facial expressions and mesh topologies, and study its ability to transfer its learned mapping to novel facial shapes and styles.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The MMNR model will significantly improve the rigging quality and realism of the CNF model, particularly for highly detailed and realistic facial expressions, but may require additional fine-tuning to adjust to diverse and nuanced facial movements, such as subtle eye blinks or nuanced muscle contractions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamically-Constrained Facial Rigging via Anisotropic Total Variation Regularization
PROPOSAL: Formulate a novel optimization problem for facial rigging that incorporates anisotropic total variation regularization (ATVR) to impose structural constraints on the FACS blendshape weights, ensuring that the resulting animation is both physically plausible and aesthetically pleasing. The ATVR term will be designed to favor smooth and consistent movements of the facial muscles, while also allowing for abrupt changes and high-frequency oscillations in regions with complex facial anatomy. Implement this using an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) framework to efficiently solve the optimization problem.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the ATVR-based facial rigging method on a variety of facial expressions and mesh topologies, and compare its results against those obtained using traditional L1/L2 regularization methods.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The ATVR-based facial rigging method will provide high-quality and realistic results, especially for facial expressions with high spatial frequencies, but may require careful tuning of its regularization parameters to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than other methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Consistency Enforcement for Facial Animation using Graph Convolutional Networks
PROPOSAL: Design a graph convolutional network (GCN) model that takes the facial animation sequence as input and predicts a set of temporal consistency scores for each frame, measuring the likelihood of smooth and coherent animation. The GCN model will be trained to minimize the temporal inconsistency errors between adjacent frames, using a contrastive loss function that encourages the model to identify and correct temporal inconsistencies. Integrate this model into the existing facial rigging pipeline to enforce temporal consistency and improve overall animation quality.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the GCN-based temporal consistency enforcement method on a variety of facial animation sequences, and compare its results against those obtained using traditional motion smoothing techniques.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The GCN-based temporal consistency enforcement method will effectively improve the smoothness and coherence of facial animations, especially for complex and dynamic facial expressions, but may require careful tuning of its hyperparameters to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than traditional motion smoothing methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Viewpoint-Invariant Facial Rigging using 3D Pose-Aware Embeddings
PROPOSAL: Develop a methodology that generates a 3D pose-aware embedding for each facial expression, which encodes the intrinsic properties of the face that are viewpoint-invariant. Utilize this embedding to perform viewpoint-invariant facial rigging, allowing the model to generate high-quality facial animations from a variety of viewpoints. Train the model on a diverse dataset of facial expressions and viewpoints, and evaluate its performance using standard metrics such as facial expression recognition accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the viewpoint-invariant facial rigging method against traditional methods that rely on viewpoint-specific parameterizations.
COST: 90 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The viewpoint-invariant facial rigging method will effectively improve the robustness and generality of facial animations, especially for applications that require animation from multiple viewpoints, but may require careful tuning of its embedding architecture to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than traditional methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data-Efficient Facial Rigging via Meta-Learning with Few-Shot Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop a meta-learning approach for facial rigging, which learns to adapt to new facial expressions with minimal data. Utilize a few-shot learning framework, where the model is trained on a small set of examples and must generalize to novel facial expressions. The model will be trained on a diverse set of facial expressions and will learn to transfer its knowledge to new expressions with minimal supervision. Evaluate the performance of the meta-learning approach using standard metrics such as facial expression recognition accuracy and FACS-weight prediction accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the meta-learning approach against traditional few-shot learning methods, and evaluate its ability to adapt to new facial expressions with varying levels of data availability.
COST: 110 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The meta-learning approach for facial rigging will effectively improve the data efficiency and adaptability of the model, especially for applications with limited data availability, but may require careful tuning of its hyperparameters to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than traditional methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Autoregressive Facial Animation Generation using Normalizing Flows
PROPOSAL: Develop an autoregressive approach for facial animation generation using normalizing flows, where the model generates a sequence of facial expressions that are conditionally dependent on the previous expressions. Utilize a combination of conditional normalizing flows and autoregressive modeling to capture the temporal dependencies in the facial animation sequence. Train the model on a large dataset of facial animations and evaluate its performance using metrics such as facial expression recognition accuracy and sequence quality metrics.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the autoregressive approach against traditional methods for facial animation generation, and evaluate its ability to capture long-range dependencies in the facial animation sequence.
COST: 130 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The autoregressive approach for facial animation generation will effectively capture the temporal dependencies in the facial animation sequence, resulting in high-quality and realistic animations, but may require careful tuning of its hyperparameters to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than traditional methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: End-to-End Facial Animation System with Human Oversight and Feedback
PROPOSAL: Develop an end-to-end facial animation system that integrates all previous models and techniques, allowing for fully automated facial animation generation with human oversight and feedback. The system will take a static 3D facial mesh as input and produce a dynamic and realistic facial animation, while allowing human animators to provide feedback and correct errors. Utilize a reinforcement learning framework to optimize the animation quality and ensure that the system adapts to the animator's preferences.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the end-to-end facial animation system using metrics such as animation quality, realism, and animator efficiency, and compare its results against those obtained using traditional facial animation techniques.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The end-to-end facial animation system will provide a robust and flexible solution for facial animation generation, allowing for efficient and high-quality animation production, but may require significant computational resources and human effort to fine-tune and optimize its performance.

The MMNR model will be trained on a diverse set of facial expression images and their corresponding rigged meshes, allowing it to learn a direct mapping between the input image and the FACS blendshape weights. Use this model as a post-processing step to refine the output of the CNF model, enhancing its rigging quality and realism.
propositions.titre: Mesh-to-Mesh Neural Rendering for Direct FACS-based Facial Rigging

propositions.controles: Evaluate the performance of the ATVR-based facial rigging method on a variety of facial expressions and mesh topologies, and compare its results against those obtained using traditional L1/L2 regularization methods.
propositions.prediction: The ATVR-based facial rigging method will provide high-quality and realistic results, especially for facial expressions with high spatial frequencies, but may require careful tuning of its regularization parameters to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than other methods.
propositions.texte: Formulate a novel optimization problem for facial rigging that incorporates anisotropic total variation regularization (ATVR) to impose structural constraints on the FACS blendshape weights, ensuring that the resulting animation is both physically plausible and aesthetically pleasing. The ATVR term will be designed to favor smooth and consistent movements of the facial muscles, while also allowing for abrupt changes and high-frequency oscillations in regions with complex facial anatomy. Implement this using an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) framework to efficiently solve the optimization problem.
propositions.titre: Dynamically-Constrained Facial Rigging via Anisotropic Total Variation Regularization

propositions.controles: Evaluate the performance of the GCN-based temporal consistency enforcement method on a variety of facial animation sequences, and compare its results against those obtained using traditional motion smoothing techniques.
propositions.prediction: The GCN-based temporal consistency enforcement method will effectively improve the smoothness and coherence of facial animations, especially for complex and dynamic facial expressions, but may require careful tuning of its hyperparameters to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than traditional motion smoothing methods.
propositions.texte: Design a graph convolutional network (GCN) model that takes the facial animation sequence as input and predicts a set of temporal consistency scores for each frame, measuring the likelihood of smooth and coherent animation. The GCN model will be trained to minimize the temporal inconsistency errors between adjacent frames, using a contrastive loss function that encourages the model to identify and correct temporal inconsistencies. Integrate this model into the existing facial rigging pipeline to enforce temporal consistency and improve overall animation quality.
propositions.titre: Temporal Consistency Enforcement for Facial Animation using Graph Convolutional Networks

propositions.controles: Compare the performance of the viewpoint-invariant facial rigging method against traditional methods that rely on viewpoint-specific parameterizations.
propositions.prediction: The viewpoint-invariant facial rigging method will effectively improve the robustness and generality of facial animations, especially for applications that require animation from multiple viewpoints, but may require careful tuning of its embedding architecture to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than traditional methods.
propositions.texte: Develop a methodology that generates a 3D pose-aware embedding for each facial expression, which encodes the intrinsic properties of the face that are viewpoint-invariant. Utilize this embedding to perform viewpoint-invariant facial rigging, allowing the model to generate high-quality facial animations from a variety of viewpoints. Train the model on a diverse dataset of facial expressions and viewpoints, and evaluate its performance using standard metrics such as facial expression recognition accuracy.
propositions.titre: Viewpoint-Invariant Facial Rigging using 3D Pose-Aware Embeddings

propositions.controles: Compare the performance of the meta-learning approach against traditional few-shot learning methods, and evaluate its ability to adapt to new facial expressions with varying levels of data availability.
propositions.prediction: The meta-learning approach for facial rigging will effectively improve the data efficiency and adaptability of the model, especially for applications with limited data availability, but may require careful tuning of its hyperparameters to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than traditional methods.
propositions.texte: Develop a meta-learning approach for facial rigging, which learns to adapt to new facial expressions with minimal data. Utilize a few-shot learning framework, where the model is trained on a small set of examples and must generalize to novel facial expressions. The model will be trained on a diverse set of facial expressions and will learn to transfer its knowledge to new expressions with minimal supervision. Evaluate the performance of the meta-learning approach using standard metrics such as facial expression recognition accuracy and FACS-weight prediction accuracy.
propositions.titre: Data-Efficient Facial Rigging via Meta-Learning with Few-Shot Learning

propositions.controles: Compare the performance of the autoregressive approach against traditional methods for facial animation generation, and evaluate its ability to capture long-range dependencies in the facial animation sequence.
propositions.prediction: The autoregressive approach for facial animation generation will effectively capture the temporal dependencies in the facial animation sequence, resulting in high-quality and realistic animations, but may require careful tuning of its hyperparameters to achieve optimal results, and its computational complexity may be higher than traditional methods.
propositions.texte: Develop an autoregressive approach for facial animation generation using normalizing flows, where the model generates a sequence of facial expressions that are conditionally dependent on the previous expressions. Utilize a combination of conditional normalizing flows and autoregressive modeling to capture the temporal dependencies in the facial animation sequence. Train the model on a large dataset of facial animations and evaluate its performance using metrics such as facial expression recognition accuracy and sequence quality metrics.
propositions.titre: Autoregressive Facial Animation Generation using Normalizing Flows

propositions.controles: Evaluate the performance of the end-to-end facial animation system using metrics such as animation quality, realism, and animator efficiency, and compare its results against those obtained using traditional facial animation techniques.
propositions.prediction: The end-to-end facial animation system will provide a robust and flexible solution for facial animation generation, allowing for efficient and high-quality animation production, but may require significant computational resources and human effort to fine-tune and optimize its performance.
propositions.texte: Develop an end-to-end facial animation system that integrates all previous models and techniques, allowing for fully automated facial animation generation with human oversight and feedback. The system will take a static 3D facial mesh as input and produce a dynamic and realistic facial animation, while allowing human animators to provide feedback and correct errors. Utilize a reinforcement learning framework to optimize the animation quality and ensure that the system adapts to the animator's preferences.
propositions.titre: End-to-End Facial Animation System with Human Oversight and Feedback

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Curriculum Learning for Automated FACS-Based Facial Rigging
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel curriculum learning approach, starting with simple expressions and gradually increasing the difficulty of the FACS parameters, to guide the facial rigging model towards learning complex expressions from limited 3D ground truth examples. The curriculum will be designed to include sequences of increasing complexity, such as starting with simple muscular movements and progressing to more complex combinations of movements.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed approach to a traditional teacher-forcing method, where the model is trained on sequences of FACS parameters in a fixed order, and an ablation study without curriculum learning.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed curriculum learning approach should improve the model's generalization ability to complex expressions and increase its robustness to the scarcity of 3D ground truth examples, leading to better performance on the test set, but it may require fine-tuning to achieve better results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Multi-Task Learning for Facial Rigging and Expression Inference
PROPOSAL: We propose an unsupervised multi-task learning framework that jointly learns to predict the FACS parameters and infer the facial expression from a single image. This approach allows the model to leverage additional supervision from expression inference and further improve the facial rigging results. We also release a new dataset of paired images and FACS parameter videos, which will serve as an additional training set for our model.
CONTROLS: We will compare our unsupervised multi-task learning approach to a baseline model trained on FACS prediction only, and an ablation study with and without the expression inference task.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed unsupervised multi-task learning approach should improve the facial rigging results by leveraging the supervision from expression inference, and also enable the model to generalize better to unseen facial expressions. However, the model may be prone to overfitting to the joint task if not properly regularized.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: (Updated) Unsupervised Multi-Task Learning for Facial Rigging and Expression Inference
PROPOSAL: We propose an unsupervised multi-task learning framework that jointly learns to predict the FACS parameters and infer the facial expression from a single image, while utilizing a memory-augmented attention mechanism to selectively focus on the most informative image regions and memory snapshots. This approach allows the model to leverage additional supervision from expression inference, more effectively learn complex facial expressions, and improve the facial rigging results. We also release a new dataset of paired images, FACS parameter videos, and mesh annotations, which will serve as an additional training set for our model.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed unsupervised multi-task learning approach with memory-augmented attention to a baseline model trained on FACS prediction only, and an ablation study with and without the expression inference task, and memory-augmentation.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed unsupervised multi-task learning approach with memory-augmented attention should improve the facial rigging results by leveraging the supervision from expression inference, and also enable the model to generalize better to unseen facial expressions and complex mesh topologies. However, the model may require careful tuning to achieve better results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Augmenting the Dataset with Synthetic Facial Expressions
PROPOSAL: We propose augmenting the existing dataset with synthetic facial expressions generated by a state-of-the-art generative model, such as a GAN or VAE, to increase the diversity and quantity of the training data. This synthetic augmentation can help bridge the gap between the limited existing real-world data and the vast range of possible facial expressions, enabling the model to better generalize to unseen expressions and meshes.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results of our model trained on the augmented dataset to a baseline model trained on the original dataset, and an ablation study with and without the synthetic augmentation.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed dataset augmentation with synthetic facial expressions should improve the model's generalization ability to unseen facial expressions and complex mesh topologies, and reduce overfitting to the limited existing real-world data. However, the quality of the synthetic data may impact the overall performance of the model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: FACS Parameter Augmentation through Hidden Markov Model Analysis
PROPOSAL: We propose using a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to analyze the temporal dynamics of FACS parameter sequences from a large dataset of annotated facial expressions. The learned HMM models can be used to augment the existing FACS parameters with newly generated sequences, capturing the complex temporal patterns and relationships between the FACS parameters. This augmentation can help increase the diversity and expressiveness of the model's output and improve its ability to generalize to unseen facial expressions.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results of our model trained on the augmented dataset with the HMM-augmented FACS parameters to a baseline model trained on the original dataset, and an ablation study with and without the HMM-augmentation.
COST: 75 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed FACS parameter augmentation through HMM analysis should improve the model's ability to learn complex temporal patterns and relationships between the FACS parameters, leading to more expressive and realistic facial expressions. However, the quality of the HMM models and the generated augmented data may impact the overall performance of the model.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: (Updated) Augmenting the Dataset with Synthetic Facial Expressions
PROPOSAL: We propose augmenting the existing dataset with synthetic facial expressions generated by a state-of-the-art generative model, such as a GAN or VAE, to increase the diversity and quantity of the training data. Additionally, we will use the learned FACS parameter sequences from the HMM analysis in step 5 to guide the generative model and improve the quality of the synthetic facial expressions, making them more realistic and diverse. This hybrid approach can help bridge the gap between the limited existing real-world data and the vast range of possible facial expressions, enabling the model to better generalize to unseen expressions and meshes.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results of our model trained on the augmented dataset with the hybrid approach to a baseline model trained on the original dataset, and an ablation study with and without the synthetic augmentation, and without the HMM-augmentation.
COST: 225 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed hybrid dataset augmentation should improve the model's generalization ability to unseen facial expressions and complex mesh topologies, reduce overfitting to the limited existing real-world data, and generate more realistic and diverse synthetic facial expressions. However, the complexity of the hybrid approach may require careful tuning to achieve better results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Camera Facial Rigging with Domain Adaptation
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-camera facial rigging approach that leverages domain adaptation to handle the variability in facial expressions and lighting conditions across different cameras and environments. We will use a clustering-based approach to identify similar domains (e.g., indoor vs. outdoor) and adapt the model to each domain separately, allowing it to learn domain-specific patterns and relationships between the FACS parameters. This approach can help improve the model's performance on unseen cameras and environments.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results of our model trained with domain adaptation to a baseline model trained on a single domain, and an ablation study with and without domain clustering.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed multi-camera facial rigging with domain adaptation should improve the model's performance on unseen cameras and environments, and enable it to generalize better to a wide range of facial expressions and lighting conditions. However, the effectiveness of domain adaptation may depend on the quality of the clustering and the similarity between the domains.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: (Updated) Unsupervised Multi-Task Learning for Facial Rigging and Expression Inference
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel unsupervised multi-task learning framework that jointly learns to predict the FACS parameters, infer the facial expression, and reconstruct the 3D facial mesh from a single image, utilizing a cycle consistent GAN to improve the quality of the generated mesh and expression. This framework can help the model learn a more nuanced understanding of the relationship between the FACS parameters, facial expressions, and 3D facial mesh, leading to more accurate and realistic facial rigging results.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results of our proposed framework to a baseline model trained on a single task (FACS prediction), and an ablation study with and without the cycle consistent GAN and mesh reconstruction.
COST: 350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed unsupervised multi-task learning framework with cycle consistent GAN and mesh reconstruction should improve the model's ability to learn a nuanced understanding of the relationship between the FACS parameters, facial expressions, and 3D facial mesh, leading to more accurate and realistic facial rigging results. However, the computational cost and training time may be increased due to the additional tasks and modules.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation of Facial Rigging Models on Real-World Datasets
PROPOSAL: We propose evaluating the performance of the previously proposed facial rigging models on real-world datasets, including the FACS EGG (a dataset of facial expressions labeled with FACS codes) and the YouTube Faces database (a dataset of videos of faces in the wild). This evaluation will assess the models' ability to generalize to real-world facial expressions and variations in lighting, pose, and age.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results of the proposed models to a baseline model trained on a synthetic dataset, and an ablation study with and without the real-world dataset.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed evaluation on real-world datasets should help identify the strengths and limitations of the proposed facial rigging models, and provide a more realistic assessment of their performance in practical applications. However, the performance of the models may be affected by the variability and complexity of the real-world data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablation Study and Model Selection for Real-World Applications
PROPOSAL: We propose conducting an ablation study to compare the performance of the proposed facial rigging models on real-world datasets, and select the best-performing model for real-world applications. This study will involve ablation of individual components, such as the curriculum learning, multi-task learning, and domain adaptation, to understand their contributions to the overall performance. We will also evaluate the selected model on a real-world avatar animation task, such as creating a 3D face animation from a user-specified FACS code.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results of the proposed models to a baseline model trained on a synthetic dataset, and an ablation study with and without the individual components.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed ablation study and model selection should help identify the most effective facial rigging approach for real-world applications, and demonstrate its performance on a practical avatar animation task. However, the selection of the best-performing model may depend on the specific requirements and constraints of the real-world application.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Modality Imbalance in Decision-Level Fusion: A Baseline Study
PROPOSAL: Experiment (Abi-WAE) - Train a set of modality-specific predictors (e.g., VGG16 for images, LSTM for text) on a diverse set of benchmark datasets (e.g., food classification, sentiment analysis), and apply a static late fusion strategy to combine their outputs. We will evaluate the accuracy of each individual modality and the fused decision, and compare them to the unimodal performance of a strong predictor specifically trained for each task. We also collect correlation coefficients between the fused predictions and individual modalities to assess the level of modality imbalance. Controls include ablations of the late fusion strategy (e.g., no fusion, equal weights, dynamic weights) and comparisons to a simple majority voting baseline.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (approximately 2-3 days on a moderate-sized cluster)
PREDICTION: We expect to observe significant modality imbalance in the fused decisions, with a few dominant modalities overpowering others. Ablations will reveal the impact of the late fusion strategy on modality strength. 

This baseline study aims to establish a fundamental understanding of modality imbalance in decision-level fusion and serves as a foundation for future experiments. We expect it to reveal which modalities are consistently strong or weak, which can inform the design of subsequent modifications to alleviate imbalance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decoupling Modality Influence in Late Fusion with Balance-Weighted Decisions
PROPOSAL: Experiment (BWD) - Introduce a new late fusion strategy that weights each modality's contribution inversely proportional to its Van der Waals coefficient (VWC), which measures the strength of the interaction between a modality and the model's output. This balance-weighted decision-making mechanism discourages over-influence from strong modalities and compensates for the underperformance of weak ones. We will experiment with various weight initialization schemes and compare the performance of BWD against the baseline static late fusion and other state-of-the-art fusion strategies (e.g., adaptive ensembling, confidence-based weighting).
CONTROLS: Ablation study of different weight initialization schemes, comparison to a fusion strategy that incorporates uncertainty estimates from individual modalities, and a control experiment that uses random weights for each modality.
COST: 300 GPU-hours (approximately 5-6 days on a moderate-sized cluster)
PREDICTION: We expect the BWD strategy to mitigate modality imbalance and improve the robustness of the fused decision, while potentially suffering from a slight decrease in overall accuracy due to the intrinsic trade-offs between balance and high-performance moderate fusion strategies

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Not changing the title

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Alleviating Modality Imbalance with Reward-Shaping
PROPOSAL:  Design a decision-level fusion system where the latent features of the dominant and weak modalities are mapped to a shared space, and then align the features of the weak modality to the decision boundary of the dominant modality, but with a twist. By adding a reward-shaping term to the loss function that encourages the weak modality to maintain its original feature distribution, we can prevent over-alignment and preserve the unique information encoded in the weak modality.
CONTROLS: Compare to a baseline late fusion approach without the reward-shaping term, and an ensemble-based method where the predictions of the weak and dominant modalities are aggregated with equal weights. 
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will improve the performance of the weak modality without affecting the dominant modality, and the robustness of the system will increase as a result. However, this approach may not be effective for very large datasets where the hyperparameters of the reward-shaping term may be difficult to tune, and it may require more computational resources than other methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Modality Strength through Exploratory Feature Loss
PROPOSAL:  Introduce an exploratory feature loss that measures the amount of redundant or irrelevant information that a modality is providing. This loss function is calculated based on the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the feature distributions of the modality and a set of baseline features. By incorporating this loss into the training process, we can determine the strength of each modality and balance their contributions to the final decision.
CONTROLS: Compare to a baseline where all modalities are given equal importance, and an approach where unimodal accuracy is used to determine modality strength but without feature-level compensation or cross-modal interaction.
COST: 8 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method will be able to effectively determine the strength of each modality and improve the performance of the system on real-world datasets. However, the computational cost of calculating the Jensen-Shannon divergence for each modality may be high for very large datasets, and it may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters to achieve good results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Late Fusion through Distributive Preferences
PROPOSAL:  Develop a framework for robust late fusion by assigning a preference distribution to each modality, which describes its relative importance in the decision-making process. The preference distribution of each modality is learned from the data using a distributive loss function, which captures the relationship between the modality's individual predictions and the overall decision. The proposed framework allows for modality-specific preferences and dynamically adjusts the weights assigned to each modality during inference.
CONTROLS: Compare to a static late fusion approach with fixed weights, a dynamic late fusion approach without distributive preferences, and an ensemble-based method where the predictions of the weak and dominant modalities are aggregated with equal weights.
COST: 15 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed framework will significantly improve the robustness of late fusion by adaptively adjusting the weights assigned to each modality during inference, and improve performance on real-world datasets. However, the computational cost of calculating the distributive preferences may be high for very large datasets, and it may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters to achieve good results.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Robust Late Fusion through Distributive Preferences
REVISED PROPOSAL: Revise the framework to incorporate an additional architectural component, a softmax layer, which captures the uncertainty of each modality's predictions. This will help to identify when a modality is uncertain or has low confidence, and dynamically adjust the weights assigned to each modality during inference, improving the overall robustness of the system.
CONTROLS: Same as before, but also compare to a revised baseline where the softmax layer is removed.
COST: Same as before, but due to the added softmax layer, the required computational resources will increase to 18 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: The revised framework will improve the robustness and performance of late fusion on real-world datasets by incorporating uncertainty estimation. However, the additional computational resources required may limit its applicability to very large-scale datasets, and it may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters to achieve good results.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: 1. Alleviating Modality Imbalance with Reward-Shaping
REVISED PROPOSAL: Modify the reward-shaping term in the loss function to use a Wasserstein distance metric, instead of the original Euclidean distance, to capture the complexity of the modality-specific feature distributions. This will provide a more robust and flexible way to encourage the weak modality to maintain its unique feature distribution.
CONTROLS: Compare to the original reward-shaping approach, and an alternative approach that uses a difference of means (DOM) penalty to encourage the weak modality to maintain its feature distribution.
COST: 12 GPU-hours (twice the original estimate, due to the computational cost of the Wasserstein distance metric)
PREDICTION: The revised reward-shaping term will improve the robustness and performance of the system, but its implementation may require careful tuning of hyperparameters, and the increased computational resources may limit its applicability to very large-scale datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identifying Weak Modalities using Information Theoretic Measures
PROPOSAL:  Develop a framework to identify weak modalities using information theoretic measures, such as the mutual information between the modality's predictions and the overall decision. By using these measures, we can quantify the amount of information that each modality is contributing to the decision-making process and identify the weak modalities that are not providing sufficient information.
CONTROLS: Compare to a baseline where all modalities are given equal importance, and an approach where unimodal accuracy is used to determine modality strength but without feature-level compensation or cross-modal interaction.
COST: 6 GPU-hours (runs on moderate-sized datasets)
PREDICTION: The proposed framework will be able to effectively identify weak modalities and improve the performance of the system on real-world datasets. However, the computational cost of calculating the mutual information between the modality's predictions and the overall decision may be high for very large datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Modality Robustness through Adversarial Training
PROPOSAL:  Introduce an adversarial training module that injects adversarial perturbations into the weak modality's predictions, forcing the system to learn more robust feature representations and improve its generalization capabilities. This will help to address the issue of model brittleness and improve the robustness of the system to adversarial attacks.
CONTROLS: Compare to a baseline where the system is trained without adversarial perturbations, and an approach where the system is robustified using data augmentation techniques.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (requires significant computational resources for adversarial training)
PREDICTION: The proposed framework will enhance modality robustness and improve the overall performance of the system on real-world datasets. However, the increased computational cost may limit its applicability to very large-scale datasets, and the adversarial training module may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve good results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing and Improving Modality Imbalance in Real-World Multimodal Systems
PROPOSAL:  Conduct an extensive analysis of modality imbalance in various real-world multimodal systems, including food classification, social media sentiment analysis, and indoor scene recognition. The analysis will help identify common causes of modality imbalance, such as sensor noise, data quality issues, and domain shift. Additionally, we will propose several improvements to address these issues and improve the overall performance of multimodal systems.
CONTROLS: Compare to state-of-the-art methods and benchmarks in each of the analyzed application domains.
COST: 30 GPU-hours (requires significant computational resources for analysis and benchmarking)
PREDICTION: The proposed analysis will provide valuable insights into the causes of modality imbalance and suggest practical solutions to improve the performance of multimodal systems. However, the analysis may require significant manual effort and the improvements may not be universally applicable across all domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Theoretical Framework for Modality Imbalance and Its Mitigation Strategies
PROPOSAL:  Develop a theoretical framework that formalizes the concept of modality imbalance and its effects on multimodal systems. The framework will establish the relationship between modality imbalance, robustness, and performance and derive a set of bounds on the performance of multimodal systems. We will also use this framework to analyze and compare the proposed mitigation strategies, such as reward-shaping, exploratory feature loss, and robust late fusion, and derive guarantees on their effectiveness.
CONTROLS: Compare to existing theoretical frameworks for robustness and multimodal systems.
COST: 0 GPU-hours (purely theoretical work)
PREDICTION: The proposed theoretical framework will provide a comprehensive understanding of modality imbalance and its mitigation strategies, and derive guarantees on their effectiveness. However, the framework may not capture all the nuances of real-world multimodal systems, and its applicability may be limited to specific domains or scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Validation of the Theoretical Framework
PROPOSAL:  Use the theoretical framework developed in proposal 7 to derive specific mitigation strategies for modality imbalance, and experimentally validate their effectiveness on a set of benchmark multimodal datasets. We will also compare the proposed mitigation strategies to existing approaches and evaluate their performance using a range of metrics, including accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.
CONTROLS: Compare to state-of-the-art methods and benchmarks in multimodal systems.
COST: 40 GPU-hours (requires significant computational resources for experimentation and evaluation)
PREDICTION: The proposed experimental validation will provide empirical evidence for the effectiveness of the proposed mitigation strategies and the theoretical framework, and will help to establish the foundations for future research in modality imbalance and multimodal systems.

By using these measures, we can quantify the amount of information that each modality is contributing to the decision-making process and identify the weak modalities that are not providing sufficient information.
Controls: Compare to a baseline where all modalities are given equal importance, and an approach where unimodal accuracy is used to determine modality strength but without feature-level compensation or cross-modal interaction.
Estimated cost: 6 GPU-hours (runs on moderate-sized datasets)
Prediction: The proposed framework will be able to effectively identify weak modalities and improve the performance of the system on real-world datasets. However, the computational cost of calculating the mutual information between the modality's predictions and the overall decision may be high for very large datasets.

PROPOSAL 5: Enhancing Modality Robustness through Adversarial Training
Introduce an adversarial training module that injects adversarial perturbations into the weak modality's predictions, forcing the system to learn more robust feature representations and improve its generalization capabilities. This will help to address the issue of model brittleness and improve the robustness of the system to adversarial attacks.
Controls: Compare to a baseline where the system is trained without adversarial perturbations, and an approach where the system is robustified using data augmentation techniques.
Estimated cost: 20 GPU-hours (requires significant computational resources for adversarial training)
Prediction: The proposed framework will enhance modality robustness and improve the overall performance of the system on real-world datasets. However, the increased computational cost may limit its applicability to very large-scale datasets, and the adversarial training module may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve good results.

PROPOSAL 6: Analyzing and Improving Modality Imbalance in Real-World Multimodal Systems
Conduct an extensive analysis of modality imbalance in various real-world multimodal systems, including food classification, social media sentiment analysis, and indoor scene recognition. The analysis will help identify common causes of modality imbalance, such as sensor noise, data quality issues, and domain shift. Additionally, we will propose several improvements to address these issues and improve the overall performance of multimodal systems.
Controls: Compare to state-of-the-art methods and benchmarks in each of the analyzed application domains.
Estimated cost: 30 GPU-hours (requires significant computational resources for analysis and benchmarking)
Prediction: The proposed analysis will provide valuable insights into the causes of modality imbalance and suggest practical solutions to improve the performance of multimodal systems. However, the analysis may require significant manual effort and the improvements may not be universally applicable across all domains.

PROPOSAL 7: A Theoretical Framework for Modality Imbalance and Its Mitigation Strategies
Develop a theoretical framework that formalizes the concept of modality imbalance and its effects on multimodal systems. The framework will establish the relationship between modality imbalance, robustness, and performance and derive a set of bounds on the performance of multimodal systems. We will also use this framework to analyze and compare the proposed mitigation strategies, such as reward-shaping, exploratory feature loss, and robust late fusion, and derive guarantees on their effectiveness.
Controls: Compare to existing theoretical frameworks for robustness and multimodal systems.
Estimated cost: 0 GPU-hours (purely theoretical work)
Prediction: The proposed theoretical framework will provide a comprehensive understanding of modality imbalance and its mitigation strategies, and derive guarantees on their effectiveness. However, the framework may not capture all the nuances of real-world multimodal systems, and its applicability may be limited to specific domains or scenarios.

PROPOSAL 8: Experimental Validation of the Theoretical Framework
Use the theoretical framework developed in proposal 7 to derive specific mitigation strategies for modality imbalance, and experimentally validate their effectiveness on a set of benchmark multimodal datasets. We will also compare the proposed mitigation strategies to existing approaches and evaluate their performance using a range of metrics, including accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.
Controls: Compare to state-of-the-art methods and benchmarks in multimodal systems.
Estimated cost: 40 GPU-hours (requires significant computational resources for experimentation and evaluation)
Prediction: The proposed experimental validation will provide empirical evidence for the effectiveness of the proposed mitigation strategies and the theoretical framework, and will help to establish the foundations for future research in modality imbalance and multimodal systems.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modality Prioritization through Hybrid Ranking and Weighting
PROPOSAL: We will investigate a novel approach to modality prioritization in late fusion systems by integrating a hybrid ranking and weighting mechanism. Using a deep neural network, we will generate a ranking score for each modality based on its importance and relevance to the overall decision-making process. This ranking score will then be used to dynamically adjust the weights assigned to each modality, allowing dominant modalities to contribute more significantly to the fused prediction while weak modalities have a greater impact only when their predictions are near the decision boundary. The ranking and weighting mechanism will be learned jointly with the late fusion model to adapt to the data distribution and optimal fusion strategy.
CONTROLS: This approach will be compared to traditional late fusion with equal weights, static weight ratios, and confidence-based weighting. We will also deconstruct the hybrid ranking and weighting mechanism to identify the most significant components and their impacts on the performance of the late fusion system.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will outperform traditional late fusion methods on most benchmark datasets, exhibit improved robustness under noisy and imbalanced conditions, and demonstrate adaptability to different data distributions. However, difficulties in optimizing the hybrid ranking and weighting mechanism may require additional regularization techniques or curious search strategies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditional Redundancy Analysis for Latent Modality Interactions
PROPOSAL: To better understand the interactions between different modalities and improve the robustness of late fusion systems, we will develop a conditional redundancy analysis (CRA) framework. CRA will measure the amount of information shared between modalities conditional on each feature space, identifying those that are highly redundant even when one modality provides poor predictions. By selectively suppressing or downweighting the redundant feature spaces while reinforcing the core information contributed by each modality, CRA can improve the overall purity of modality-specific signals and achieved decisionmaking in high noise scenarios. 
CONTROLS: This analysis framework will be validated and compared with methods relying on correlation coefficients, information coefficients and modality adequacy depth.
COST: 750 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: CRA reveals heterogeneity in latent space interactions and shows substantial reductions in misalignment across conditional sets, strongly featuring beneficial to late fusion predictive accuracy as measures enhance decisionspace purification.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Modality Prioritization through Hybrid Ranking and Weighting
REVISED PROPOSAL: We will extend the hybrid ranking and weighting mechanism to incorporate a conditional mutual information (CMI) component, allowing the model to identify and adapt to modality correlations conditional on the input data. This CMI component will assess the mutual information between each modality pair based on the input features and their respective predictions. By using CMI as an auxiliary signal, the hybrid ranking and weighting mechanism can dynamically adjust the weights assigned to each modality, considering not only the modality ranking but also the statistical dependencies between modalities. This optimized weighting strategy is expected to achieve better fusion results, especially when modalities exhibit non-trivial conditional correlations.
CONTROLS: The CMI-based variant of the hybrid ranking and weighting mechanism will be compared to its original version and other competing methods that handle modality correlations.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Incorporating CMI into the modality prioritization framework fine-tunes the quality of the learned weights and leads to notable gains in decision-level fusion accuracy, especially in cases with considerable dependencies between modalities, and shows unprecedented robustness for varied conditions.

TITLE: Spectral Binning for Weak Modality Preservation
PROPOSAL: To preserve the unique information contributed by weak modalities, we will develop a spectral binning approach. This approach involves representing each modality's predictive distribution as a spectral density and using binning techniques to analyze the corresponding energy distribution. By adjusting the bin sizes and location, we can selectively focus on regions with higher spectral energies, effectively boosting the representation of weak modalities in the decision-making process.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate spectral binning against competing methods that adaptively emphasize weak modalities, and compare its performance across different dataset and class balances.
COST: 700 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By adaptively compensating for spectral imbalances, spectral binning demonstrates significant enhancements in the performance of late fusion and substantially reveals reductions in decision space redundancy by manner of weak modality specific representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Regularized Modality Dropout for Feature-Level Compensation
PROPOSAL: To alleviate the impact of modality imbalance while preserving the distinctive information encoded in each modality, we will develop a regularized modality dropout (RMD) approach. RMD involves randomly dropping or "gating" specific modalities during training, but with a biased probability distribution that emphasizes the importance of each modality. By using a notion of "modality worth" calculated based on their contribution to the overall prediction accuracy and confidence, RMD balances between discarding weak modalities and giving them a chance to correct the predictions from strong ones. With progressively expanded modality dropout and fine tuned regularization, we will demonstrate that this simple strategy achieves comparable results, yet stays backed with adaptability to heterogeneous datasets.
CONTROLS: RMD will be compared to other methods that compensate for modality imbalance, and its performance will be evaluated on datasets with varying modality importance and imbalance levels.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: RMD is expected to improve the overall decision-level fusion accuracy through guided assignment of prominence to critical modality interaction variables.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensembled Cross-Modal Distillation for Knowledge Transfer
PROPOSAL: To enhance the performance of weak modalities and improve late fusion robustness, we will develop an ensembled cross-modal distillation (ECMD) framework. ECMD involves training student models to learn from multiple teacher models, where each teacher model is an ensemble of modalities that contribute differently to the decision-making process. By leveraging knowledge transfer between teacher and student models, ECMD adapts the representation space of weak modalities and compensates for the lack of relevant features through the support from privileged information sources. Our experiments aim to validate the proposed framework on diverse datasets and show that ECMD facilitates desirable behaviors in the "teacher" - "student" duo adaptive interactions.
CONTROLS: ECMD will be evaluated against state-of-the-art techniques in knowledge transfer and model distillation, additionally adapting to future multimodal splitting of trained models.
COST: 1250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: ECMD's deployment to aligned weak modalities eases then promotes stronger knowledge extractability for latent predictive information and advances multiple exemplary learning offering with overall qualities – multiplicative/multiply.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Ensembled Cross-Modal Distillation for Knowledge Transfer
REVISED PROPOSAL: Building upon our ensembled cross-modal distillation (ECMD) framework, we will incorporate a meta-learning component to enable the ECMD framework to adapt to a variety of datasets and modality settings. By using a meta-learning approach, the ECMD framework can learn to learn from the teacher models and update its own parameters to better fit the new modality settings. This allows the ECMD framework to automatically adapt to the properties of the data distribution, class imbalance, and modality importance, facilitating improved performance and robustness under various conditions.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate this revised ECMD framework against the original ECMD and compare its performance on a variety of multimodal datasets and tasks.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised ECMD framework will demonstrate its ability to generalize well across different datasets and modality settings, achieving improved performance and robustness compared to the original ECMD framework.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Norm-constraint-based Late Fusion for Reduction of Information Interference
PROPOSAL: To mitigate the impact of information interference between modalities and enhance the decision-making process, we will propose norm-constraint-based late fusion (NCLF). NCLF involves applying a regularization term that enforces a soft constraint on the norm of the fused prediction residual. By incorporating this regularization term, NCLF encourages the exploration of diverse relevant information from each modality and reduces the impact of the potentially noisy or redundant predictions of individual modalities.
CONTROLS: NCLF will be compared to competing late fusion methods and its performance will be evaluated on datasets with varying levels of information interference and redundancy.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: NCLF is expected to produce robust and reliable fused predictions by efficiently controlling the impact of information interference and redundancy between modalities.

PROPOSAL: To mitigate the impact of information interference between modalities and enhance the decision-making process, we will propose norm-constraint-based late fusion (NCLF). NCLF involves applying a regularization term that enforces a soft constraint on the norm of the fused prediction residual. By incorporating this regularization term, NCLF encourages the exploration of diverse relevant information from each modality and reduces the impact of the potentially noisy or redundant predictions of individual modalities.
CONTROLS: NCLF will be compared to competing late fusion methods and its performance will be evaluated on datasets with varying levels of information interference and redundancy. We will also investigate the sensitivity of NCLF to different norm types and propose a method to adaptively select the optimal norm for each dataset.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: NCLF is expected to produce robust and reliable fused predictions by efficiently controlling the impact of information interference and redundancy between modalities.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Hard Attention for Modality-specific Importance Estimation
PROPOSAL: To estimate modality-specific importance scores accurately and efficiently, we will develop an adaptive hard attention (AHA) mechanism. AHA involves learning a set of modality-agnostic and modality-specific attention vectors through an iterative optimization process. By leveraging these attention vectors, AHA adaptively identifies the most relevant and informative modalities and estimates their importance scores, which can be used to guide the decision-making process and late fusion.
CONTROLS: AHA will be compared to existing methods for modality importance estimation and its performance will be evaluated on datasets with varying levels of modality informativeness and balance.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: AHA is expected to produce accurate and adaptive modality importance scores, improving the performance of late fusion and decision-making tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multimodal Uncertainty Modeling and Robust Decision Making
PROPOSAL: To address the challenges in multimodal decision making, we will develop a framework for multimodal uncertainty modeling and robust decision making (MUM-DRM). MUM-DRM involves learning a shared uncertainty representation across modalities and using this representation to inform decision making. We will use a Gaussian process-based approach to model the uncertainty of each modality and then use a decision-theoretic framework to fuse the uncertainty representations and make predictions. By considering the uncertainty in each modality, MUM-DRM can provide more robust and reliable decisions.
CONTROLS: MUM-DRM will be compared to existing methods for multimodal decision making and its performance will be evaluated on datasets with varying levels of modality informativeness and balance.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: MUM-DRM is expected to provide accurate and robust decision making by considering the uncertainty in each modality, and its performance will be significantly better than existing methods on challenging datasets.

This concludes the research proposal. The set contains 7 experiments and theoretical results to address the research questions on modality imbalance and robust decision making in multimodal learning.

propositions.texte: We will investigate the use of adversarial regularization as a means to maximize the predictive diversity of late fusion systems. By introducing an adversarial component that aims to confuse the predictions of each modality, we can promote model uncertainty and, in turn, improve the diversity of modality-specific predictions. We will use a robust optimization approach to adapt the late fusion model to the adversarial environment and demonstrate the benefits of this approach in terms of improved predictive diversity and robustness against noise.
propositions.titre: Predictive Diversity Maximization through Adversarial Regularization

propositions.controles: RMD will be compared to other methods that compensate for modality imbalance, and its performance will be evaluated on datasets with varying modality importance and imbalance levels.
propositions.prediction: RMD is expected to improve the overall decision-level fusion accuracy through guided assignment of prominence to critical modality interaction variables.
propositions.texte: To alleviate the impact of modality imbalance while preserving the distinctive information encoded in each modality, we will develop a regularized modality dropout (RMD) approach. RMD involves randomly dropping or "gating" specific modalities during training, but with a biased probability distribution that emphasizes the importance of each modality. By using a notion of "modality worth" calculated based on their contribution to the overall prediction accuracy and confidence, RMD balances between discarding weak modalities and giving them a chance to correct the predictions from strong ones. With progressively expanded modality dropout and fine tuned regularization, we will demonstrate that this simple strategy achieves comparable results, yet stays backed with adaptability to heterogeneous datasets.
propositions.titre: Regularized Modality Dropout for Feature-Level Compensation

propositions.controles: ECMD will be evaluated against state-of-the-art techniques in knowledge transfer and model distillation, additionally adapting to future multimodal splitting of trained models.
propositions.prediction: ECMD's deployment to aligned weak modalities eases then promotes stronger knowledge extractability for latent predictive information and advances multiple exemplary learning offering with overall qualities – multiplicative/multiply.
propositions.texte: To enhance the performance of weak modalities and improve late fusion robustness, we will develop an ensembled cross-modal distillation (ECMD) framework. ECMD involves training student models to learn from multiple teacher models, where each teacher model is an ensemble of modalities that contribute differently to the decision-making process. By leveraging knowledge transfer between teacher and student models, ECMD adapts the representation space of weak modalities and compensates for the lack of relevant features through the support from privileged information sources. Our experiments aim to validate the proposed framework on diverse datasets and show that ECMD facilitates desirable behaviors in the "teacher" - "student" duo adaptive interactions.
propositions.titre: Ensembled Cross-Modal Distillation for Knowledge Transfer

propositions.controles: NCLF will be compared to competing late fusion methods and its performance will be evaluated on datasets with varying levels of information interference and redundancy. We will also investigate the sensitivity of NCLF to different norm types and propose a method to adaptively select the optimal norm for each dataset.
propositions.prediction: NCLF is expected to produce robust and reliable fused predictions by efficiently controlling the impact of information interference and redundancy between modalities.
propositions.texte: To mitigate the impact of information interference between modalities and enhance the decision-making process, we will propose norm-constraint-based late fusion (NCLF). NCLF involves applying a regularization term that enforces a soft constraint on the norm of the fused prediction residual. By incorporating this regularization term, NCLF encourages the exploration of diverse relevant information from each modality and reduces the impact of the potentially noisy or redundant predictions of individual modalities.
propositions.titre: Norm-constraint-based Late Fusion for Reduction of Information Interference

propositions.controles: MUM-DRM will be compared to existing methods for multimodal decision making and its performance will be evaluated on datasets with varying levels of modality informativeness and balance.
propositions.prediction:
MUM-DRM is expected to provide accurate and robust decision making by considering the uncertainty in each modality, and its performance will be significantly better than existing methods on challenging datasets.

This concludes the research proposal. The set contains 7 experiments and theoretical results to address the research questions on modality imbalance and robust decision making in multimodal learning.
propositions.texte: To address the challenges in multimodal decision making, we will develop a framework for multimodal uncertainty modeling and robust decision making (MUM-DRM). MUM-DRM involves learning a shared uncertainty representation across modalities and using this representation to inform decision making. We will use a Gaussian process-based approach to model the uncertainty of each modality and then use a decision-theoretic framework to fuse the uncertainty representations and make predictions. By considering the uncertainty in each modality, MUM-DRM can provide more robust and reliable decisions.
propositions.titre: Multimodal Uncertainty Modeling and Robust Decision Making

TITLE:  Redesigned Attention-Based Sequence Mixer with Per-Channel Indexing
PROPOSAL: Design a new attention-style sequence mixer that incorporates per-channel indexing, where different channels can retrieve different past indices in the same step, while maintaining causal parallelism and the same asymptotic time complexity as softmax attention.
CONTROLS: Implement the new mixer alongside softmax attention and linear attention, and compare their performance on datasets from various domains, including weather forecasting, solar power forecasting, and electricity transformer load and temperature forecasting.

PREDICTION: The redesigned mixer should exhibit competitive performance with softmax attention on tasks requiring sequential data and channel-wise structure, while offering better suitability for tasks with non-sequential or irregular timestep indexing.

COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The results should demonstrate that the redesigned mixer effectively captures channel-wise structure and improves forecast accuracy on long-range sequences, while being computationally efficient.

TITLE:  Causal Per-Token Attention: A Building Block for Per-Channel Indexing
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel attention mechanism, causal per-token attention, which allows each token to selectively attend to a different subset of past tokens. This mechanism can serve as a building block for designing efficient per-channel indexing schemes.
CONTROLS: Analyze the properties of causal per-token attention, including its computational efficiency, ability to capture long-range dependencies, and ability to preserve causal relationships.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Causal per-token attention should exhibit promising properties, making it a suitable building block for designing more expressive and efficient sequence modeling architectures, such as the redesigned mixer proposed in task 1.

TITLE:  Theoretical Analysis of Per-Channel Indexing for Efficient Attention
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to analyze the expressive power and computational efficiency of per-channel indexing in attention-based sequence mixers. Investigate the relationship between the number of past indices retrieved, the dimensionality of the input sequence, and the computational complexity of per-channel indexing.
CONTROLS: Derive bounds on the performance of per-channel indexing in terms of the number of parameters, computational complexity, and expressiveness, and compare them with the existing bounds for softmax attention and linear attention.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (largely theoretical, with minimal computational cost)
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis should provide a deeper understanding of the benefits and limitations of per-channel indexing in attention-based sequence mixers, and guide the design of more efficient and expressive architectures.

PROPOSAL: Employ automated architecture search techniques to explore a wide range of possible per-channel indexing mechanisms and their combinations, and to identify the most efficient and effective architectures for a variety of sequence modeling tasks.
CONTROLS: Use a combination of reinforcement learning and evolutionary algorithms to search for the best architecture, and evaluate its performance on a suite of benchmark tasks and datasets.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The architecture search should yield a set of efficient and effective per-channel indexing mechanisms that can be used to improve the performance of attention-based sequence mixers, and provide a new starting point for future research on this topic.
