actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Revisiting Softmax Attention for Inconsistent Channel Access
PROPOSAL: Experiment on causal softmax attention with each head applying a unique set of weights to retrieve different past indices, extending its current lossy-processing limitation, by adding a channel-specific masking mechanism rebasing the softmax distribution per channel. This allows for asynchronous, context-dependent channel selection.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will include standard Transformer and recent efficient variants (Sparse Transformer, Linearized Transformer), as well as an ablation study to understand the impact of unique channel weights on the softmax glow.
COST: 400 GPU-hours (20 million tokens × 1000 seq len × 2 attention heads).
PREDICTION: Our experimental version of softmax attention with per-channel access may demonstrate noticeable improvement in time series forecasting tasks for weather and solar power forecasting, reducing MAE by 3-5% compared to the baseline, with potential failures in explaining the significant increase of complexity in the new attention variant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Neural Dictionary Methods for Efficient Contextual Lookups
PROPOSAL: Design meta-learning neural dictionaries of contextualized representations to support per-channel, context-dependent query-based embedding lookups in the sequence mixer, allowing for free-form indexing in the memory while preserving parallel efficiency. During training, dictionaries will be learned to replicate the Transformer's key-values.
CONTROLS: Experiments will compare the dictionary size and efficiency against the existing attention heads under constraint of an equal embedding dimension. Additionally, ablation testing will be conducted to isolate the benefits from training sequences to fixed-size dictionary sizes.
COST: 600 GPU-hours (10 million sequences × 128 dict entries × 3 neural networks).
PREDICTION: Neural dictionaries for contextualized key lookups may prove 40% more accurate than existing neural network head architectures, potentially showing an 8% improvement in MAE in weather forecasting for the lossless storage and lossy-processing framework with multitask deployment plan.

PROPOSAL: REVISED PROPOSAL: Extend the gated-softmax mechanism by introducing adaptive quantization for the channel weights learned during training. This allows the model to iteratively refine the weights and learn more nuanced, context-dependent patterns in the data, further improving per-channel access and contextual understanding.
CONTROLS: Controls include the revised gated-softmax variant, a baseline Transformer without attention modifications, and an ablation study to isolate the impact of adaptive quantization on the gated-softmax mechanism.
COST: 500 GPU-hours (15 million tokens × 1000 seq len × 4 trained dummy heads + learning period to stabilize quantized weights).
PREDICTION: The revised gated-softmax mechanism with adaptive quantization may demonstrate a 6-8% improvement in MAE for solar power forecasting and weather forecasting, reducing the difference in predictions between consecutive days, while maintaining parallel efficiency and avoiding the drawbacks of dictionary methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Memoization-Augmented Transformers for Long-Term Dependencies
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of memoization mechanisms to store and reuse computationally expensive function evaluations in attention mechanisms, particularly for tasks involving long-term dependencies. This allows the model to capture complex, non-linear relationships between distant positions in the sequence while maintaining parallel efficiency.
CONTROLS: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without memoization, memoization-augmented variants with cache sizes varies, and an ablation study to understand the impact of cache implementation on model performance.
COST: 900 GPU-hours (20 million sequences × 10 memory cache entries).
PREDICTION: Memoization-augmented Transformers may show a 12-15% improvement in MAE for electricity transformer load forecasting, allowing the model to accurately capture complex, long-term patterns in the data despite the large time gaps between transformer measurements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Attention with Adaptive Row-Wise Normalization
PROPOSAL: Introduce adaptive row-wise normalization to reduce the impact of channel-wise imbalance and highlight gradients across channels in the soft-attention output. This will allow the model to exploit local patterns in the data while capturing global relationships between channels.
CONTROLS: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without normalization, variants with different normalization mechanisms, and an ablation study to understand the impact of normalization on model performance.
COST: 700 GPU-hours (15 million sequences × 5 versions of attention normalization).
PREDICTION: Adaptive row-wise normalization may lead to a 4-6% improvement in MAE for solar power forecasting, as it enables the model to better identify recurring local patterns and phase changes in the data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Contextualized Filtering for Channel Access
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a contextualized filtering mechanism for channel access in attention-based models. This mechanism leverages knowledge of the entire sequence to selectively filter out irrelevant channels and focus on the most informative ones, enabling more efficient processing and memory usage.
CONTROLS: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without filtering, variants with different filtering mechanisms, and an ablation study to understand the impact of filtering on model performance.
COST: 800 GPU-hours (20 million sequences × 3 filtering mechanisms).
PREDICTION: The contextualized filtering mechanism may lead to a 10-12% reduction in computational complexity and a 5% improvement in MAE for weather forecasting tasks, as it enables more efficient processing of the large quantities of environmental data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Aggregation of Attention Weights for Multi-Channel Tasks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of hierarchical aggregation of attention weights to handle multi-channel tasks, allowing the model to effectively integrate information from multiple channels and capture complex relationships between them.
CONTROLS: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without hierarchical aggregation, variants with different aggregation mechanisms, and an ablation study to understand the impact of aggregation on model performance.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours (25 million sequences × 4 aggregation mechanisms).
PREDICTION: Hierarchical aggregation of attention weights may lead to a 15-20% improvement in MAE for electricity transformer load forecasting, as it enables the model to better capture the complex relationships between different channels and provide more accurate predictions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of Multi-Channel Attention Mechanisms
PROPOSAL: Conduct a thorough evaluation of the robustness of the proposed multi-channel attention mechanisms, including their sensitivity to hyperparameter tuning, noise in input data, and variability in model initialization. This will provide insights into the stability and reliability of these mechanisms in real-world applications.
CONTROLS: Controls will include a comprehensive hyperparameter tuning schedule, noise-injection experiments, and model initialization analysis using various techniques (e.g., weight perturbation, label noise injection).
COST: 1200 GPU-hours (30 million sequences × 5 robustness analysis scenarios).
PREDICTION: The robustness evaluation may reveal that the multi-channel attention mechanisms are sensitive to certain hyperparameters and noise levels, requiring careful tuning and adaptation strategies in real-world deployments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Combining Multi-Channel Attention Mechanisms for Scalable Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Experiment with combining the proposed multi-channel attention mechanisms to create a single, scalable model that can effectively capture complex patterns in time series data. This will be evaluated on a suite of real-world weather and energy forecasting tasks.
CONTROLS: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without attention modifications, individual mechanisms, and a hyperparameter search to optimize the combination.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours (50 million sequences × 5 attention mechanism combinations).
PREDICTION: The combined multi-channel attention model may achieve a 25-30% improvement in MAE for both weather and energy forecasting tasks, demonstrating its potential as a robust and scalable solution for time series prediction applications.

This allows the model to capture complex, non-linear relationships between distant positions in the sequence while maintaining parallel efficiency.
Controls: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without memoization, memoization-augmented variants with cache sizes varies, and an ablation study to understand the impact of cache implementation on model performance.
Estimated cost: 900 GPU-hours (20 million sequences × 10 memory cache entries).
Prediction: Memoization-augmented Transformers may show a 12-15% improvement in MAE for electricity transformer load forecasting, allowing the model to accurately capture complex, long-term patterns in the data despite the large time gaps between transformer measurements.

PROPOSAL 4: Attention with Adaptive Row-Wise Normalization
Introduce adaptive row-wise normalization to reduce the impact of channel-wise imbalance and highlight gradients across channels in the soft-attention output. This will allow the model to exploit local patterns in the data while capturing global relationships between channels.
Controls: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without normalization, variants with different normalization mechanisms, and an ablation study to understand the impact of normalization on model performance.
Estimated cost: 700 GPU-hours (15 million sequences × 5 versions of attention normalization).
Prediction: Adaptive row-wise normalization may lead to a 4-6% improvement in MAE for solar power forecasting, as it enables the model to better identify recurring local patterns and phase changes in the data.

PROPOSAL 5: Efficient Contextualized Filtering for Channel Access
Design and evaluate a contextualized filtering mechanism for channel access in attention-based models. This mechanism leverages knowledge of the entire sequence to selectively filter out irrelevant channels and focus on the most informative ones, enabling more efficient processing and memory usage.
Controls: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without filtering, variants with different filtering mechanisms, and an ablation study to understand the impact of filtering on model performance.
Estimated cost: 800 GPU-hours (20 million sequences × 3 filtering mechanisms).
Prediction: The contextualized filtering mechanism may lead to a 10-12% reduction in computational complexity and a 5% improvement in MAE for weather forecasting tasks, as it enables more efficient processing of the large quantities of environmental data.

PROPOSAL 6: Hierarchical Aggregation of Attention Weights for Multi-Channel Tasks
Investigate the use of hierarchical aggregation of attention weights to handle multi-channel tasks, allowing the model to effectively integrate information from multiple channels and capture complex relationships between them.
Controls: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without hierarchical aggregation, variants with different aggregation mechanisms, and an ablation study to understand the impact of aggregation on model performance.
Estimated cost: 1000 GPU-hours (25 million sequences × 4 aggregation mechanisms).
Prediction: Hierarchical aggregation of attention weights may lead to a 15-20% improvement in MAE for electricity transformer load forecasting, as it enables the model to better capture the complex relationships between different channels and provide more accurate predictions.

PROPOSAL 7: Evaluating the Robustness of Multi-Channel Attention Mechanisms
Conduct a thorough evaluation of the robustness of the proposed multi-channel attention mechanisms, including their sensitivity to hyperparameter tuning, noise in input data, and variability in model initialization. This will provide insights into the stability and reliability of these mechanisms in real-world applications.
Controls: Controls will include a comprehensive hyperparameter tuning schedule, noise-injection experiments, and model initialization analysis using various techniques (e.g., weight perturbation, label noise injection).
Estimated cost: 1200 GPU-hours (30 million sequences × 5 robustness analysis scenarios).
Prediction: The robustness evaluation may reveal that the multi-channel attention mechanisms are sensitive to certain hyperparameters and noise levels, requiring careful tuning and adaptation strategies in real-world deployments.

PROPOSAL 8: Combining Multi-Channel Attention Mechanisms for Scalable Time Series Forecasting
Experiment with combining the proposed multi-channel attention mechanisms to create a single, scalable model that can effectively capture complex patterns in time series data. This will be evaluated on a suite of real-world weather and energy forecasting tasks.
Controls: Controls will include a baseline Transformer without attention modifications, individual mechanisms, and a hyperparameter search to optimize the combination.
Estimated cost: 1500 GPU-hours (50 million sequences × 5 attention mechanism combinations).
Prediction: The combined multi-channel attention model may achieve a 25-30% improvement in MAE for both weather and energy forecasting tasks, demonstrating its potential as a robust and scalable solution for time series prediction applications.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Linear-Time Causal Softmax Attention with Non-Uniform Sampling
PROPOSAL: We modify the standard causal softmax attention to use non-uniform sampling, where instead of choosing the context indices uniformly at random, we sample from a non-uniform distribution that is skewed towards more relevant context indices. This is achieved by scaling the softmax output by a learned weighting factor.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard causal softmax attention with uniform sampling and ablate the learned weighting factor to measure its importance.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This variant should show improved performance on tasks that benefit from focusing on more relevant context, such as long-range modeling and tasks with non-sequential indexing. However, it may come at the cost of increased computational requirements for training the weighting factor.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effect of Channel-Wise Indices on Sequence Modeling Tasks
PROPOSAL: We introduce a simple yet effective approach to allow for per-channel, context-dependent selection from memory in causal softmax attention. Specifically, we enable the model to select different past indices for each channel by adding a learnable permutation matrix to the attention output. This is done at each step, allowing the model to adapt its selection to the task at hand.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original causal softmax attention and the non-uniform sampling variant from Experiment 1, with and without the permutation matrix, to measure its impact on performance and computational requirements.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This modification should significantly improve performance on tasks that require channel-wise structure, such as multivariate time series modeling, and demonstrate that closing the gap between lossless storage and lossy processing can lead to better sequence modeling. However, it may increase the computational requirements of the attention mechanism.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Hierarchical Attention on Weather Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We modify the attention mechanism to incorporate hierarchical attention, where the model散 selects a subset of channels at each hierarchical level, followed by per-channel indexing within each selected channel. This allows the model to adapt to the complexity of the task and focus on the most relevant channels at different hierarchical levels.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard hierarchical attention models without the per-channel indexing mechanism and against the approaches from Experiments 1 and 2, to measure the impact of closing the gap between lossless storage and lossy processing on modeling complex tasks like weather forecasting.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This hierarchical attention approach should demonstrate improved performance on tasks like weather forecasting, where channel-wise structure is critical, and show that per-channel indexing can be effectively integrated into hierarchical attention mechanisms. However, it may be computationally expensive to train and evaluate.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Investigating the Impact of Hierarchical Attention on Weather Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We modify the attention mechanism to incorporate hierarchical attention, where the model first selects a subset of channels at each hierarchical level, followed by a learned weighting factor for each channel to control the contribution of each channel to the final output. This allows the model to adapt to the complexity of the task and focus on the most relevant channels at different hierarchical levels.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard hierarchical attention models without the learned weighting factor and against the approaches from Experiments 1 and 2, to measure the impact of closing the gap between lossless storage and lossy processing on modeling complex tasks like weather forecasting.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (no change)
PREDICTION: By introducing the learned weighting factor, this hierarchical attention approach should further improve performance on tasks like weather forecasting, and demonstrate the effectiveness of per-channel indexing in conjunction with hierarchical attention mechanisms.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: REVISED Investigating the Impact of Hierarchical Attention on Weather Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We modify the attention mechanism to incorporate hierarchical attention, where the model first selects a subset of channels at each hierarchical level, followed by a learned weighting factor for each channel to control the contribution of each channel to the final output. This allows the model to adapt to the complexity of the task and focus on the most relevant channels at different hierarchical levels.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard hierarchical attention models without the learned weighting factor, against the approaches from Experiments 1 and 2, and also ablate the sampling mechanism at each hierarchical level to measure its impact on performance.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By introducing the learned weighting factor, this hierarchical attention approach should further improve performance on tasks like weather forecasting, and demonstrate the effectiveness of per-channel indexing in conjunction with hierarchical attention mechanisms. The ablation study will help identify the importance of the sampling mechanism at each hierarchical level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing Hierarchical Attention with Channel-Wise Indices to Transition-Based Models
PROPOSAL: We compare the performance of hierarchical attention with channel-wise indices to transition-based models, which are widely used in tasks like weather forecasting and solar power forecasting. We evaluate the two approaches on tasks like predicting temperature, wind speed, and solar irradiance, and analyze their strengths and weaknesses.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard hierarchical attention models without channel-wise indices, and ablate the hierarchical attention mechanism to measure its impact on performance.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This comparison will help identify whether the hierarchical attention with channel-wise indices approach is beneficial for tasks like weather forecasting and solar power forecasting, and whether it can match or outperform transition-based models. If successful, this could lead to a new standard approach for modeling temporal dependencies in these tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Input-Sample Transformation on Attention Mechanisms
PROPOSAL: We investigate the effect of input-sample transformation on attention mechanisms, specifically by applying techniques like normalization, scaling, or masking to the input sequences. We explore how these transformations can improve the performance of attention mechanisms in tasks like weather forecasting and solar power forecasting.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard attention mechanisms without input-sample transformation, and ablate the specific transformation technique to measure its impact on performance.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This investigation may reveal new insights into how input-sample transformation can be used to improve the performance of attention mechanisms, and potentially reveal new techniques for adapting attention mechanisms to specific tasks. However, it may also require significant computational resources to explore the various transformation techniques.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing a Rigorous Lower Bound for Attention Mechanisms
PROPOSAL: We develop a rigorous lower bound for attention mechanisms, specifically for the case of causal softmax attention. This lower bound will provide a theoretical limit on the performance of attention mechanisms and help identify the necessary conditions for achieving optimal performance.
CONTROLS: Compare against the current state-of-the-art attention mechanisms, and analyze the gap between the theoretical lower bound and the actual performance of these mechanisms.
COST: negligible (since this is a theoretical result)
PREDICTION: This lower bound will provide a deeper understanding of the fundamental limits of attention mechanisms and help identify the key factors that contribute to their performance. If successful, this will have a lasting impact on the research community and provide a clear direction for future research in this area.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Computational Complexity of Hierarchical Attention Mechanisms
PROPOSAL: We analyze the computational complexity of hierarchical attention mechanisms, specifically for large-scale applications like weather forecasting and solar power forecasting. We investigate the trade-offs between model complexity, computational resources, and performance, and provide a detailed analysis of the time and space complexity of hierarchical attention mechanisms.
CONTROLS: Compare against the theoretical lower bound developed in Experiment 6, and evaluate the computational resources required for large-scale applications.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This analysis will provide a clear understanding of the computational complexity of hierarchical attention mechanisms and help identify the necessary computational resources required for large-scale applications. If successful, this will have significant implications for the deployment of hierarchical attention mechanisms in production environments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling Up Hierarchical Attention Mechanisms for Large-Scale Sequence Modeling
PROPOSAL: We scale up hierarchical attention mechanisms to process large-scale sequence data, leveraging distributed computing and data parallelism techniques. We explore strategies for efficient model deployment, profiling, and optimization, and provide a comprehensive analysis of the performance and scalability of hierarchical attention mechanisms on large-scale datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare against the current state-of-the-art sequence modeling architectures, and evaluate the performance of hierarchical attention mechanisms on large-scale datasets.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: If successful, this experiment will demonstrate the feasibility of deploying hierarchical attention mechanisms at scale, and provide a comprehensive understanding of the performance and scalability of these mechanisms on large-scale sequence modeling tasks. This will have significant implications for the adoption of hierarchical attention mechanisms in production environments, particularly in applications that require real-time processing of large-scale sequence data.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Baseline Detectors for Univariate Time Series Anomalies
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of five state-of-the-art unsupervised detectors for UTS anomalies: ETSpy ( employing exponential smoothing to detect anomalies), lurking (utilizing a generalized additive model for UTS anomalies), pyramid (using a per-dimension thresholding approach), ReBeL (reconstruction-based local outlier factor detection), and Prophet (prediction-based UTS anomaly detection). We'll experiment on three real-world datasets: ECG monitor waveforms, web server log traffic metrics, and temperature sensor readings. We will use the metrics of precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the ROCAUC curve.
CONTROLS: Evaluate each detector's performance on three known anomalies (point, segment, and gradually rising) in the testing set.
COST: 10 GPU-hours (method implementation, setup, and baseline evaluation)
PREDICTION: The unsupervised detectors exhibit varying strength in detecting different anomaly types; ReBeL will struggle with small point anomalies, while pyramid will be strong at detecting slowly rising anomalies and Prophet demonstrates poor performance for UTS. Additionally, precision, recall, and F1-score generally show a tradeoff for these detectors when trying to maintain high performance across different anomaly types due to their weaknesses in handling anomalous variations and patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Local Trend Extraction for UTS Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel method to capture local trends in univariate time series for anomaly detection. The approach is based on a hybrid model combining a variance stabilizing transformation (VST) to optimize feature extraction for short-term trends, a locality-sensitive learning (LSL) framework to identify anomalous patterns in the time domain, and an exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) to strengthen local propagated anomalies from low-level points in the graph structure. The LSL structure aims to encode dependencies between time points using neighborhood nodes. We evaluate this on the same datasets as before (ECG, web server log traffic metrics, and temperature sensor readings) and use the same metrics as before.
CONTROLS: Compare LSL-EWMA model with ETSpy and lurking baselines from Proposal 1 on their capacity to detect small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies.
COST: 15 GPU-hours (setting up LSL-EWMA framework, computing the features, and the comparison)
PREDICTION: Local Trend Extraction would be better at detecting small point anomalies and segment anomalies with moderately slow rises with a slightly improved ROCAUC performance but at sometimes lower precision and recall rates due to its overemphasis of variance in anomalies such as those with high-frequency signal oscillation.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Refining Local Trend Extraction for UTS Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: Enhance Proposal 2 (Local Trend Extraction for UTS Anomaly Detection) to better tackle gradual segment anomalies by incorporating dynamic periodicity modeling based on a learnt periodic pattern analyst system (LPPAS). Our modification integrates LPPAS with the Local_Sensitive_Learning_EWMA (LSL-EWMA) framework. The LPPAS roughly searches high-variance inflection points in frequency compositions, covering variations in long-term shifting changes of periodic waveforms. Compute the distance between these high-variance locations to understand changes within periodic features. The enhanced LSL-EWMA-LPPAS will be further compared against the baseline methods of ETSpy and lurking, which will task both in exploiting behavior within low to moderate increasing anomalies.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigation of Local Trend Models in UTS Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: Compare the effectiveness of different local trend models for capturing point anomalies in UTS and investigate their ability to adapt to evolving periodic patterns. Specifically, develop and implement three different models based on local moving averages, local exponential smoothing, and local exponential-weighted moving averages, and evaluate their performance on real-world UTS datasets from web service and cloud server KPI monitoring (AIOps) and environmental air-temperature monitoring.
CONTROLS: Compare against the state-of-the-art frequency-conditioned reconstruction approach and the recent timing-information-based prediction approach, as well as ablate each local trend model by removing its core innovation and measuring the performance degradation.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (can be distributed across 5 days of running 1-hour experiments)
PREDICTION: Expected result: the local trend models provide a significant improvement in point anomaly detection over the frequency-conditioned reconstruction approach, and reasonable performance on slowly rising anomalies compared to the timing-information-based prediction approach. Can fail if the models are not robust enough to adapt to complex periodic patterns or insufficiently capture local trends.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: AutoML for Periodicity Models in UTS
PROPOSAL: Utilize AutoML to find effective periodicity models for UTS anomaly detection, focusing on capturing both static and dynamic periodic patterns. Develop a hyperparameter search space for models such as the Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter, the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), and the Seasonal Decomposition method, and evaluate the performance of each model on the same real-world UTS datasets used in proposal 1. Measure how well the AutoML-discovered models perform in distinguishing slow anomalies from normal periodic changes and detecting evolving periodic patterns.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the AutoML-discovered models against hand-crafted periodicity models (e.g., staggers, multiple frequency peaks with phase shifting) and assess their robustness to noise and anomalies in the training data.
COST: 30 GPU-hours (will require distributed computation and a moderate-sized hyperparameter search space)
PREDICTION: Expected result: the AutoML-discovered models provide a good trade-off between model complexity, adaptability to dynamic periodic patterns, and robustness to outliers and noise. Performance may degrade if the search space is not extensive enough or if the ranking method biases towards simpler models.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigation of Local Trend Models in UTS Anomaly Detection (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Modify proposal 1 to jointly consider both local trends and periodic patterns when detecting point anomalies. Implement a combined local trend and periodicity model based on a non-linear combination of the three local trend models (local moving average, local exponential smoothing, and local exponential-weighted moving averages) with the best performing periodicity models discovered by AutoML in proposal 2. Assess the impact of the combined model on point anomaly detection, slow anomaly detection, and robustness to noise and unlabeled anomalies.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the combined model against the baseline models (frequency-conditioned reconstruction approach and the recent timing-information-based prediction approach) and the individual local trend and periodicity models, as well as ablate the combined model by removing its periodic component and measuring the performance degradation.
COST: 25 GPU-hours (moderate-sized hyperparameter search space for the combined model)
PREDICTION: Expected result: the combined model significantly improves performance on both point anomalies and slow anomalies and provides robustness to noise and anomalies in the training data. Can fail if the combined model is overfitting or overly complex.

Current set remains at 2; revision retains proposal 1's structure but refines its objectives and methodology.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Noise-Robust Normal Pattern Learning for UTS
PROPOSAL: Investigate how to learn normal patterns for UTS from training data contaminated with noise and unlabeled anomalies, enabling more robust UTS anomaly detection. Propose a denoising autoencoder (DAE) architecture that uses a combination of contractive regularization, gradient clipping, and an exponential moving average schedule to minimize the impact of outliers and anomalies on normal pattern learning. Evaluate the performance of the DAE in detecting anomalies when trained on noisy data and compare it against traditional autoencoders.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art normal pattern learning methods and ablate the proposed denoising mechanism by removing each component to measure its contribution.
COST: 15 GPU-hours ( relatively small hyperparameter search space)
PREDICTION: Expected result: the DAE architecture provides better robustness to noise and anomalies in the training data and improves performance on unknown anomalies. May fail if the DAE is not well-suited for learning non-linear relationships between UTS features or if the noise in the training data introduces artifacts that are misinterpreted as anomalies.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Baseline Models for UTS Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: We will use three existing unsupervised detection methods as baselines to evaluate our new approach: AutoARIMA for local fitting, ETS+KDE for reconstruction, and Prophet for long-term forecasting.
CONTROLS: The baseline models will be run on the same datasets and metrics as our proposed method. 
COST: 0.5 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect these baselines to struggle with small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies. The AutoARIMA model may not fit the short-term behavior accurately, ETS+KDE may not capture the nuances of local trends, and Prophet may not adapt to the evolving periodicity of the time series. PREDICTION: 

The baselines will exhibit modest performance (AUC-ROC ~0.7-0.8) on detecting large point anomalies, but will struggle with small point anomalies (AUC-ROC <0.6) and slowly rising anomalies (AUC-ROC <0.7).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Prophet for UTS Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate an enhanced version of the Prophet model that incorporates a novel loss function to encourage the model to capture local trends and dynamic periodicity. The loss function will balance the normal log-likelihood with a penalty for large local deviations. 
CONTROLS: We will compare the enhanced Prophet model against the original Prophet baseline using the same datasets and metrics. Additionally, we will conduct an ablation study to separate the contributions of the loss function and the Prophet architecture.
COST: 3 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The enhanced Prophet model should improve over the original baseline, especially on datasets with a significant local trend or evolving periodicity (AUC-ROC ~0.8). However, Prophet still may struggle with short-term anomalies due to its focus on long-term forecasting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Time-Wavelet Autoencoder for Adaptive Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel autoencoder-based method that incorporates a time-wavelet transform to adaptively reconstruct UTS data. The time-wavelet layer will extract local features that capture both temporal and frequency information. The autoencoder will learn a representation of normal behavior through ℓ1 regularization. 
CONTROLS: We will compare the time-wavelet autoencoder against baseline reconstruction methods (e.g., ETS+KDE, temporal Fourier transform-based autoencoder) using both real-world datasets and synthetic datasets with controlled levels of noise and anomalies.
COST: 4 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The time-wavelet autoencoder should improve upon the baselines, especially in capturing subtle anomalies within short-term local trends and segment-level patterns (AUC-ROC ~0.85). However, its performance may degrade in cases with high levels of noise or multiple periodic components in the data.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Time-Wavelet Autoencoder for Adaptive Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We modify the previous proposal by introducing a contrastive learning regularization term to the autoencoder's reconstruction loss. This term encourages the model to differentiate between normal and anomalous data points, leading to improved anomaly detection performance. Additionally, we will incorporate a hierarchical attention mechanism to focus the model's learning on the most informative time periods. 
CONTROLS: The revised autoencoder will be compared against both the original autoencoder and other state-of-the-art unsupervised anomaly detection methods using real-world datasets.
COST: 6 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised time-wavelet autoencoder should exhibit significant improvement in detecting small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies (AUC-ROC ~0.9).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Graph-Based Long Short-Term Memory Network for UTS Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel graph-based LSTM approach that modeling the dynamic periodicity and local trends in UTS data as a graph, where time points are connected based on similarity in frequency content. The LSTM network will be applied to this graph to capture the dependencies between neighboring time points.
CONTROLS: We will compare the graph-based LSTM against other state-of-the-art methods on the AIOps and ECG monitoring datasets, and evaluate its performance on detecting both small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies.
COST: 8 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The graph-based LSTM should exhibit strong performance on both AIOps and ECG monitoring datasets, especially in capturing the evolution of periodic patterns (AUC-ROC ~0.92). However, its performance may degrade on datasets with high levels of noise or non-stationary behavior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Fidelity Alert System for Robust Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-fidelity alert system that leverages the strengths of multiple models to detect anomalies in UTS data. The system will use the output of the graph-based LSTM network ( proposal 4) as a high-fidelity detection, and combine it with the output of the time-wavelet autoencoder (proposal 3) as a low-fidelity detection. The final alert will be generated based on a weighted combination of these two detections.
CONTROLS: We will compare the multi-fidelity alert system against individual models on both AIOps and ECG monitoring datasets, and evaluate its performance on detecting both small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The multi-fidelity alert system should exhibit improved performance compared to individual models, especially in detecting small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies (AUC-ROC ~0.95). However, its performance may degrade if there are significant discrepancies between the high- and low-fidelity detections.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expectation-Maximization Algorithm-Based Anomaly Labeling for Semi-Supervised Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a semi-supervised learning method that uses the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm to label anomalous points in the UTS data. The EM algorithm will be used to iteratively update the model parameters and anomaly labels, allowing the model to learn from limited labeled data and robustly detect anomalies.
CONTROLS: We will compare the EM-based labeling method against other semi-supervised learning approaches on both AIOps and ECG monitoring datasets, and evaluate its performance on detecting both small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies.
COST: 12 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The EM-based labeling method should exhibit strong performance on semi-supervised learning tasks, especially with limited labeled data (AUC-ROC ~0.96). However, its performance may degrade if the initial model parameters are far from optimal or if there are significant outliers in the data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anomaly-Seeded Training for Robust UTS Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel training method, anomaly-seeded training, where the model is trained with a few carefully selected anomalous points as additional training data. These anomalous points are selected using a density-based anomaly detection method and are added to the normal training data to create a more robust and generalized model.
CONTROLS: We will compare the anomaly-seeded training method against traditional supervised and unsupervised training methods on both AIOps and ECG monitoring datasets, and evaluate its performance on detecting both small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies.
COST: 15 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The anomaly-seeded training method should exhibit improved performance compared to traditional methods, especially on datasets with a large number of anomalies or complex anomaly distributions (AUC-ROC ~0.98). However, its performance may degrade if the selected anomalous points are not representative of the true anomalies.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Enhancing Prophet for UTS Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: We modify the previous proposal by integrating the anomaly-seeded training method (proposal 7) with the enhanced Prophet model (proposal 2). The Prophet model will be trained with a few carefully selected anomalous points as additional training data, and will learn to capture both local trends and dynamic periodicity in a more robust and generalized manner.
CONTROLS: We will compare the revised enhanced Prophet model against the original enhanced Prophet model and other state-of-the-art anomaly detection methods on both AIOps and ECG monitoring datasets, and evaluate its performance on detecting both small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies.
COST: 18 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised enhanced Prophet model should exhibit improved performance compared to the original enhanced Prophet model, especially on datasets with complex anomaly distributions or a large number of anomalies (AUC-ROC ~0.99). However, its performance may degrade if the selected anomalous points are not representative of the true anomalies.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Baseline Models for UTS Anomaly Detection
PROPOSAL: We refine the previous proposal by incorporating the multi-fidelity alert system (proposal 5) into the baseline models. The multi-fidelity alert system will be used to generate a final binary alert decision based on the outputs of the baseline models. This will allow us to evaluate the impact of the multi-fidelity alert system on the overall performance of the baseline models.
CONTROLS: We will compare the refined baseline models against the original baseline models and other state-of-the-art anomaly detection methods on both AIOps and ECG monitoring datasets, and evaluate their performance on detecting both small point anomalies and slowly rising anomalies.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The refined baseline models should exhibit improved performance compared to the original baseline models, especially on datasets with a large number of anomalies or complex anomaly distributions (AUC-ROC ~0.95).

We modify the previous proposal by introducing a contrastive learning regularization term to the autoencoder's reconstruction loss. This term encourages the model to differentiate between normal and anomalous data points, leading to improved anomaly detection performance. We propose a novel graph-based LSTM approach that modeling the dynamic periodicity and local trends in UTS data as a graph, where time points are connected based on similarity in frequency content. TITLE: Diverse Traces Fine-Tuning Baseline
PROPOSAL: Sample a large number of diverse reasoning traces per question from matrix-factorization-distilled teacher models, using the intended fine-tuning dataset. Then, we fine-tune a standard transformer model on these traces, treating each as an independent example.
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline sequential fine-tuning on the same traces; (2)Ablation to verify the effect of the diverse traces on the model's ability to retain multiple reasoning modes.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (an hour for data collection and 4 hours for training for 25 iterations with batch size 16 on a 64 GPU Tesla A100).
PREDICTION: We expect the model to show some improvement over the baseline sequential fine-tuning, especially in terms of ability to generate multiple reasoning modes. However, accuracy may not improve as much as expected due to the mixture of potentially conflicting modes in the diverse traces.

Note: This experiment serves as a baseline for experiments to follow, which will look to improve upon this fine-tuning scheme by incorporating competition-based teacher models, recursive aggregation, and new objective functions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: AMoRE (Aggregated Moment Recognition Ensemble)
PROPOSAL: Train a separate model on the same diverse traces as in the baseline, but this time using an aggregated moment recognition (AMoRE) training objective: instead of focusing on individual tokens or classes, the model learns to match the frequency distributions of token co-occurrence in the traces. We expect this to improve model ability to capture transient forking tokens and their contexts.
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline sequential fine-tuning; (2)Diverse traces fine-tuning from Diverse Traces Fine-Tuning Baseline (1).
COST: 150 GPU-hours (5 hours for pre-training and 3.75 hours for fine-tuning for 20 iterations with batch size 16 on a 64 GPU Tesla A100).
PREDICTION: We expect AMoRE to show better retention of diverse reasoning modes and lower continuity error (i.e., the rate at which the succession of tokens in a chain of thought changes), indicating a better understanding of context and maintaining forks.
 
– note: AMoRE simply involves a side head trained on the objective comparing the individual  joint probabilities levels of overlapping between the traces.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Diverse Traces Fine-Tuning Baseline with  Trained Competitive Teachers
PROPOSAL: We use diverse traces from multiple models trained on the same dataset with different architectures (e.g., RoBERTa, Longformer) or different parameters (e.g., differently- initialized weights), to provide multiple views on the same problem, reducing over-reliance on a single teacher model. The individual models are pre-trained on a similar task (e.g., multiple Q&A datasets), then fine-tuned on different subsets of data with different objectives to produce diverse responses.
CONTROLS: (1) Original Diverse Traces Fine-Tuning Baseline (1).
COST: 200 GPU-hours (50 hours for pre-training and 50 hours for fine-tuning for 20 iterations with batch size 16 on a 64 GPU Tesla A100).
PREDICTION: We expect diverse and better- performing reasoning modes to emerge from the ensemble of competing teacher models, and the fine-tuned model to generalize better across tasks.

Note: While AMoRE is expected to improve upon the baseline, REVISED Diverse Traces Fine-Tuning Baseline aims to introduce new modes from teacher models, possibly providing state-of-the-art performance.

This aims to improve the model's understanding of correct reasoning paths and prevent collapsing modes.
CONTROLS: Baseline Rev.1 (2), which is the original AMoRE, and the ablation to verify the effect of the consistency-reward based loss.
COST: 75 GPU-hours (5 hours for fine-tuning  for 15 iterations with batch size 16 on a 64 GPU Tesla A100).
PREDICTION: We expect the additional verification-based loss to improve AMoRE's consistency and accuracy, allowing it to arguably surpass baseline Rev.1 and demonstrate higher accuracy for diverse reasoning modes.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Native Parallel Fine-Tuning with a Distillation Regime
PROPOSAL: Train a large language model on a set of diverse, correct reasoning traces per question distilled from teacher models, using a combination of reconstruction loss and a divergence-promoting regularizer to encourage distinct reasoning modes. The model will be fine-tuned with a custom objective that rewards verifiable correctness and promotes diversity across different reasoning modes.
CONTROLS: Compare with standard supervised fine-tuning, parallel reasoning models without the custom objective, and a baseline of sequential reasoning.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should improve both the accuracy of a single generation and the accuracy and coverage obtained by aggregating a small number of parallel generations. However, it may require careful tuning to optimize the trade-off between diversity and accuracy.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Enhancing Native Parallel Fine-Tuning with a Distillation Regime
PROPOSAL: Modify the distillation regime by adding a novel "modes-restrictor" component, which analyzes the generated reasoning traces and selectively prunes the redundant or uninformative modes, ensuring that the model retains a diverse and relevant set of distinct reasoning modes. This component will be implemented using a variant of the attention mechanism to identify and filter out weak modes.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original proposal 1, as well as a variation where the modes-restrictor is removed.
COST: 20 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This modification should lead to more robust and accurate representations of distinct reasoning modes, leading to improved accuracy and coverage when aggregating parallel generations. However, it may also introduce additional noise or bias if not carefully calibrated.

This component will be implemented using a variant of the attention mechanism to identify and filter out weak modes.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original proposal 1, as well as a variation where the modes-restrictor is removed.
COST: 20 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This modification should lead to more robust and accurate representations of distinct reasoning modes, leading to improved accuracy and coverage when aggregating parallel generations. However, it may also introduce additional noise or bias if not carefully calibrated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Routing for Mode Identification
PROPOSAL: Introduce a hierarchical routing mechanism that automatically identifies and routes the most diverse and accurate reasoning modes from the output of the model, allowing for efficient selection of the best representing modes. This will be based on a hierarchy of clustering and routing, starting from the aggregation of individual generations to the highest-level mode selection.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline using random routing, as well as a simplified version of the hierarchical routing mechanism.
COST: 30 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should lead to improved selection of the best representing modes and help maintain diversity in the aggregated output, however, it may require careful tuning of the routing mechanism.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enabling Plug-and-Play Transfer to New Domains
PROPOSAL: Develop a transfer module that enables the trained model to adapt to new domains (e.g., competition mathematics, code generation, and graduate-level science question answering) with minimal additional training. This will be achieved through a lightweight adapter learned through a self-supervised task that fine-tunes the model to the new domain while preserving the overall weights.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline where the model is retrained from scratch for each new domain, as well as a variation that uses a more extensive adaptation mechanism.
COST: 40 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This transfer module should enable seamless adaptation to new domains without compromising the model's performance on the original tasks, thanks to the lightweight adaptation mechanism. However, it may introduce minor degradation in performance if the new domain requires significant changes in reasoning.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Enabling Pr-Ent-Red Plug-and-Play Transfer to New Domains
PROPOSAL: Enhance the transfer module from proposal 3 by incorporating a Pre-training stage to adapt to the new domain's characteristic reasoning patterns, an Ent-Analysis stage to select the most relevant model components to transfer, and a Red-Rectification stage to rectify any potential errors or biases during the adaptation process. This refined transfer module will be learned through a multi-stage fine-tuning process.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline in proposal 3, as well as a control using the Reptile method for model adaptation.
COST: 20 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This enhanced transfer module should improve the model's adaptation to new domains by reducing the forgetting of original task knowledge, improving the selection of relevant model components, and rectifying any potential errors or biases during adaptation. However, it may be computationally more expensive due to the multi-stage fine-tuning process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exposing Hidden Modes through Group-Based Hypernetworks
PROPOSAL: Introduce a Group-Based Hypernetwork (GBH) that learns to generate a set of diverse and accurate reasoning modes by encoding the input question as a sequence of groupings and then using a hypernetwork to generate a corresponding sequence of mode-generating weights. This approach will enable the model to expose hidden modes and improve the overall diversity and accuracy of the generated output.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline using random groupings and a simplified version of the GBH.
COST: 50 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should lead to a significant improvement in the model's ability to expose hidden modes and generate more diverse and accurate responses. However, it may be computationally expensive and require careful tuning to achieve optimal performance.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Enhancing Native Parallel Fine-Tuning with a Distillation Regime
PROPOSAL: Modify the distillation regime to incorporate the output of the Group-Based Hypernetwork from proposal 4, using the generated mode-generating weights to guide the distillation process. This will enable the model to learn more diverse and accurate representations of reasoning modes and further improve the overall diversity and accuracy of the generated output.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original proposal 1 and the revised proposal 4.
COST: 15 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This enhancement should lead to a significant improvement in the model's ability to learn diverse and accurate representations of reasoning modes and generate more accurate responses. However, it may also introduce additional complexity and require careful tuning to achieve optimal performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Reasoning with a Rollback Mechanism
PROPOSAL: Introduce a Rollback Mechanism that allows the model to recover from errors or suboptimal decisions made during the reasoning process by updating the context and re-executing the reasoning only for the affected steps. This will enable the model to learn more efficient and accurate representations of reasoning modes and generate more accurate responses.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that does not implement a rollback mechanism and a variation that uses a greedy rollout instead of a backward rollback.
COST: 60 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This mechanism should lead to a significant improvement in the model's efficiency and accuracy, particularly for complex reasoning tasks. However, it may also introduce additional computational overhead and require careful tuning to achieve optimal performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Competency-Aware Reasoning for High-Stakes Domains
PROPOSAL: Develop a Competency-Aware Reasoning Framework that integrates the knowledge and reasoning from proposals 1-5 with a confidence estimation and competency assessment module to determine the model's true competence on a given task. This framework will enable the model to automatically identify its limitations and provide more accurate and transparent responses.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline that does not implement competency-aware reasoning and a variation that uses a domain-agnostic confidence estimation approach.
COST: 80 additional GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This framework should lead to a significant improvement in the model's overall performance and reliability, particularly for high-stakes domains such as graduate-level science question answering and competition mathematics.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identifying Forking Tokens for Diversity Enhancement
PROPOSAL: Use unsupervised clustering algorithms (e.g. DBSCAN, K-Means) to identify tokens within a chain of thought that have high likelihood of being forking tokens, based on their co-occurrence patterns and semantic meanings. Train a small auxiliary model to predict these tokens using side effects (e.g. jumpiness, sinkhorn distance, geometric derivatives).
CONTROLS: Baseline: Randomly select tokens for forking. Ablation: Train without auxiliary model for prediction.
COST: 2,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: With proper parameter tuning, the proposed method will be able to identify around 20-30% of the forking tokens with 60-70% accuracy, and will improve diversity by 1.5 times compared to random sampling methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diversity-Enhanced Fine-Tuning through Distillation
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a language model on a set of diverse, correct reasoning traces per question using the Hindsight Distillation framework. This framework uses teacher models to generate hard attention masks that highlight the relevant information for each reasoning mode. Train the student model to mimic the attention patterns of the teachers, thereby encouraging the student to learn the distinct reasoning modes present in the training traces.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard supervised fine-tuning without hardness-aware distillation. Ablation: No distillation.
COST: 10,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: With proper hyperparameters, the proposed method will retain around 80-90% of the distinct reasoning modes compared to collapse (-50% reduction), and improve accuracy on a set of diverse reasoning tasks by 2-3% compared to the baseline, measured by a new adapter-based evaluation protocol.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Enhancement of Diversity-Enhanced Fine-Tuning through Distillation
PROPOSAL: Enhance the Diversity-Enhanced Fine-Tuning through Distillation method (2) by incorporating the identified forking tokens (1) into the hardness-aware distillation process. Add a special token to the input sequence that is pre-filled with the identified forking tokens, and modify the teacher models to pay extra attention to this token while generating hard attention masks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Enhanced method without forking tokens. Ablation: Remove special token and forking tokens.
COST: (approximately double the original estimate, around 20,000 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: This enhancement will allow the fine-tuned model to retain around 95% of the distinct reasoning modes compared to collapse (-75% reduction), and improve accuracy by 4-5% compared to the non-enhanced method.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Triggering Distinct Reasoning Modes through Adversarial Evaluation
PROPOSAL: Develop an adversarial evaluation protocol that triggers the distinct reasoning modes in the fine-tuned model. Use a set of pre-defined trigger tokens to inject hints that systematically seek out the existence of hidden pathways in the model's reasoning process. Evaluate the model's ability to reason correctly while triggering specific reasoning modes, and compare its performance to the baselines.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard fine-tuning without trigger tokens. Ablation: Remove triggers for specific modes.
COST: 8,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This protocol will demonstrate a 5-7% increase in accuracy when triggering the distinct reasoning modes, with an average 3-4x increase in diversity compared to the baselines, indicating the robustness and dependability of the modes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-Consistency Training for Reasoning Mode Retention
PROPOSAL: Modify the standard fine-tuning objective to incorporate a self-consistency regularization term. Train the model to generate a set of diverse, correct reasoning traces per question, and then have the model evaluate and correct its own outputs. This self-consistency term encourages the model to retain the distinct reasoning modes learned during fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard fine-tuning without self-consistency regularization. Ablation: Remove self-consistency term.
COST: 5,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will improve the retention of distinct reasoning modes by 3-4% compared to the baseline, with an average 2-3% increase in accuracy on a set of diverse reasoning tasks, indicating the effectiveness of the self-consistency regularization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Native Parallel Reasoning through Token-Invariant Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Extend the teacher-student framework used in Diversity-Enhanced Fine-Tuning to train a model that naturally generates diverse, correct reasoning traces per question. Use token-invariant contrastive learning to encourage the model to focus on the essential information across different reasoning modes, rather than the specifics of each mode.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard contrastive learning without token-invariance. Ablation: Remove token-invariance constraint.
COST: 15,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will improve the model's ability to generate diverse, correct reasoning traces per question by 4-6% compared to the baseline, with an average 5-7% increase in accuracy on a set of diverse reasoning tasks, indicating the effectiveness of native parallel reasoning.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Enhancement of Native Parallel Reasoning through Token-Invariant Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Enhance the Native Parallel Reasoning through Token-Invariant Contrastive Learning method (5) by incorporating the identified forking tokens (1) and leveraging the diversity-enhanced fine-tuning (2) approach. Train the model to predict forking tokens and utilize them as a guidance for generating diverse, correct reasoning traces.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Enhanced method without forking tokens and fine-tuning. Ablation: Remove forking token prediction and fine-tuning components.
COST: (approximately double the original estimate, around 30,000 GPU-hours)
PREDICTION: This enhancement will allow the model to improve its ability to generate diverse, correct reasoning traces per question by 7-10% compared to the baseline, with an average 10-12% increase in accuracy on a set of diverse reasoning tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Aggregation Methods for Reasoning Mode Ensemble
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate aggregation methods for combining the outputs of different reasoning modes generated by the Native Parallel Reasoning approach. Investigate methods such as voting, weighted voting, and diversity-regularized ensemble learning to determine which methods lead to the most accurate and diverse final outputs.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Individual reasoning modes. Ablation: Remove diversity regularization.
COST: 4,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This analysis will reveal that the ensemble approaches improve accuracy by 5-7% and diversity by 2-3 times compared to individual reasoning modes, indicating the effectiveness of aggregation methods in leveraging the strengths of multiple reasoning modes.

TITLE: Rare Event Targeting via Surrogate Regression
PROPOSAL: Develop a surrogate regression task that focuses on predicting the likelihood of rare events, such as forking tokens, within the context of Native Parallel Reasoning. Use this task to selectively sample from the model's output distribution, prioritizing regions where rare events are more likely.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard sampling strategy. Ablation: Remove surrogate regression.
COST: 12,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will enhance sampling efficiency by 20-30% and increase the accuracy of rare event targeting by 15-20% compared to the baseline, indicating the effectiveness of choosing optimal sampling locations to expose the model's knowledge on rarer events.

bilan.ensemble:
PROPOSAL 1: Identifying Forking Tokens for Diversity Enhancement
Use unsupervised clustering algorithms (e.g. DBSCAN, K-Means) to identify tokens within a chain of thought that have high likelihood of being forking tokens, based on their co-occurrence patterns and semantic meanings. Train a small auxiliary model to predict these tokens using side effects (e.g. jumpiness, sinkhorn distance, geometric derivatives).
Controls: Baseline: Randomly select tokens for forking. Ablation: Train without auxiliary model for prediction.
Estimated cost: 2,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: With proper parameter tuning, the proposed method will be able to identify around 20-30% of the forking tokens with 60-70% accuracy, and will improve diversity by 1.5 times compared to random sampling methods.

PROPOSAL 2: Diversity-Enhanced Fine-Tuning through Distillation
Fine-tune a language model on a set of diverse, correct reasoning traces per question using the Hindsight Distillation framework. This framework uses teacher models to generate hard attention masks that highlight the relevant information for each reasoning mode. Train the student model to mimic the attention patterns of the teachers, thereby encouraging the student to learn the distinct reasoning modes present in the training traces.
Controls: Baseline: Standard supervised fine-tuning without hardness-aware distillation. Ablation: No distillation.
Estimated cost: 10,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: With proper hyperparameters, the proposed method will retain around 80-90% of the distinct reasoning modes compared to collapse (-50% reduction), and improve accuracy on a set of diverse reasoning tasks by 2-3% compared to the baseline, measured by a new adapter-based evaluation protocol.

PROPOSAL 3: Triggering Distinct Reasoning Modes through Adversarial Evaluation
Develop an adversarial evaluation protocol that triggers the distinct reasoning modes in the fine-tuned model. Use a set of pre-defined trigger tokens to inject hints that systematically seek out the existence of hidden pathways in the model's reasoning process. Evaluate the model's ability to reason correctly while triggering specific reasoning modes, and compare its performance to the baselines.
Controls: Baseline: Standard fine-tuning without trigger tokens. Ablation: Remove triggers for specific modes.
Estimated cost: 8,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: This protocol will demonstrate a 5-7% increase in accuracy when triggering the distinct reasoning modes, with an average 3-4x increase in diversity compared to the baselines, indicating the robustness and dependability of the modes.

PROPOSAL 4: Self-Consistency Training for Reasoning Mode Retention
Modify the standard fine-tuning objective to incorporate a self-consistency regularization term. Train the model to generate a set of diverse, correct reasoning traces per question, and then have the model evaluate and correct its own outputs. This self-consistency term encourages the model to retain the distinct reasoning modes learned during fine-tuning.
Controls: Baseline: Standard fine-tuning without self-consistency regularization. Ablation: Remove self-consistency term.
Estimated cost: 5,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: This approach will improve the retention of distinct reasoning modes by 3-4% compared to the baseline, with an average 2-3% increase in accuracy on a set of diverse reasoning tasks, indicating the effectiveness of the self-consistency regularization.

PROPOSAL 5: Native Parallel Reasoning through Token-Invariant Contrastive Learning
Extend the teacher-student framework used in Diversity-Enhanced Fine-Tuning to train a model that naturally generates diverse, correct reasoning traces per question. Use token-invariant contrastive learning to encourage the model to focus on the essential information across different reasoning modes, rather than the specifics of each mode.
Controls: Baseline: Standard contrastive learning without token-invariance. Ablation: Remove token-invariance constraint.
Estimated cost: 15,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: This approach will improve the model's ability to generate diverse, correct reasoning traces per question by 4-6% compared to the baseline, with an average 5-7% increase in accuracy on a set of diverse reasoning tasks, indicating the effectiveness of native parallel reasoning.

Estimated cost: 4,000 GPU-hours
Prediction: This analysis will reveal that the ensemble approaches improve accuracy by 5-7% and diversity by 2-3 times compared to individual reasoning modes, indicating the effectiveness of aggregation methods in leveraging the strengths of multiple reasoning modes.
